1	# Notes
2	
3	This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
4	Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.
5	
6	By default there are chores-*.md and todo.md. Chores are general notes
7	about tasks and todo.md contains short term tasks and their status.
8	
9	App architecture — module map, the CLI-args / `Context`+`Params`
10	split, the subcommand model, and the in-flight migrations — lives
11	at the repo root in [`../ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md).
12	
13	In the future we I expect we may want to create a "notes"
14	database to better manage the information, TBD.
15	
16	Examples chore file:
17	```
18	# Chores-01.md
19	 
20	General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
21	more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
22	how and why of a particular chore.
23	
24	## Create a binary that lists jj info 
25	
26	This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
27	and using `jj-lib`
28	```
29	
30	## Workflow and conventions
31	
32	Bot-facing workflow, versioning, and code conventions live in
33	[`../CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md). Start there for:
34	
35	- **Versioning during development** — single-step vs multi-step,
36	  `-N` pre-release suffixes, done-marker discipline.
37	- **Code Conventions** — doc comments on every file / fn / method,
38	  `// OK: …` justifications on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
39	  stuck detection.
40	- **Commit-Push-Finalize Flow** — two-checkpoint per-step
41	  discipline with hard stop after finalize.
42	
43	## Todo format
44	
45	Todo.md contains two main sections "Todo" and "Done" each item is a
46	short explanations of a tasks and links to more details using 1 or more
47	references.
48	
49	Todo items use lazy numbering — every entry begins with `1. ` and the
50	markdown renderer auto-numbers them. Reorder or insert items without
51	renumbering, and reference an entry by its displayed number ("let's
52	work on #3"). The Done section keeps `-` bullets — items aren't
53	referenced by number once completed.
54	
55	Reference citations are **double-bracketed** — `[[1]]`, or
56	`[[2]],[[3]]` for several — so the brackets show when rendered
57	(a bare `[1]` renders as just `1`, which doesn't read as a
58	reference). Separate multiple with a comma: `[[2]],[[3]]`, not
59	`[2,3]` (a single ref key — won't resolve) or `[[2]][[3]]`. The
60	`[N]:` definition lines and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)`
61	links stay single-bracketed (their brackets already show in
62	source, and the link text reads as a link when rendered).
63	
64	Examples:
65	
66	# Todo
67	- Add new feature X [details](features.md#feature-x)
68	- Fix bug Y [[1]]
69	
70	# Done
71	- Fixed issue Z [[2]],[[3]]
72	
73	[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
74	[2]: issues.md#issue-z
75	[3]: fixes.md#fix-z
76	
77	## Reference numbering
78	
79	Every note file (`todo.md`, `chores-NN.md`, `done.md`) keeps a
80	file-local `# References` section at the bottom. Reference numbers
81	are scoped to that file — `[1]` in `chores-07.md` and `[1]` in
82	`chores-01.md` are independent slots that may point at completely
83	different URLs. New chores files start their numbering at `[1]`.
84	
85	Treat `[N]` like a **footnote**: the number is a local slot, only
86	meaningful within its file's `# References`. So a `[N]` *citation*
87	(bare `[N]`, or doubled `[[N]]` — see below) never reuses another
88	file's number; to cite a target a sibling file references, pick
89	your own next-local slot and define it (the same target may carry
90	a different number in each file). A `[N]` *inside a code span*
91	(`` `[72]` ``) is different — that's a quoted identifier: literal
92	text naming a ref-key (often from another file's namespace), data,
93	not a citation; it needs no definition here. To point at a section
94	of another file from prose, use an inline link with an anchor —
95	`[that section](../chores-07.md#…)` — not a bare number.
96	
97	A `chores-NN.md` `# References` entry is usually a
98	`/notes/<file>.md#anchor` (or `/ARCHITECTURE.md`) path, but may
99	also be a **commit reference** —
100	`[N]: <commit-url-with-12-hex-SHA> "<full-40-hex-SHA>"`, cited by
101	a section's `Commits:` line. See
102	[`../CLAUDE.md`](../CLAUDE.md#chores-commit-references) for the
103	why and the exact shape.
104	
105	A file's `# References` can be **re-packed** to a contiguous
106	`[1]..[N]` in first-citation-appearance order — walk the file's
107	prose in document order (`todo.md`: `## Todo` then `## Done`;
108	`chores-NN.md`: top to bottom) and number refs as their first
109	`[[N]]` citation appears. This is a file-local rewrite — only
110	that file's `[[N]]` citations and `[N]:` definitions move; every
111	target and sibling file is untouched. A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` ``
112	code span is a literal token, not a citation, and is left alone.
113	Do it opportunistically (when the namespace has drifted enough to
114	annoy), not on a schedule: `todo.md` fragments fastest (entries
115	land and get pruned every cycle) and is the usual candidate;
116	`chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are append-mostly and only need it
117	after an unusual event (e.g. a bulk retrofit that allocated slots
118	out of document order).
119	
120	## Retiring Done entries
121	
122	`todo.md`'s `## Done` section is a rolling buffer of recently shipped
123	work, not a permanent log. Move entries into `done.md` at two natural
124	beats:
125	
126	- **Closing a ladder** — when the final `X.Y.Z` (no suffix) commit
127	  ships, decide which prior entries are no longer needed for nearby
128	  context and migrate them.
129	- **Opening a new ladder** — at `X.Y.Z-0`, do the same sweep before
130	  bumping the version.
131	
132	Migration mechanics:
133	
134	- Move the bullet itself from `todo.md > ## Done` to
135	  `done.md` (preserving the original ref number).
136	- Copy any references the moved entries cite into
137	  `done.md`'s `# References` section (those refs are file-local,
138	  so coexisting with `todo.md`'s namespace is fine).
139	- Prune any references in `todo.md > # References` no longer cited
140	  by anything in `## In Progress` / `## Todo` / `## Done`. This
141	  frees the numbers for future reuse.
142	
```

1	# Architecture
2	
3	How the `vc-x1` binary is structured: the clap-aware CLI
4	layer and the (emerging) clap-free subcommand layer.
5	
6	This is a living document; the app is under continuous
7	development and the repo will keep changing. Per-cycle design
8	discussion lives in `notes/chores-*.md`; near-term tasks in
9	`notes/todo.md`.
10	
11	## Overview
12	
13	`vc-x1` is a single binary that supports subcommands,
14	`vc-x1 <subcommand>`, for managing a jj-git **dual-repo workspace**
15	with an app repo plus a `.claude` bot-session repo. The commits
16	cross-reference each other via `ochid:` trailers at the bottom
17	of each commit message. See [`README.md`](README.md)
18	for the user-facing picture and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
19	the bot workflow.
20	
21	## Two layers: CLI args vs subcommand Context + Params
22	
23	Goal: separate clap-aware argument parsing from subcommand
24	operation logic, so a future front-end (TUI, library
25	embedding) can call the same core without dragging clap
26	along. The trigger was `args.account.account`-style
27	nested-leaf access leaking into subcommand bodies; accessor
28	shortcuts were rejected as hiding the mismatch rather than
29	fixing it.
30	
31	- **CLI layer (clap-aware)**:
32	  Builds `XxxParams` from the user-facing `XxxArgs`
33	  `#[derive(Args)]` clap struct. Options/flags used in more
34	  than one subcommand live as flattened leaves in
35	  `src/options_flags/`.
36	- **Subcommand layer (clap-free)**:
37	  Entrypoint shape: `fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams) -> Result<…>`.
38	  And this isolates the subcommand from user and clap.
39	  - `Context` — common state shared with all subcommands.
40	  - `XxxParams` — a subcommand's parameters, derived from
41	    config or command-line arguments.
42	- **Boundary conversion**:
43	  Converting `XxxArgs` to `XxxParams` uses either
44	  `impl From<&XxxArgs> for XxxParams` or
45	  `impl TryFrom<&XxxArgs> for XxxParams`, depending on whether
46	  the conversion can fail.
47	
48	Two parameters per subcommand; the signature documents what
49	the subcommand depends on. `Context` is the same across all
50	subcommands; `XxxParams` carry the per-subcommand inputs.
51	
52	Rules for the subcommand layer (some still aspirational — see
53	[Migration A](#migration-a--args--context--params)):
54	
55	1. Plain options, flat fields, `Default` — no clap types in
56	   `XxxParams`. Domain types (`RepoSelector`, `Scope`) are
57	   fine; leaf wrappers (`RepoOption`) are not.
58	2. Typed errors (`enum XError`, not `Box<dyn Error>`) — a
59	   TUI matches variants to pick dialogs; CLI formats them.
60	3. Returned outcomes, not `println!` — each subcommand
61	   returns a structured result; CLI formats it, a library
62	   writes nothing to stdout itself.
63	4. Progress via an optional `&mut dyn ProgressSink` on
64	   long-running subcommands — CLI installs a stderr sink, tests a
65	   recording sink.
66	5. No globals, no implicit cwd/env reads in subcommands — CLI
67	   resolves cwd/env once at startup and builds `Context`.
68	
69	None of this is sacred — the whole structure is an experiment
70	and the repo keeps changing. The current scope is deliberately
71	narrow:
72	
73	- a small `Context` — two params, not one god blob;
74	- no trait-based DI yet;
75	- one crate, not a workspace split;
76	- `src/options_flags/` leaves left in place — only their
77	  consumers change shape.
78	
79	Widen any of it when the evidence (a second front-end, a second
80	consumer crate, a real platform-surface divergence) calls for
81	it — not before.
82	
83	### Naming
84	
85	Earlier drafts of this design (and the `notes/chores-09.md`
86	capture) used `Workspace` / `XOptions`. The implementation
87	(0.44.0) chose `Context` / `XxxParams` instead:
88	
89	- `Workspace` → `Context` — Cargo owns "workspace" formally,
90	  and this codebase already uses "workspace" for the
91	  dual-repo project root (`find_workspace_root`).
92	- `XOptions` → `XxxParams` — avoids visual collision with
93	  `Option<T>` (a params struct mixes required and
94	  `Option<T>`-typed fields) and with `src/options_flags/`.
95	
96	## Module map
97	
98	CLI layer:
99	
100	- `src/main.rs` — the clap edge:
101	  - `pub struct Cli` — clap `Parser`.
102	  - `pub enum Commands` — clap `Subcommand`; matched in the
103	    dispatch arms.
104	  - `cli_with_banner()` — walks the command tree adding the
105	    `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as `before_help` on every subcommand.
106	  - `CompleteEnv` wiring for dynamic completion.
107	  - `bm_track` — a permanent `main`-bookmark tracking
108	    diagnostic printed on entry/exit of every command.
109	
110	- `src/options_flags/` — options/flags shared across
111	  subcommands, so a flag is defined once (parser, help,
112	  completer); Migration B tracks what's been moved here so
113	  far. See
114	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md).
115	  - reusable **leaves**: `account`, `config`, `dry_run`,
116	    `private`, `push_retry`, `repo`, `scope`, `squash`,
117	    `use_template`.
118	  - reusable **bundles**: `provision_bundle`.
119	- `src/common.rs` — `CommonArgs` (the shared positional-rev /
120	  `-R` repo-list / `-n` / `--limit` / `-L` flag set flattened
121	  by `chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`) plus the repo-iteration
122	  and revision-resolution helpers they share.
123	
124	Subcommand layer scaffolding:
125	
126	- `src/context.rs` — `Context`: the shared platform handle
127	  every subcommand runs against. Today it carries the loaded
128	  `UserConfig` and the `--log` path; built once at startup
129	  via `Context::load(log)`.
130	- `src/config.rs` — `UserConfig` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`).
131	- `src/scope.rs` — `Scope` enum (`Roles(Vec<Side>)` for the
132	  dual-repo `code`/`bot` roles, `Single(PathBuf)` for
133	  single-repo mode) and `parse_scope`.
134	
135	Subcommand modules — each holds an `XxxArgs` `#[derive(Args)]`
136	struct and a `pub fn x(...)` entrypoint:
137	
138	| Module | Subcommand | Notes |
139	| --- | --- | --- |
140	| `chid.rs` | `chid` | flattens `CommonArgs` |
141	| `desc.rs` (+ `desc_helpers.rs`) | `desc` | flattens `CommonArgs` |
142	| `list.rs` | `list` | flattens `CommonArgs` |
143	| `show.rs` | `show` | flattens `CommonArgs` |
144	| `validate_desc.rs` | `validate-desc` | migrated (0.48.0-4) — `validate_desc(&Context, &ValidateDescParams)`, `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |
145	| `fix_desc.rs` | `fix-desc` | migrated (0.48.0-5) — `fix_desc(&Context, &FixDescParams)`, `From<&FixDescArgs>` |
146	| `clone.rs` | `clone` | migrated (0.48.0-2) — `clone_repo(&Context, &CloneParams)`, `From<&CloneArgs>` |
147	| `init.rs` (+ `init/params.rs`) | `init` | subcommand-layer worked example (0.44.0) |
148	| `symlink.rs` | `symlink` | migrated (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`, `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
149	| `sync.rs` | `sync` | migrated (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`, `From<&SyncArgs>` |
150	| `finalize.rs` | `finalize` | migrated (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`, `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` |
151	| `push.rs` | `push` | resumable state machine; migrated (0.48.0-6) — `push(&Context, &PushParams)`, `From<&PushArgs>` |
152	
153	Support:
154	
155	- `src/repo_utils.rs`, `src/url.rs`, `src/toml_simple.rs`,
156	  `src/logging.rs` — jj/repo helpers, URL parsing, a minimal
157	  TOML reader, the CLI logger.
158	- `src/test_helpers.rs`, `src/test_tmp_root.rs` —
159	  `#[cfg(test)]` fixtures (`Fixture` / `FixturePor`) and
160	  tempdir resolution. Subcommand modules also carry their
161	  own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (and `integration_tests` for
162	  `sync` / `push`).
163	
164	## Subcommand model
165	
166	Adding a subcommand `x`:
167	
168	1. Create `src/x.rs` with `pub struct XxxArgs`
169	   (`#[derive(Args)]`), composing leaves from
170	   `src/options_flags/` where one exists.
171	2. Add a variant `X(x::XxxArgs)` to `Commands` in
172	   `src/main.rs` with a `///` summary (and
173	   `#[command(long_about = …)]` for the long form).
174	3. Add a dispatch arm in `main()` calling `x::x(&args)` (or,
175	   once ported, `x::x(&ctx, &params)`).
176	4. Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help`; add
177	   `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, …)]` on any field whose doc
178	   comment uses bullets (clap otherwise reflows them into
179	   prose).
180	5. Dynamic value completion (`--account=<TAB>`) is an
181	   `ArgValueCompleter` attached to the leaf in
182	   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
183	   and stays at this layer.
184	
185	## Migration A — args → Context + Params
186	
187	Port each subcommand's `pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to
188	`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, adding an
189	`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the
190	conversion is fallible) at the binary edge. `init` (0.44.0) is
191	the worked example; `finalize` (0.46.0) added the `TryFrom` /
192	`Context.log` variant; the `0.48.0` cycle swept the rest of the
193	standalone subcommands. Only `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`
194	remain — their Migration A is bundled into the future
195	"CommonArgs sweep" (Migration A + B are entangled for the
196	`CommonArgs`-flattening subcommands). The live checklist is the
197	"Subcommand layer / CLI decoupling" item in
198	[`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md).
199	
200	| Subcommand | Status |
201	| --- | --- |
202	| `init` | done (0.44.0) — `init(&Context, &InitParams)`; `From<&InitArgs>` |
203	| `finalize` | done (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`; `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` (fallible boundary); `--log` moved onto `Context` |
204	| `symlink` | done (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`; `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
205	| `clone` | done (0.48.0-2) — `clone_repo(&Context, &CloneParams)`; `From<&CloneArgs>` |
206	| `sync` | done (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`; `From<&SyncArgs>` |
207	| `validate-desc` | done (0.48.0-4) — `validate_desc(&Context, &ValidateDescParams)`; `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |
208	| `fix-desc` | done (0.48.0-5) — `fix_desc(&Context, &FixDescParams)`; `From<&FixDescArgs>` |
209	| `push` | done (0.48.0-6) — `push(&Context, &PushParams)`; `From<&PushArgs>` (collapses the two bookmark spellings) |
210	| `chid` | deferred — rides the CommonArgs sweep (Migration A + B entangled) |
211	| `desc` | deferred — rides the CommonArgs sweep (Migration A + B entangled) |
212	| `list` | deferred — rides the CommonArgs sweep (Migration A + B entangled) |
213	| `show` | deferred — rides the CommonArgs sweep (Migration A + B entangled) |
214	
215	Out of scope for these ports (deferred until a real consumer
216	surfaces): typed errors, returned outcomes vs `println!`, the
217	`ProgressSink`, and `Context` fields beyond `UserConfig` + the
218	`--log` path (`finalize` surfaced `log`).
219	
220	## Migration B — per-subcommand flags → `src/options_flags/`
221	
222	Independently of Migration A, per-subcommand inline `#[arg]`
223	fields are being lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under
224	`src/options_flags/` so a flag is defined (parser, help,
225	completer) exactly once. See
226	[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
227	for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
228	Flag-vs-Option classification.
229	
230	State today:
231	
232	- **`init`** — fully composed from leaves/bundles
233	  (`account`, `repo`, `scope`, the `provision` bundle,
234	  `use_template`, `config`).
235	- **`chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`** — share
236	  `common::CommonArgs`, a per-domain shared struct rather
237	  than an `options_flags/` leaf. The "CommonArgs sweep"
238	  todo item folds these into the leaf model (and drops the
239	  repeatable `-R`/`--repo` in favor of the `--scope` path
240	  form).
241	- **`finalize`** — `--squash` lifted to the `squash` leaf
242	  (which carries the `value`-field naming convention — see
243	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
244	  "Adding a new leaf"). `--delay` / `--detach` / `--exec` /
245	  `--repo` / `--push` stay inline (no second consumer yet).
246	- **`sync` / `push` / `clone` / `validate-desc` /
247	  `fix-desc` / `symlink`** — still mostly inline `#[arg]`
248	  fields. The `--scope` retrofits queued in
249	  [`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md) are the usual entry
250	  point for converting one.
251

## docs: renumber todo.md + chores-09 refs (0.48.4)

Compact two files' `# References` to a contiguous `[1]..[N]` in
first-citation-appearance order — walk the file's prose in
document order (`todo.md`: `## Todo` items then `## Done` items;
`chores-09.md`: top to bottom) and assign `[1]`, `[2]`, … as
each ref's first `[[N]]` citation appears.

- **`todo.md`** — the 0.48.2/0.48.3 retrofits and routine entry
  churn left a sparse namespace (gaps from pruned entries,
  numbers into the 90s); the re-pack makes the next new ref
  `[N+1]`, not `[96]`.
- **`chores-09.md`** — the 0.48.2/0.48.3 bulk retrofit allocated
  slots in *conversion* order, not document order: `[1]` was the
  first section converted (the 0.48.1 section, near the bottom),
  `[2]..[22]` the historical sections top-to-bottom, `[24]` the
  chores-07 design ref (first cited near the top). The re-pack
  puts the numbers back in reading order — `[1]` is the topmost
  citation.

Properties of the renumber:

- **File-local.** Only the file's own `[[N]]` citations and
  `[N]:` definition lines move; every `[N]:` *target* and every
  other note file is untouched (ref numbers are file-local
  slots — `done.md` keeps its own numbering).
- **First-citation order, not definition order.** The number a
  reader meets first is `[1]`; following a citation walks *down*
  the `# References` list, never up.
- **Code spans are not citations.** A `[[N]]` inside a `` ` ``
  span (e.g. this section's `[[9]],[[13]],[[14]]` example) is a
  literal token, not a reference — the script masks fenced and
  inline code before scanning.
- **Cosmetic: multi-ref groups sorted ascending** — a cluster is
  written `[[9]],[[13]],[[14]]`, not in the order the refs
  happened to land.

### When to re-pack a file's references

- A renumber is a whole-file rewrite of citations + defs — do it
  opportunistically (when the namespace has drifted enough to
  annoy) rather than under a standing "keep it dense" rule that
  would force a rewrite on every prune.
- `todo.md` is the live churn surface (entries land and get
  pruned every cycle) so it fragments fastest and is the usual
  candidate. `chores-NN.md` / `done.md` are append-mostly; their
  numbering only drifts out of reading order after an unusual
  event like the 0.48.2/0.48.3 retrofit — which is exactly why
  `chores-09` got re-packed here and the other chores files
  don't need it.

A single Rust binary with subcommands for managing a **jj-git dual-repo workspace**: an app repo + a `.claude` bot-session repo, cross-linked by `ochid:` trailers. Subcommands: `init`, `clone`, `symlink`, `sync`, `chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`, `finalize`, `push`.

65	/// Result of parsing positional `..` notation.

69	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
70	pub struct DotSpec {
71	    /// The bare revision (without `..`).
72	    pub rev: String,
73	    /// Descendant count: `None` = open (dotted), `Some(0)` = closed.
74	    pub desc_count: Option<usize>,

79	/// Parse a positional REV string for `..` notation.
80	///
81	/// Returns the bare revision with open/closed counts per side.
82	/// `None` means the side had dots (open for expansion);
83	/// `Some(0)` means no dots on that side (closed).
84	/// Actual counts are applied later from positional args.
85	pub fn parse_dot_rev(rev: &str) -> DotSpec {
86	    if let Some(inner) = rev.strip_prefix("..").and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix("..")) {
87	        DotSpec {
88	            rev: inner.to_string(),
89	            desc_count: None,
90	            anc_count: None,
91	        }
92	    } else if let Some(inner) = rev.strip_prefix("..") {
93	        DotSpec {
94	            rev: inner.to_string(),
95	            desc_count: None,
96	            anc_count: Some(0),
97	        }
98	    } else if let Some(inner) = rev.strip_suffix("..") {
99	        DotSpec {
100	            rev: inner.to_string(),
101	            desc_count: Some(0),
102	            anc_count: None,
103	        }
104	    } else {
105	        DotSpec {
106	            rev: rev.to_string(),
107	            desc_count: Some(0),
108	            anc_count: Some(0),
109	        }
110	    }
111	}
112	
113	/// Resolve positional and flag args into a `DotSpec` ready for `collect_ids`.
114	///
115	/// Handles: dot notation parsing, flag vs positional precedence,
116	/// count-means-total semantics (subtracts 1 for anchor).
117	pub fn resolve_spec(
118	    pos_rev: Option<&str>,
119	    pos_count: Option<usize>,
120	    flag_rev: &str,
121	    flag_limit: Option<usize>,
122	    default_rev: &str,
123	) -> DotSpec {
124	    let flag_rev_set = flag_rev != default_rev;
125	    let rev_str = if flag_rev_set {
126	        flag_rev
127	    } else {
128	        pos_rev.unwrap_or(default_rev) // OK: positional absent → fall back to CLI default
129	    };
130	    let mut spec = parse_dot_rev(rev_str);
131	
132	    let count = if flag_limit.is_some() {
133	        flag_limit
134	    } else {
135	        pos_count
136	    };
137	
138	    if let Some(c) = count {
139	        let n = c.saturating_sub(1);
140	        let both_open = spec.desc_count.is_none() && spec.anc_count.is_none();
141	        if both_open {
142	            // Split budget across both sides: ancestors get the extra
143	            let desc_n = n / 2;
144	            let anc_n = n - desc_n;
145	            spec.desc_count = Some(desc_n);
146	            spec.anc_count = Some(anc_n);
147	        } else {
148	            if spec.desc_count.is_none() {
149	                spec.desc_count = Some(n);
150	            }
151	            if spec.anc_count.is_none() {
152	                spec.anc_count = Some(n);
153	            }
154	            // bare `x 5` → treat as `x.. 5` (ancestors)
155	            if spec.desc_count == Some(0) && spec.anc_count == Some(0) {
156	                spec.anc_count = Some(n);
157	            }
158	        }
159	    }
160	
161	    spec
162	}

164	/// Run a shell command. Returns stdout on success.
165	///
166	/// Logs the command at `debug!` and the process streams as follows:
167	/// - **stderr at `debug!`** on success — jj's chatter (`Moved 1 bookmarks
168	///   to …`, `Rebased N commits`, `Nothing changed.`) is hidden by default
169	///   and surfaced with `-v`. The debug formatter indents each line two
170	///   spaces so subprocess output sits visually under the caller's own
171	///   `info!` line in `-v` mode.
172	/// - **stdout at `debug!`** — callers usually consume stdout as data
173	///   (bookmark lists, commit IDs, etc.), and `info!` would flood the user
174	///   with machine-readable output they didn't ask for.
175	/// - **Failures propagate as `Err`** carrying the stderr; the caller's
176	///   error handler (`main::run_command`) surfaces it at `error!`.
177	pub fn run(cmd: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
178	    let args_str = args.join(" ");
179	    debug!("$ {cmd} {args_str}");
180	    trace!("cwd: {}", cwd.display());
181	    let output = std::process::Command::new(cmd)
182	        .args(args)
183	        .current_dir(cwd)
184	        .output()
185	        .map_err(|e| format!("failed to run {cmd}: {e}"))?;
186	    let stdout = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).trim().to_string();
187	    let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).trim().to_string();
188	    if !stdout.is_empty() {
189	        debug!("{stdout}");
190	    }
191	    if !output.status.success() {
192	        return Err(format!("{cmd} {args_str} failed: {stderr}").into());
193	    }
194	    if !stderr.is_empty() {
195	        debug!("{stderr}");
196	    }
197	    Ok(stdout)
198	}

241	/// Indent all lines after the first by `n` spaces.
242	///
243	/// Returns the string unchanged if `n == 0` or there is only one line.
244	pub fn indent_body(s: &str, n: usize) -> String {
245	    if n == 0 {
246	        return s.to_string();
247	    }
248	    let pad = " ".repeat(n);
249	    let mut lines = s.lines();
250	    let mut result = match lines.next() {
251	        Some(first) => first.to_string(),
252	        None => return String::new(),
253	    };
254	    for line in lines {
255	        result.push('\n');
256	        if !line.is_empty() {
257	            result.push_str(&pad);
258	        }
259	        result.push_str(line);
260	    }
261	    result
262	}

291	/// placeholder of that width is used. When `bookmarks` is non-empty it is

295	    let change_hex = encode_reverse_hex(commit.change_id().as_bytes());

303	    };
304	    if bookmarks.is_empty() {
305	        format!("{change_short}  {ochid:<width$}  {title}")
306	    } else {
307	        format!("{change_short}  {ochid:<width$}  {bookmarks} | {title}")

370	///
371	/// Returns `(commit_ids, anchor_index)` — the IDs in display order
372	/// (descendants closest to anchor, anchor, ancestors closest to anchor)
373	/// and the index of the anchor commit within the list.
374	///
375	/// - `desc_count`: `Some(n)` = n closest descendants, `None` = all, `Some(0)` = none
376	/// - `anc_count`: `Some(n)` = n closest ancestors, `None` = all, `Some(0)` = none
377	pub fn collect_ids(
378	    workspace: &Workspace,
379	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
380	    rev: &str,
381	    desc_count: Option<usize>,
382	    anc_count: Option<usize>,
383	) -> Result<(Vec<CommitId>, usize), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
384	    let anchor_ids = resolve_revset(workspace, repo, rev)?;
385	    if anchor_ids.is_empty() {
386	        return Err(format!("no commit found for revision '{rev}'").into());
387	    }
388	    let anchor_id = &anchor_ids[0];
389	    let root_commit_id = repo.store().root_commit_id().clone();
390	
391	    // Descendants (closest to anchor)
392	    let mut desc_ids: Vec<CommitId> = Vec::new();
393	    if desc_count != Some(0) {
394	        let descendant_ids = resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &format!("{rev}::"))?;
395	        desc_ids = descendant_ids
396	            .into_iter()
397	            .filter(|id| *id != root_commit_id && *id != *anchor_id)
398	            .collect();
399	        if let Some(n) = desc_count {
400	            let start = desc_ids.len().saturating_sub(n);
401	            desc_ids = desc_ids[start..].to_vec();
402	        }
403	    }
404	
405	    // Ancestors (closest to anchor)
406	    let mut anc_ids: Vec<CommitId> = Vec::new();
407	    if anc_count != Some(0) {
408	        let ancestor_ids = resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &format!("::{rev}"))?;
409	        let limit = anc_count.unwrap_or(usize::MAX); // OK: no --ancestors limit → unbounded
410	        let mut count = 0;
411	        for commit_id in ancestor_ids {
412	            if commit_id == root_commit_id || commit_id == *anchor_id {
413	                continue;
414	            }
415	            anc_ids.push(commit_id);
416	            count += 1;
417	            if count >= limit {
418	                break;
419	            }
420	        }
421	    }
422	
423	    let anchor_index = desc_ids.len();
424	    let mut result = desc_ids;
425	    result.push(anchor_id.clone());
426	    result.extend(anc_ids);
427	    Ok((result, anchor_index))
428	}

430	/// Header style between repos in multi-repo output.
431	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
432	pub enum Header {
433	    /// Show `deco path deco` header per repo.
434	    Label(String),
435	    /// No header at all.
436	    None,
437	}
438	
439	/// Resolve `-l` / `-L` flags into a `Header`.
440	///
441	/// `-L` (no header) takes precedence over `-l` (label decoration).
442	pub fn resolve_header(label: &str, suppress: bool) -> Header {
443	    if suppress {
444	        Header::None
445	    } else {
446	        Header::Label(label.to_string())
447	    }
448	}
449	
450	/// Expand comma-separated repo paths, default to `["."]`, and run a closure for each.
451	///
452	/// Header style controls output between repos.
453	/// Continues past errors, printing them to stderr, and returns an error if any failed.
454	pub fn for_each_repo<F>(
455	    raw_repos: &[PathBuf],
456	    header: &Header,
457	    mut body: F,
458	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
459	where
460	    F: FnMut(&Workspace, &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>,
461	{
462	    let repos: Vec<PathBuf> = if raw_repos.is_empty() {
463	        vec![PathBuf::from(".")]
464	    } else {
465	        raw_repos
466	            .iter()
467	            .flat_map(|p| {
468	                p.to_string_lossy()
469	                    .split(',')
470	                    .map(|s| PathBuf::from(s.trim()))
471	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
472	            })
473	            .collect()
474	    };
475	    let multi = repos.len() > 1;
476	    let mut first = true;
477	    let mut errors: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
478	
479	    for repo_path in &repos {
480	        if multi {
481	            match header {
482	                Header::Label(deco) => {
483	                    if !first {
484	                        info!("");
485	                    }
486	                    info!(
487	                        "{}",
488	                        bold(&format!("{deco} {} {deco}", repo_path.display()))
489	                    );
490	                }
491	                Header::None => {}
492	            }
493	        }
494	        first = false;
495	
496	        match load_repo(repo_path) {
497	            Ok((workspace, repo)) => {
498	                if let Err(e) = body(&workspace, &repo) {
499	                    error!("({}): {e}", repo_path.display());
500	                    errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
501	                }
502	            }
503	            Err(e) => {
504	                error!("({}): {e}", repo_path.display());
505	                errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
506	            }
507	        }
508	    }
509	
510	    if errors.is_empty() {
511	        Ok(())
512	    } else {
513	        Err(format!("{} repo(s) had errors", errors.len()).into())
514	    }
515	}
516	
517	pub fn load_repo(
518	    path: &Path,
519	) -> Result<(Workspace, Arc<ReadonlyRepo>), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
520	    let config = StackedConfig::with_defaults();
521	    let settings = UserSettings::from_config(config)?;
522	    let store_factories = StoreFactories::default();
523	    let working_copy_factories = default_working_copy_factories();
524	
525	    let workspace = Workspace::load(&settings, path, &store_factories, &working_copy_factories)?;
526	    let repo = workspace.repo_loader().load_at_head().block_on()?;
527	
528	    Ok((workspace, repo))
529	}

531	/// Parse and evaluate a revset string, returning commit IDs.
532	pub fn resolve_revset(
533	    workspace: &Workspace,
534	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
535	    revset_str: &str,
536	) -> Result<Vec<CommitId>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
537	    let aliases_map = RevsetAliasesMap::new();
538	    let fileset_aliases_map = FilesetAliasesMap::new();
539	    let extensions = RevsetExtensions::default();
540	    let workspace_root = workspace.workspace_root().to_path_buf();
541	    let path_converter = RepoPathUiConverter::Fs {
542	        cwd: workspace_root.clone(),
543	        base: workspace_root,
544	    };
545	    let workspace_name = workspace.workspace_name();
546	    let workspace_ctx = RevsetWorkspaceContext {
547	        path_converter: &path_converter,
548	        workspace_name,
549	    };
550	    let context = RevsetParseContext {
551	        aliases_map: &aliases_map,
552	        local_variables: HashMap::new(),
553	        user_email: "",
554	        date_pattern_context: chrono::Utc::now().fixed_offset().into(),
555	        default_ignored_remote: None,
556	        fileset_aliases_map: &fileset_aliases_map,
557	        use_glob_by_default: false,
558	        extensions: &extensions,
559	        workspace: Some(workspace_ctx),
560	    };
561	
562	    let mut diagnostics = RevsetDiagnostics::new();
563	    let expression = jj_lib::revset::parse(&mut diagnostics, revset_str, &context)?;
564	
565	    let no_extensions: &[Box<dyn jj_lib::revset::SymbolResolverExtension>] = &[];
566	    let symbol_resolver = SymbolResolver::new(repo.as_ref(), no_extensions);
567	    let resolved = expression.resolve_user_expression(repo.as_ref(), &symbol_resolver)?;
568	    let revset = resolved.evaluate(repo.as_ref())?;
569	
570	    let mut commit_ids = Vec::new();
571	    for result in revset.iter() {
572	        commit_ids.push(result?);
573	    }
574	    Ok(commit_ids)
575	}
576	
577	/// Scan `jj bookmark list -a <name>` output for non-tracking remote refs.
578	///
579	/// Tracked remotes appear indented (`  @origin: ...`); non-tracking remotes
580	/// appear at column 0 as `<bookmark>@<remote>: ...`. Returns the
581	/// non-tracking remote name if any is found.
582	pub fn find_non_tracking_remote(list_output: &str, bookmark: &str) -> Option<String> {
583	    let prefix = format!("{bookmark}@");
584	    for line in list_output.lines() {
585	        if line.starts_with(&prefix)
586	            && let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(&prefix)
587	            && let Some((remote, _)) = rest.split_once(':')
588	        {
589	            return Some(remote.to_string());
590	        }
591	    }
592	    None
593	}
594	
595	/// Verify all remote refs for `bookmark` in `repo` are tracked.
596	///
597	/// Returns `Err` with the exact `jj bookmark track …` remediation command if
598	/// any non-tracking remote ref is found. Used as a preflight by repo-modifying
599	/// commands (sync, push, finalize) and as a post-condition assertion by setup
600	/// commands (init, clone, test-fixture).
601	pub fn verify_tracking(repo: &Path, bookmark: &str) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
602	    let repo_str = repo.to_string_lossy();
603	    let cwd = Path::new(".");
604	    let all = run(
605	        "jj",
606	        &["bookmark", "list", "-a", bookmark, "-R", &repo_str],
607	        cwd,
608	    )?;
609	    if let Some(remote) = find_non_tracking_remote(&all, bookmark) {
610	        return Err(format!(
611	            "bookmark '{bookmark}' has non-tracking remote '{bookmark}@{remote}' — \
612	             run `jj bookmark track {bookmark} --remote={remote} -R {repo_str}` to fix"
613	        )
614	        .into());
615	    }
616	    Ok(())
617	}
618	
619	/// Walk up from `start` to find the workspace root.
620	///
621	/// The workspace root is the directory whose `.vc-config.toml` has
622	/// `path = "/"`. Returns `None` if no such config is found up to the
623	/// filesystem root — the caller is in a "plain old repo" (POR) with
624	/// no vc-x1 workspace metadata.
625	pub fn find_workspace_root_from(start: &Path) -> Option<PathBuf> {
626	    let mut cur = start.to_path_buf();
627	    loop {
628	        let cfg = cur.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE);
629	        if let Ok(map) = toml_simple::toml_load(&cfg)
630	            && toml_simple::toml_get(&map, "workspace.path").map(String::as_str) == Some("/")
631	        {
632	            return Some(cur);
633	        }
634	        cur = cur.parent()?.to_path_buf();
635	    }
636	}
637	
638	/// Cwd-anchored wrapper over [`find_workspace_root_from`].
639	pub fn find_workspace_root() -> Option<PathBuf> {
640	    let cur = std::env::current_dir().ok()?;
641	    find_workspace_root_from(&cur)
642	}
643	
644	/// Resolve the workspace's default `--scope`.
645	///
646	/// Reads `<workspace_root>/.vc-config.toml > [workspace] other-repo`:
647	///
648	/// - dual workspace (non-empty `other-repo`) → `Roles([Code, Bot])`
649	/// - single-repo workspace (missing / empty `other-repo`) → `Roles([Code])`
650	/// - POR (no workspace_root) → `Single(cwd)` — operate on cwd as a
651	///   one-off jj repo, ignoring any workspace context.
652	pub fn default_scope(workspace_root: Option<&Path>, cwd: &Path) -> Scope {
653	    let Some(root) = workspace_root else {
654	        return Scope::Single(cwd.to_path_buf());
655	    };
656	    let cfg = match toml_simple::toml_load(&root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE)) {
657	        Ok(c) => c,
658	        Err(_) => return Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code]),
659	    };
660	    match toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg, "workspace.other-repo") {
661	        Some(v) if !v.is_empty() => Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]),
662	        _ => Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code]),
663	    }
664	}
665	
666	/// Resolve a `Scope` to concrete repo paths.
667	///
668	/// `Roles(...)` arm:
669	///
670	/// - `Side::Code` → `workspace_root` (or cwd's `.` when `workspace_root` is None).
671	/// - `Side::Bot` → `workspace_root.join(other-repo)`.
672	///
673	/// Errors when `Side::Bot` is requested but the workspace doesn't define
674	/// one (POR or single-repo workspace).
675	///
676	/// `Single(p)` arm: returns `vec![p]` directly — no workspace lookup,
677	/// no `other-repo` resolution. The path is whatever the caller stored
678	/// (typically the value the user passed to `--scope=<path>`, or cwd
679	/// from `default_scope`'s POR branch); shell-style expansion (tilde,
680	/// `$VAR`) happens at the parser/consumer boundary, not here.
681	pub fn scope_to_repos(
682	    scope: &Scope,
683	    workspace_root: Option<&Path>,
684	) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
685	    let sides = match scope {
686	        Scope::Roles(v) => v,
687	        Scope::Single(p) => return Ok(vec![p.clone()]),
688	    };
689	    let mut repos = Vec::new();
690	    for side in sides {
691	        match side {
692	            Side::Code => repos.push(
693	                workspace_root
694	                    .map(Path::to_path_buf)
695	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")),
696	            ),
697	            Side::Bot => {
698	                let root = workspace_root.ok_or(
699	                    "--scope=bot: not in a vc-x1 workspace (no .vc-config.toml with path = \"/\") — drop --scope or use --scope=code",
700	                )?;
701	                let cfg = toml_simple::toml_load(&root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE))?;
702	                let other = toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg, "workspace.other-repo")
703	                    .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
704	                    .ok_or(
705	                        "--scope=bot: no other-repo configured. Add `other-repo = \"…\"` to .vc-config.toml to enable dual-repo operations",
706	                    )?;
707	                repos.push(root.join(other));
708	            }
709	        }
710	    }
711	    Ok(repos)
712	}

1	use std::sync::Arc;
2	
3	use chrono::Offset;
4	use clap::Args;
5	use jj_lib::backend::TreeValue;
6	use jj_lib::commit::Commit;

8	use jj_lib::merged_tree::TreeDiffIterator;
9	use jj_lib::object_id::ObjectId;
10	use jj_lib::repo::{ReadonlyRepo, Repo};

12	use pollster::FutureExt;

14	use log::{debug, info};

16	use crate::common;

18	/// Parsed file limit: None (suppress), Some(n) (cap at n), or all.
19	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
20	pub enum FileLimit {
21	    /// Don't show changed files section at all.
22	    None,
23	    /// Show up to N files (with first/last split if truncated).
24	    Cap(usize),
25	    /// Show all files.
26	    All,
27	}
28	
29	impl FileLimit {
30	    fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
31	        match s {
32	            "0" => Ok(FileLimit::None),
33	            "all" => Ok(FileLimit::All),
34	            _ => s
35	                .parse::<usize>()
36	                .map(FileLimit::Cap)
37	                .map_err(|_| format!("invalid file limit '{s}': expected number, 0, or 'all'")),
38	        }
39	    }
40	}
41	
42	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
43	pub struct ShowArgs {
44	    #[command(flatten)]
45	    pub common: common::CommonArgs,
46	
47	    /// Max changed files: number, 0 (none), or 'all'
48	    #[arg(short = 'f', long = "files", default_value = "50")]
49	    pub files: String,
50	}
51	
52	pub fn show(args: &ShowArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
53	    debug!("show: enter");
54	    let file_limit = FileLimit::parse(&args.files)?;
55	    let c = &args.common;
56	
57	    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, "@");
58	    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);
59	
60	    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {
61	        let (ids, anchor_index) =
62	            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;
63	
64	        let mut first = true;
65	        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {
66	            if !first {
67	                info!("────────────────────────────────────────");
68	            }
69	            first = false;
70	
71	            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;
72	            show_one_commit(&commit, workspace, repo, file_limit, i == anchor_index)?;
73	        }
74	        Ok(())
75	    })?;
76	    debug!("show: exit");
77	    Ok(())
78	}
79	
80	fn show_one_commit(
81	    commit: &Commit,
82	    workspace: &Workspace,
83	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
84	    file_limit: FileLimit,
85	    is_primary: bool,
86	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
87	    // Author
88	    let author = commit.author();
89	    info!(
90	        "Author:    {} <{}> ({})",
91	        author.name,
92	        author.email,
93	        format_timestamp(&author.timestamp)
94	    );
95	
96	    // Committer
97	    let committer = commit.committer();
98	    info!(
99	        "Committer: {} <{}> ({})",
100	        committer.name,
101	        committer.email,
102	        format_timestamp(&committer.timestamp)
103	    );
104	
105	    // Ids
106	    let bookmarks = common::format_bookmarks_at(repo, commit.id());
107	    let ids_line = common::format_commit_short(commit, &bookmarks);
108	    if is_primary {
109	        info!("Ids:       {}", common::bold(&ids_line));
110	    } else {
111	        info!("Ids:       {ids_line}");
112	    }
113	
114	    // Parents
115	    let root_commit_id = repo.store().root_commit_id().clone();
116	    for parent_id in commit.parent_ids() {
117	        if *parent_id == root_commit_id {
118	            continue;
119	        }
120	        let parent = repo.store().get_commit(parent_id)?;
121	        let bm = common::format_bookmarks_at(repo, parent.id());
122	        info!("Parent:    {}", common::format_commit_short(&parent, &bm));
123	    }
124	
125	    // Children
126	    let children_ids =
127	        common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &format!("children({})", commit.id().hex()))?;
128	    for child_id in &children_ids {
129	        if *child_id == root_commit_id {
130	            continue;
131	        }
132	        let child = repo.store().get_commit(child_id)?;
133	        let bm = common::format_bookmarks_at(repo, child.id());
134	        info!("Child:     {}", common::format_commit_short(&child, &bm));
135	    }
136	
137	    // Branches
138	    let branches_str = format_branches(commit, workspace, repo)?;
139	    info!("Branches:  {branches_str}");
140	
141	    // Follows
142	    let follows = find_nearest_tag(commit, workspace, repo, true)?;
143	    info!("Follows:   {}", follows.as_deref().unwrap_or("")); // OK: obvious
144	
145	    // Precedes
146	    let precedes = find_nearest_tag(commit, workspace, repo, false)?;
147	    info!("Precedes:  {}", precedes.as_deref().unwrap_or("")); // OK: obvious
148	
149	    // Description (body only — title is on the Ids line)
150	    print_description(commit);
151	
152	    // Changed files
153	    if file_limit != FileLimit::None {
154	        print_diff(commit, repo, file_limit)?;
155	    }
156	
157	    Ok(())
158	}
159	
160	fn find_nearest_tag(
161	    commit: &Commit,
162	    workspace: &Workspace,
163	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
164	    ancestor: bool,
165	) -> Result<Option<String>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
166	    let commit_hex = commit.id().hex();
167	
168	    let revset_str = if ancestor {
169	        format!("heads(tags() & ::{})", commit_hex)
170	    } else {
171	        format!("roots(tags() & {}::)", commit_hex)
172	    };
173	
174	    let tag_ids = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
175	    if tag_ids.is_empty() {
176	        return Ok(None);
177	    }
178	
179	    let tag_id = &tag_ids[0];
180	    let view = repo.view();
181	    for (name, local_remote) in view.tags() {
182	        if local_remote.local_target.added_ids().any(|id| id == tag_id) {
183	            return Ok(Some(name.as_str().to_string()));
184	        }
185	    }
186	
187	    Ok(None)
188	}
189	
190	fn format_branches(
191	    commit: &Commit,
192	    workspace: &Workspace,
193	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
194	) -> Result<String, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
195	    let commit_hex = commit.id().hex();
196	    let view = repo.view();
197	    let mut names: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
198	
199	    for (name, local_remote) in view.bookmarks() {
200	        for bookmark_id in local_remote.local_target.added_ids() {
201	            let revset_str = format!("{} & ::{}", commit_hex, bookmark_id.hex());
202	            let results = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
203	            if !results.is_empty() {
204	                names.push(name.as_str().to_string());
205	                break;
206	            }
207	        }
208	
209	        for (remote_name, remote_ref) in &local_remote.remote_refs {
210	            if remote_name.as_str() == "git" {
211	                continue;
212	            }
213	            for bookmark_id in remote_ref.target.added_ids() {
214	                let revset_str = format!("{} & ::{}", commit_hex, bookmark_id.hex());
215	                let results = common::resolve_revset(workspace, repo, &revset_str)?;
216	                if !results.is_empty() {
217	                    names.push(format!("{}@{}", name.as_str(), remote_name.as_str()));
218	                    break;
219	                }
220	            }
221	        }
222	    }
223	
224	    Ok(names.join(", "))
225	}
226	
227	fn format_timestamp(ts: &jj_lib::backend::Timestamp) -> String {
228	    let millis = ts.timestamp.0;
229	    let secs = millis / 1000;
230	    let tz_minutes = ts.tz_offset;
231	
232	    let dt = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(secs, 0)
233	        .unwrap_or_default() // OK: invalid timestamp → epoch for display
234	        .with_timezone(
235	            &chrono::FixedOffset::east_opt(tz_minutes * 60).unwrap_or(chrono::Utc.fix()), // OK: invalid tz → UTC for display
236	        );
237	
238	    dt.format("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S").to_string()
239	}
240	
241	fn print_description(commit: &Commit) {
242	    let desc = commit.description();
243	    let body: String = desc
244	        .lines()
245	        .skip(1)
246	        .skip_while(|l| l.is_empty())
247	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
248	        .join("\n");
249	
250	    info!("Description:");
251	    for line in body.lines() {
252	        info!("    {line}");
253	    }
254	}
255	
256	fn print_diff(
257	    commit: &Commit,
258	    repo: &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>,
259	    file_limit: FileLimit,
260	) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
261	    let parent_tree = commit.parent_tree(repo.as_ref()).block_on()?;
262	    let commit_tree = commit.tree();
263	
264	    let diff_iter = TreeDiffIterator::new(&parent_tree, &commit_tree, &EverythingMatcher);
265	
266	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
267	    for entry in diff_iter {
268	        let diff = entry.values?;
269	        let before = diff.before.as_resolved().cloned().flatten();
270	        let after = diff.after.as_resolved().cloned().flatten();
271	
272	        if matches!(&before, Some(TreeValue::Tree(_))) || matches!(&after, Some(TreeValue::Tree(_)))
273	        {
274	            continue;
275	        }
276	
277	        let path_str = entry.path.as_internal_file_string().to_string();
278	
279	        let line = match (before, after) {
280	            (None, Some(value)) => {
281	                format!("    Added {} {path_str}", file_type_str(&value))
282	            }
283	            (Some(_), None) => {
284	                format!(
285	                    "    Removed {} {path_str}",
286	                    file_type_str_from_merged(&diff.before),
287	                )
288	            }
289	            (Some(_), Some(value)) => {
290	                format!("    Modified {} {path_str}", file_type_str(&value))
291	            }
292	            (None, None) => continue,
293	        };
294	        lines.push(line);
295	    }
296	
297	    let total = lines.len();
298	    let cap = match file_limit {
299	        FileLimit::All | FileLimit::None => 0,
300	        FileLimit::Cap(n) => n,
301	    };
302	    let show_all = cap == 0 || total <= cap;
303	
304	    if show_all {
305	        info!("Changed files: {total}");
306	        for line in &lines {
307	            info!("{line}");
308	        }
309	    } else {
310	        info!("Changed files: {total}, showing first {cap}");
311	        for line in &lines[..cap] {
312	            info!("{line}");
313	        }
314	    }
315	
316	    Ok(())
317	}
318	
319	fn file_type_str(value: &TreeValue) -> &'static str {
320	    match value {
321	        TreeValue::File {
322	            executable: false, ..
323	        } => "regular file",
324	        TreeValue::File {
325	            executable: true, ..
326	        } => "executable file",
327	        TreeValue::Symlink(_) => "symlink",
328	        TreeValue::Tree(_) => "tree",
329	        TreeValue::GitSubmodule(_) => "git submodule",
330	    }
331	}
332	
333	fn file_type_str_from_merged(merged: &jj_lib::merge::Merge<Option<TreeValue>>) -> &'static str {
334	    if let Some(Some(value)) = merged.as_resolved() {
335	        file_type_str(value)
336	    } else {
337	        "file"
338	    }
339	}

1	//! Flat plain-struct input to the init op.
2	//!
3	//! `InitParams` is the clap-free shape that `pub fn init` reads
4	//! from. Built `From<&InitArgs>` at the binary edge (main.rs);
5	//! callers without clap (tests, future TUI / library embedding)
6	//! construct it directly.
7	//!
8	//! Per `notes/chores-09.md > ## InitParams implementation
9	//! (0.44.0)`: domain types pass through (`RepoSelector`,
10	//! `ScopeKind`, `ConfigKind`, `PushRetryOptions`); leaf clap
11	//! wrappers do not.
12	
13	use crate::config::RepoSelector;
14	use crate::init::InitArgs;
15	use crate::options_flags::config::ConfigKind;
16	use crate::options_flags::push_retry::PushRetryOptions;
17	use crate::options_flags::scope::ScopeKind;
18	
19	/// Inputs to the init op, flat, owned, clap-free.
20	///
21	/// - `target`: the TARGET positional argument (URL, owner/name,
22	///   path, or bare NAME).
23	/// - `name`: optional `NAME` positional override.
24	/// - `account`: `--account` value (None ⇒ default account chain).
25	/// - `repo`: `--repo` value parsed into a `RepoSelector`.
26	/// - `scope`: `--scope` resolved (default `code,bot`).
27	/// - `private`: `--private`.
28	/// - `dry_run`: `--dry-run`.
29	/// - `push_retry`: `--push-retries` / `--push-retry-delay`.
30	/// - `use_template`: `--use-template` value.
31	/// - `config`: resolved `--config` value (None ⇒ canned write).
32	/// - `create_symlink`: whether `init` should create the
33	///   `~/.claude/projects/` symlink for dual-scope runs (production
34	///   path = true; test fixtures suppress with false).
35	pub struct InitParams {
36	    pub target: String,
37	    pub name: Option<String>,
38	    pub account: Option<String>,
39	    pub repo: Option<RepoSelector>,
40	    pub scope: ScopeKind,
41	    pub private: bool,
42	    pub dry_run: bool,
43	    pub push_retry: PushRetryOptions,
44	    pub use_template: Option<String>,
45	    pub config: Option<ConfigKind>,
46	    pub create_symlink: bool,
47	}
48	
49	impl From<&InitArgs> for InitParams {
50	    /// Convert clap-derived `InitArgs` into the flat `InitParams`.
51	    ///
52	    /// Production path: sets `create_symlink: true`. Tests that
53	    /// need `create_symlink: false` construct `InitParams`
54	    /// directly (or post-edit the field).
55	    fn from(a: &InitArgs) -> Self {
56	        Self {
57	            target: a.target.clone(),
58	            name: a.name.clone(),
59	            account: a.account.account.clone(),
60	            repo: a.repo.repo.clone(),
61	            scope: a.scope.scope,
62	            private: a.provision.private.private,
63	            dry_run: a.provision.dry_run.dry_run,
64	            push_retry: a.provision.push_retry.clone(),
65	            use_template: a.use_template.use_template.clone(),
66	            config: a.config.resolve(ConfigKind::None),
67	            create_symlink: true,
68	        }
69	    }
70	}

> AGENT

Here's the picture for finishing Migration A on `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`.

## What's involved

All four flatten `common::CommonArgs`. Each subcommand body immediately turns that into a `DotSpec` (`resolve_spec`) + a `Header` (`resolve_header`) and then iterates `for_each_repo`. `list` adds `--width`, `show` adds `--files` (which it *parses* into a `FileLimit`).

Proposed shape:

- **`src/common.rs`** — add a clap-free `CommonParams { spec: DotSpec, header: Header, repos: Vec<PathBuf> }` plus `impl From<&CommonArgs> for CommonParams` (does the `resolve_spec` + `resolve_header` work at the binary edge). This is the shared piece all four reuse.
- **`chid` / `desc`** — add thin `ChidParams { common: CommonParams }` / `DescParams { common: CommonParams }` + `From<&XxxArgs>`; port `chid(&Context, &ChidParams)` / `desc(&Context, &DescParams)` (`_ctx` unused, matching `validate-desc` / `fix-desc` / `symlink`).
- **`list`** — `ListParams { common: CommonParams, width: usize }` + `From`; port `list(&Context, &ListParams)`.
- **`show`** — `ShowParams { common: CommonParams, files: FileLimit }` + **`TryFrom<&ShowArgs>`** (fallible — `FileLimit::parse` moves to the boundary, mirroring `finalize`'s `TryFrom`); port `show(&Context, &ShowParams)`.
- **`src/main.rs`** — four dispatch arms gain the `Context::load` + `XxxParams::from`/`try_from` pattern (the `suppress_banner` match keeps reading `a.common.no_label` off the args — unchanged).
- **Docs** — `ARCHITECTURE.md` Migration A table → all 12 done; flip the "only chid/desc/list/show remain" intro; `notes/todo.md` item #1 → `## Done`; `notes/chores-09.md` new section. Migration B section stays (the CommonArgs→leaf + `--scope` sweep is still pending for these four).

The existing `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` parse tests are untouched (they test `XxxArgs` parsing). I'll add a small "construct `XxxParams` directly" test per the worked-example precedent.

## Versioning — recommend multi-step

Mirrors the 0.48.0 sweep (which did 6 subcommands as `-1`..`-6`). Ladder:

- `0.49.0-0` — open cycle (Cargo bump, todo.md ladder, chores-09 open section); also backfill the `Commits:` ref on the `0.48.4` chores section.
- `0.49.0-1` — `chid` + introduce `CommonParams` in `common.rs`.
- `0.49.0-2` — `desc`.
- `0.49.0-3` — `list`.
- `0.49.0-4` — `show` (the `TryFrom` one).
- `0.49.0` — close-out: todo→Done, ARCHITECTURE.md, chores header sync. Squash-vs-keep-separate decided at close-out.

## docs: chores edit list → commit message (0.48.2)

Commits: [[24]]

Move the per-file edit list out of `chores-NN.md` sections
into the commit message body — git becomes the source of
truth for what each commit changed mechanically. A chores
section now keeps only the narrative + `###` design
subsections, cites its commit(s) via a `Commits:` ref, and —
when it records a commit, as does a `todo.md > ## Done` entry —
takes its header verbatim from that commit's title
(organizational headings and design subsections don't).
CLAUDE.md and `notes/README.md` codify it; the `0.48.1`
section here and its `todo.md > ## Done` entry are converted
as the worked example, this section is born in the new shape
(its own `Commits:` ref backfilled at the next cycle's start).

### Why git owns the edit record

- **DRY.** The old setup had the commit body mirror a chores
  `### Edits` list — the same content twice, which drifts.
  Git's copy is immutable, `git show`-able, commit-scoped; it
  wins as canonical. Chores keeps what git is bad at — the
  why.
- **`Commits:` ref shape.** Markdown reference-link
  definitions put the destination first, so to keep the
  `[[N]]` citation clickable the `[N]:` definition's
  destination is the URL (`…/commit/<12-hex>` — short, and
  GitHub / GitLab resolve a unique prefix), and the full
  40-hex SHA rides in the title slot: host-agnostic,
  unambiguous, and present in the raw markdown for external
  tooling (a database, say) to scrape.
- **Backfill timing.** A commit's URL/SHA don't exist when
  its section is written, so `Commits:` is filled in at the
  *next* cycle's start — the newest section is briefly
  ref-less, which is fine (the commit itself is the record).
- **Doubled citations.** Reference *citations* are written
  `[[N]]` (not `[N]`) so the brackets render — `[27]` reads
  as a reference, `27` doesn't. `[N]:` definitions and inline
  links stay single-bracketed. `todo.md` is fully retrofitted;
  `chores-01..08` grandfathered (chores-09 retrofitted in
  0.48.3).

## docs: chores-09 → new shape (0.48.3)

Retroactively convert every commit-recording section in

foreign-namespace citation attempt) → a `chores-09`-local ref
to the chores-07 `--scope` design section. Lines 38–40's
renumbering description left code-spanned (literal historical
tokens, no stable current target). `notes/README.md` codifies
the footnote framing — ref numbers are file-local slots; a
`[N]` in a code span is a quoted identifier (data), not a
citation; cross-file pointing uses an inline link.

### Why retrofit one file

- **Surfaced by adding `# References`.** 0.48.2 gave
  `chores-09` a `# References` section; a reader then expects
  it to define the page's `[N]` mentions — but most were

  both; either the page runs the convention fully or it

- **Bounded.** One file, 21 historical commit-recording

  similar vestigials but no `# References` forcing the issue —
  they stay grandfathered (the convention sunsets their
  `### Edits` lists by attrition, not retrofit).

> DEVELOPER

Does CommonParams need to be done bfore updating chid, desc ...?

> AGENT

Yes — `CommonParams` is the type the four `XxxParams` embed, so it has to exist before any of them can be ported. In the plan it's not a *separate* step, though: `0.49.0-1` introduces `CommonParams` (+

> DEVELOPER

Why wasn't it necessary for the other commands we've already converted to the XxxArgs -> XxxParams model?

> AGENT

Because those commands don't share a multi-field args struct the way these four do.

- **init / finalize / symlink / clone / sync / validate-desc / fix-desc / push** each have their *own* `XxxArgs`, built from inline `#[arg]` fields plus small `options_flags/` **leaves** (`RepoOption`, `AccountOption`, `SquashOption`, …). A leaf is a one- or two-field wrapper. When porting, the `XxxParams` just unwraps each leaf to its inner value at the boundary — `a.account.account.clone()`, `a.repo.repo.clone()`, `a.config.resolve(...)`. There's no shared *struct* on the params side because the shared unit (the leaf) is tiny and gets flattened away, not carried.

- **chid / desc / list / show** are the exception: all four `#[command(flatten)]` the *same* `common::CommonArgs` — a 7-field struct (`pos_rev`, `pos_count`, `revision`, `repos`, `limit`, `label`, `no_label`), and ARCHITECTURE.md explicitly calls it "a per-domain shared struct rather than an `options_flags/` leaf." Their bodies all run the same `resolve_spec` + `resolve_header` over it. So the clap-free counterpart of that shared struct — `CommonParams` — is itself the shared thing each `XxxParams` embeds. It's the params-layer mirror of `CommonArgs`; nothing analogous existed for the earlier ports.

So it's not that `CommonParams` is a new kind of requirement — it's that this is the first port where the *args* side had a shared struct big enough to be worth mirroring rather than unwrapping.

  "new_string": "    /// Suppress label between repos\n    #[arg(short = 'L', long = \"no-label\")]\n    pub no_label: bool,\n}\n\n/// Clap-free counterpart of [`CommonArgs`], built at the binary edge.\n///\n/// The read-only subcommands (chid, desc, list, show) all resolve\n/// their flattened `CommonArgs` into a [`DotSpec`] + [`Header`] before\n/// iterating repos; `CommonParams` carries that resolved shape so the\n/// op bodies never touch the clap struct.\n///\n/// - `spec`: bare revision plus per-side (descendant / ancestor)\n///   counts, from [`resolve_spec`] over the positional / `-r` / `-n`\n///   args (default rev `@`).\n/// - `header`: how to decorate output between repos in multi-repo runs\n///   (`-l` / `-L`), from [`resolve_header`].\n/// - `repos`: the raw `-R` / `--repo` paths; comma-expansion and the\n///   `.` default happen in [`for_each_repo`].\n#[derive(Debug, Clone)]\npub struct CommonParams {\n    pub spec: DotSpec,\n    pub header: Header,\n    pub repos: Vec<PathBuf>,\n}\n\nimpl From<&CommonArgs> for CommonParams {\n    /// Resolve clap-derived [`CommonArgs`] into the flat `CommonParams`\n    /// — runs [`resolve_spec`] (default rev `@`) and [`resolve_header`].\n    fn from(a: &CommonArgs) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            spec: resolve_spec(a.pos_rev.as_deref(), a.pos_count, &a.revision, a.limit, \"@\"),\n            header: resolve_header(&a.label, a.no_label),\n            repos: a.repos.clone(),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of parsing positional `..` notation."
}

```
1	# options_flags — Reusable CLI Options and Flags
2	
3	Per-flag CLI surfaces shared across multiple subcommands. Each
4	shared option or flag (OF) lives in its own submodule so its
5	type, parser, and tests stay together.
6	
7	This module is the CLI-layer leaf store for "Migration B" in
8	[`../../ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../ARCHITECTURE.md); see there for
9	how the leaves fit the wider clap-args / `Context`+`Params`
10	split.
11	
12	## Architecture
13	
14	Three composition patterns:
15	
16	- **Leaf** — a `#[derive(Args)]` struct holding the flag(s),
17	  `value_parser`, default, and help text (via the field
18	  doc-comment). One `#[derive(Args)]` per logical OF — single
19	  flag or a small fixed pair (e.g. `push_retry`'s two fields).
20	  Help text aims to be generic enough for any reasonable
21	  consumer.
22	- **Bundle** — a `#[derive(Args)]` that flattens N leaves into a
23	  named role (e.g. `ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`). One
24	  `#[command(flatten)]` line at the consumer picks up the whole
25	  bundle.
26	- **Pattern A escape hatch** — when a consumer needs unique help
27	  text (or different defaults), it skips the leaf's flatten and
28	  inlines its own `#[arg(value_parser = …)]` field, reusing the
29	  leaf's typed value and parser.
30	
31	## Flag vs Option — classify by domain, not wire syntax
32	
33	Every leaf falls into one of two categories, picked by the value
34	domain it carries:
35	
36	- **Flag** — boolean domain. Wire form may be presence/absence
37	  (`--dry-run`), explicit negation (`--no-dry-run`), or value
38	  (`--dry-run=true|false`). All three express a `bool`. Type
39	  name suffix: `*Flag`.
40	- **Option** — non-boolean domain (string, integer, enum, path,
41	  …). Wire form is always `--name=<value>` (or `--name <value>`).
42	  Type name suffix: `*Option` (or `*Options` for a multi-field
43	  leaf like `PushRetryOptions`).
44	
45	Wire form is presentation; the category is the underlying domain.
46	
47	## Adding a new leaf
48	
49	1. Create `options_flags/<name>.rs` with a
50	   `#[derive(Args, Debug, Clone, Default)]` struct.
51	2. Pick the suffix per domain: `*Flag` (boolean) or `*Option(s)`
52	   (non-boolean).
53	3. Name the field(s):
54	   - **Single-field leaf** — call the field `value` (it holds the
55	     parsed value-side of the option) and declare the flag
56	     explicitly with `#[arg(long = "<flag>", …)]`. The consumer
57	     then reads `args.<leaf>.value` rather than doubling the flag
58	     name (`args.squash.value`, not `args.squash.squash`).
59	   - **Multi-field leaf** — descriptive per-field names
60	     (`push_retries`, `push_retry_delay`); clap derives each
61	     flag from its field name as usual.
62	   - The pre-existing single-field leaves (`scope`, `repo`,
63	     `dry_run`, `private`, `account`, `config`, `use_template`)
64	     predate this and still derive the flag from the field name;
65	     migrating them to `value` is tracked in
66	     [`../../notes/todo.md`](../../notes/todo.md).
67	4. Add `pub mod <name>;` to `mod.rs`.
68	5. If the leaf has explicit parsing logic, declare a unit-struct
69	   implementor of `FlagParser` (boolean domain) or `OptionParser`
70	   (non-boolean domain). Bare `Option<String>` leaves and
71	   presence/absence boolean leaves need no parser impl — clap
72	   handles them.
73	6. Add tests for any non-trivial parser/resolver logic.
74	7. Leaves do **not** implement a Bundle marker — bundles do.
75	
76	## Consuming an OF
77	
78	Default — flatten the leaf into your subcommand's `Args`:
79	
80	```rust
81	#[derive(Args)]
82	pub struct MyArgs {
83	    #[command(flatten)]
84	    pub config: ConfigOption,
85	    // ...
86	}
87	```
88	
89	Pattern A — when generic help doesn't fit:
90	
91	```rust
92	#[derive(Args)]
93	pub struct MyArgs {
94	    /// My subcommand-specific help for --config.
95	    #[arg(long = "config", value_name = "none|PATH",
96	          verbatim_doc_comment)]
97	    pub config: Option<String>,
98	    // ...
99	}
100	```
101	
102	A Pattern A consumer reuses the leaf's types (e.g. `ConfigKind`)
103	and parsers (e.g. `parse_config_kind`) but owns its own clap
104	attributes.
105	
106	## Consumer function shape
107	
108	Helper functions called by a subcommand body should accept the
109	relevant leaf type by reference rather than unpacking individual
110	fields at the call site:
111	
112	```rust
113	// Multi-field leaf — pass the whole leaf
114	fn run_retry(cmd: &str, args: &[&str], cwd: &Path,
115	             retry: &PushRetryOptions) -> Result<…> { … }
116	
117	run_retry("git", &["push", …], cwd, &args.provision.push_retry)?;
118	```
119	
120	This wins on:
121	- Readability — `&args.provision.push_retry` reads as a single
122	  unit; the function body works with `retry.push_retries` (no
123	  leaf-name doubling because the parameter name is the consumer's
124	  choice).
125	- Argument count — every multi-field leaf collapses N args into
126	  one ref, so chained helpers don't accumulate
127	  `clippy::too_many_arguments` warnings.
128	- Future-proofing — extending a leaf with another field is a
129	  zero-touch change at every call site.
130	
131	For **single-field leaves** (e.g. `SquashOption`, `DryRunFlag`,
132	`PrivateFlag`), direct read at the consumer site
133	(`args.squash.value`, or `args.provision.dry_run.dry_run` for the
134	pre-`value` leaves) is fine — wrapping the inner value in a
135	`&LeafType` parameter doesn't earn the indirection.
136	
137	## Marker traits
138	
139	Three Bundle markers — one per content classification. Bundles
140	implement exactly one. Leaves do **not** implement these markers
141	(their category lives in the type-name suffix).
142	
143	- `FlagBundle: clap::Args` — pure-boolean bundle (every
144	  constituent leaf is a Flag). Rare in practice.
145	- `OptionBundle: clap::Args` — pure-non-boolean bundle (every
146	  constituent leaf is an Option).
147	- `OptionFlagBundle: clap::Args` — mixed bundle (constituents
148	  include both Flag and Option leaves). Most common in practice.
149	
150	Two Parser traits — conditional contracts implemented only when
151	a leaf has explicit parsing logic (custom `value_parser`):
152	
153	- `FlagParser` — boolean-domain parser. Implemented only for
154	  boolean leaves that take a value form (`--flag=true|false`).
155	  Presence/absence flags need no impl; clap parses directly.
156	- `OptionParser` — non-boolean-domain parser. Implemented only
157	  for leaves with custom parsing logic (e.g. `ScopeParser`,
158	  `RepoParser`); bare `Option<String>` leaves need no impl.
159	
160	`FlagParser` and `OptionParser` share an identical method shape;
161	the difference is documentation (which value-domain the parser
162	targets).
163	
164	All five traits are documentation-level — clap derive doesn't
165	see them; the discipline is that every leaf and bundle declares
166	the appropriate ones explicitly.
167	
168	## Bundle marker discipline
169	
170	Bundle markers aren't compiler-checked against contents. If a
171	bundle's leaf set shifts category — e.g. a pure-Flag bundle gains
172	an Option leaf — you must update the marker by hand
173	(`FlagBundle` → `OptionFlagBundle`). No lint, no failure; silent
174	drift if forgotten. Worth a glance at the marker line whenever a
175	bundle's `#[command(flatten)]` set changes.
176	
177	## Pattern A worked example
178	
179	`init`'s `--config` field originally carried init-specific help
180	("Only valid with `--scope=por`..."). It currently flattens
181	`ConfigOption` for the generic help; the `--scope=por` constraint
182	surfaces in `init`'s preflight error. If the help-text generality
183	becomes a usability problem, init will switch to Pattern A as the
184	worked example.
185	
186	## Layout note
187	
188	OFs currently sit as flat `<name>.rs` files alongside this
189	README. Bundle modules carry the `_bundle` suffix
190	(e.g. `provision_bundle.rs`) so the leaf/bundle split is visible
191	in the directory listing without opening files. If an individual
192	OF accumulates enough rationale, edge-case detail, or examples
193	to outgrow doc-comments, it will graduate to a `<name>/mod.rs` +
194	`<name>/README.md` subdirectory layout. Mechanical when needed;
195	not done preemptively.
196	
```

> AGENT

You're right that conceptually it belongs there — it's a shared, multi-subcommand arg struct, same role as `ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`. Two wrinkles on *how cleanly* it fits today:

1. **It's a fat single struct, not a leaf-bundle.** `options_flags/` is built around *leaves* (one flag or a small fixed pair) composed into *bundles* (`#[command(flatten)]` of N leaves). `CommonArgs` has 7 inline `#[arg]` fields (`pos_rev`, `pos_count`, `-r`, `-R`, `-n`, `-l`, `-L`). To put it there *properly* you'd decompose it into leaves first — which is exactly the "CommonArgs sweep" todo, and that one also swaps the `-R`/`--repo` leaf for the `--scope` path form. So "do it right" = a separate, bigger cycle (Migration B + a `--scope` rollout), not a drop-in.
2. **A file-move-as-is is possible** — `CommonArgs` lands in `src/options_flags/common_args.rs` (or `common_bundle.rs`) undecomposed, marked as a bundle "pending leaf decomposition." Low risk, but it parks a non-leaf/non-bundle thing in the leaf store that the sweep then has to take apart anyway.

`CommonParams` (the clap-free side I just added) stays in `common.rs` regardless — it bundles the resolved `DotSpec` / `Header` / repos that `common.rs`'s `for_each_repo` / `collect_ids` consume; that's its natural home.

1	//! Which side(s) of a workspace a command should operate on.
2	//!
3	//! - `Side` is the clap `ValueEnum` — one of `code`, `bot`.
4	//! - `Scope` is an enum:
5	//!   - `Roles(Vec<Side>)` — dual-repo workspace; the parsed
6	//!     keyword form (`code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`).
7	//!   - `Single(PathBuf)` — explicit single-repo mode; ignores
8	//!     `.vc-config.toml` and operates on the one repo at the
9	//!     given path. Wired up incrementally (parser lands in
10	//!     0.42.0-2, consumers in later steps).
11	//! - Helpers (`has_code`, `is_both`, etc.) reflect the `Roles`
12	//!   arm only; on `Single(_)` they all return `false`. Callers
13	//!   that must distinguish modes match on the enum directly.
14	//! - See `notes/chores-07.md > --scope enum refactor (0.42.0)`
15	//!   for the migration plan, and `notes/chores-06.md > 0.41.0-4`
16	//!   for the vocabulary capture.
17	
18	use clap::ValueEnum;
19	use std::fmt;
20	use std::path::PathBuf;
21	
22	/// One side of a dual-repo workspace.
23	///
24	/// - `Code` — the primary (app) repo.
25	/// - `Bot` — the Claude Code session repo (typically at `.claude/`).
26	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
27	pub enum Side {
28	    Code,
29	    Bot,
30	}
31	
32	/// Parsed `--scope` value.
33	///
34	/// - `Roles(_)` — dual-repo workspace; the requested side set.
35	/// - `Single(_)` — explicit single-repo mode at the given path.
36	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
37	pub enum Scope {
38	    Roles(Vec<Side>),
39	    #[allow(dead_code)]
40	    Single(PathBuf),
41	}
42	
43	/// Parse a `--scope` value string.
44	///
45	/// Accepted forms:
46	///
47	/// - Keyword: exactly one of `code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`
48	///   → `Scope::Roles(...)`. Order is preserved.
49	/// - Path: starts with `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or is the bare `~`
50	///   → `Scope::Single(PathBuf)`. The raw string is stored; tilde
51	///   and `$VAR` expansion happens at the consumer (see
52	///   `init::expand_vars`).
53	///
54	/// Anything else — including a bare unprefixed name like `foo`, an
55	/// empty string, or an unrecognized keyword combination — is an
56	/// error. The error message hints at the path-prefix requirement
57	/// so users see the disambiguation rule when they mistype.
58	#[allow(dead_code)]
59	pub fn parse_scope(s: &str) -> Result<Scope, String> {
60	    if s == "~"
61	        || s.starts_with("./")
62	        || s.starts_with("../")
63	        || s.starts_with('/')
64	        || s.starts_with("~/")
65	    {
66	        return Ok(Scope::Single(PathBuf::from(s)));
67	    }
68	    match s {
69	        "code" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code])),
70	        "bot" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Bot])),
71	        "code,bot" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot])),
72	        "bot,code" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Bot, Side::Code])),
73	        "" => Err("--scope: value is empty".into()),
74	        other => Err(format!(
75	            "--scope: '{other}' is not a recognized form. \
76	             Expected one of `code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`, \
77	             or a path (`./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`). \
78	             Bare names without `./` are reserved for keywords; \
79	             prefix paths with `./` to disambiguate."
80	        )),
81	    }
82	}
83	
84	impl Scope {
85	    /// True when the `Roles` arm includes the code side.
86	    pub fn has_code(&self) -> bool {
87	        matches!(self, Scope::Roles(v) if v.contains(&Side::Code))
88	    }
89	
90	    /// True when the `Roles` arm includes the bot side.
91	    pub fn has_bot(&self) -> bool {
92	        matches!(self, Scope::Roles(v) if v.contains(&Side::Bot))
93	    }
94	
95	    /// Roles-only with exactly the code side — single-side dual-repo op.
96	    pub fn is_code_only(&self) -> bool {
97	        self.has_code() && !self.has_bot()
98	    }
99	
100	    /// Roles-only with exactly the bot side — single-side dual-repo op.
101	    #[allow(dead_code)]
102	    pub fn is_bot_only(&self) -> bool {
103	        !self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
104	    }
105	
106	    /// Roles arm including both sides — full dual-repo op.
107	    pub fn is_both(&self) -> bool {
108	        self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
109	    }
110	}
111	
112	/// Render a `Scope` as the canonical string form `parse_scope` accepts.
113	///
114	/// - `Roles(_)` → `code` / `bot` / `code,bot` / `bot,code` (preserves
115	///   original side ordering).
116	/// - `Single(p)` → the path's lossy display form. The stored path
117	///   already carries a parser-recognized prefix (the parser is the
118	///   only constructor of `Single`), so the round-trip through
119	///   `parse_scope` is well-defined.
120	impl fmt::Display for Scope {
121	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
122	        match self {
123	            Scope::Roles(sides) => {
124	                let parts: Vec<&'static str> = sides
125	                    .iter()
126	                    .map(|s| match s {
127	                        Side::Code => "code",
128	                        Side::Bot => "bot",
129	                    })
130	                    .collect();
131	                f.write_str(&parts.join(","))
132	            }
133	            Scope::Single(p) => write!(f, "{}", p.display()),
134	        }
135	    }
136	}
137
