1	//! `--scope` — code,bot|por target set selector.
2	//! See [options_flags](README.md) for shared architecture.
3	
4	use clap::Args;
5	
6	/// Typed value of `--scope` — the kinds of repo set a
7	/// subcommand can target.
8	///
9	/// - `CodeBot` (default) — dual-repo: code + `.claude` bot
10	///   session.
11	/// - `Por` — single repo (Plain Old Repo); no `.claude/`,
12	///   no `.vc-config.toml`.
13	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
14	pub enum ScopeKind {
15	    #[default]
16	    CodeBot,
17	    Por,
18	}
19	
20	/// Parse the `--scope` value into a `ScopeKind`.
21	///
22	/// - Accepts `code,bot` / `bot,code` (commutative) and `por`.
23	/// - Standalone `code` or `bot` errors — these are
24	///   config-lookup keywords; subcommands using `ScopeKind`
25	///   have no config-driven sides to look up against.
26	pub fn parse_scope_kind(s: &str) -> Result<ScopeKind, String> {
27	    match s {
28	        "code,bot" | "bot,code" => Ok(ScopeKind::CodeBot),
29	        "por" => Ok(ScopeKind::Por),
30	        "code" | "bot" => Err(format!(
31	            "'--scope={s}' is not a valid scope kind — use 'code,bot' (dual) or 'por' (single)"
32	        )),
33	        _ => Err(format!(
34	            "'--scope={s}' is not recognized — expected 'code,bot' or 'por'"
35	        )),
36	    }
37	}
38	
39	/// `OptionParser` impl for `--scope` (non-boolean domain).
40	/// Documentation-level — consumers can use either
41	/// `parse_scope_kind` directly or `ScopeParser::parse`.
42	pub struct ScopeParser;
43	
44	impl super::OptionParser for ScopeParser {
45	    type Value = ScopeKind;
46	
47	    fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, String> {
48	        parse_scope_kind(s)
49	    }
50	}

## Generalize --scope to all commands (design)

Surfaced 2026-04-23 (from the user, top of todo): vc-x1 commands
should support both single and dual repo modes. The technique
sketched for `vc-x1 push` (`--scope=app|claude|both`) is the
right shape, but the scope concept should be a project-wide
convention rather than push-only.

**Naming:** `--scope=app|other|both` — "other" rather than
"claude" because the second repo isn't always `.claude`; could
be a different bot or a different sibling project structure.

**Why scope-first** (before adding more commands or push
features): each new command that operates across both repos
would otherwise need its own ad-hoc handling. Locking in the
convention now means new commands inherit it for free, and
existing commands (sync, finalize, push) get retrofitted under
the same vocabulary.

**Rough scope of the change:**

- Shared CLI flag definition + parsing helper (likely in
  `common.rs`).
- `sync`: already accepts `-R` for single-repo. Migrate to
  `--scope`; alias or deprecate `-R` (TBD below).
- `push`: `--scope` per the existing design, with
  warn-on-WC-mismatch.
- `finalize`: already takes `--repo`; rationalize naming.
- New commands (`status` etc.) start with `--scope` from day 1.

**Open:** do we deprecate `-R` immediately, alias it, or keep
both indefinitely? Probably: alias for one minor cycle,
deprecate, remove. Decide before implementation.


============ chores-06 1305-1500 ============
### 0.41.0-3: capture --scope-everywhere direction

Notes-only step. Records the directional decisions that
came out of the 0.41.0-2 close-out conversation
(2026-04-26) so the rest of the cycle and the post-0.41.0
follow-ups don't relitigate them.

**Consistency principle (decided).** Every subcommand that
operates on one or both repos gets `--scope=code|bot|code,
bot`. No vocabulary forks across commands; `--scope` is the
project-wide convention. Existing per-command flags
(`-R/--repo`, `--repo`) stay as back-compat aliases where
they already exist; new commands inherit `--scope` from day
one.

**Per-command rollout map.**

- `init` — done (0.40.0). `--scope=code|bot|code,bot`.
- `sync` — done (0.41.0-2). `--scope` + `-R` (mutually
  exclusive); `-R` retained for arbitrary multi-repo.
- `push` — 0.41.0-4. State machine becomes scope-aware;
  single-side path skips `commit-claude` /
  `finalize-claude` and bookmarks one repo only.
- `finalize` — 0.41.0-5. `--scope` is canonical; existing
  `--repo` becomes a back-compat alias (overrides scope
  when present, prints a soft deprecation note, slated
  for removal in a future cycle). Does *not* downgrade to
  the "review-only / no-op" outcome the original 0.41.0-4
  sketch hedged toward.
- `clone` — post-0.41.0. Parallel to `init --scope`;
  single-repo clone for `vc-template-x1`-shape remotes.
- `validate-desc` / `fix-desc` — post-0.41.0. Same
  vocabulary as everywhere else, no rename to `--side`.
  Semantic: `--scope=code` validates code's commits
  against bot, `--scope=bot` reverses the direction,
  `--scope=code,bot` does both (the new default).
- `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` — post-0.41.0. Add
  `--scope` via `CommonArgs` so all four inherit it
  in one cycle. Existing `-R` / `--repo` stays alongside.
- `symlink` — N/A. Bot-only by definition; scope doesn't
  apply.

**Deferred design questions** (caught in todo, not blocking
the rollout):

- `[workspace]` section name in `.vc-config.toml` reads as
  a Cargo workspace to Rust users but isn't one. Rename
  candidates: `[repo-list]` / `[project]` / `[dual-repo]`.
  Breaking change; needs migration.
- Help layout uniformity — clap auto-picks two-column vs
  over-under per command based on widest flag spec.
  `sync -h` is two-column, `init -h` is over-under. Force
  uniform via `next_line_help(true)` at the root.

### 0.41.0-4: capture --scope enum vocabulary

Notes-only step. Mid-implementation rethink — the
original `-4` (push --scope on top of `Vec<Side>`)
exposed a vocabulary gap that the user surfaced
2026-04-26: `code` plays two distinct roles depending on
context (a *role* in a dual workspace; an implicit
*fallback to cwd* in POR). Conflating them muddies what
"obvious to the user" looks like. Splitting them honestly
is a type-model change, not a per-command implementation
detail — so the cycle pivots: capture the refined
vocabulary here, defer all command implementations to
0.42.0, and close 0.41.0 cleanly.

**Settled vocabulary.**

- `--scope` (short form `-s`) accepts:
  - `code` — the app side of a dual-repo workspace.
  - `bot` — the bot side of a dual-repo workspace.
  - `code,bot` / `bot,code` — both (commutative; same
    semantic, same default).
  - `<path>` — single-repo mode; ignore `.vc-config.toml`,
    operate on the given path. Path values must be
    prefixed (`./`, `/`, `~/`) to disambiguate from the
    keyword set. Tilde expansion mirrors init's existing
    behavior on `--repo-local` / `--repo-remote`.
- No discoverable `single` keyword. `--scope=.` is the
  cwd form; `--scope=/abs/path` or `--scope=./rel` is the
  explicit form. Bare names that aren't keywords error
  with a "did you mean `./foo`?" hint.

**Internal type model.**

```rust
pub enum Scope {
    Roles(Vec<Side>), // code | bot | code,bot
    Single(PathBuf),  // explicit path, single-repo mode
}
```

Replaces today's `Scope(pub Vec<Side>)`. The current
`has_code` / `has_bot` / `is_code_only` etc. helpers all
shift to operate on `Roles` only — `Single(_)` is a
distinct mode, not a one-element role list.

**Default-scope rules (revised).**

| Workspace state | `.vc-config.toml` shape | Default scope |
|---|---|---|
| Dual workspace | `path` + non-empty `other-repo` | `Roles([Code, Bot])` |
| Single-repo workspace | `path`, no `other-repo` | `Roles([Code])` |
| POR | (no file) | `Single(cwd)` |

The single-repo-workspace concept stays — it's a real,
distinct state with a non-trivial default (`Roles([Code])`
not `Single(...)`). `--scope=bot` errors there with
"no other-repo configured."

**Per-command applicability matrix.**

| Command | `Roles` accepted | `Single(_)` accepted |
|---|---|---|
| `init` | yes | no — init creates workspaces, not POR repos |
| `sync` | yes | yes |
| `push` | yes | yes |
| `finalize` | yes (currently has `--repo`; migrates to `--scope`) | yes |
| `clone` | yes | yes (single-repo clone target) |
| `validate-desc` | yes | **error** — validate compares two repos by definition; `Single` is meaningless |
| `fix-desc` | yes | **error** (same reason as validate-desc) |
| `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` | yes | yes |
| `symlink` | n/a | n/a |

`Single` is *always* available as the explicit
"ignore-the-config" escape hatch on commands where it
applies, even inside a dual workspace — the user
explicitly bypasses the dispatcher. On commands where it
can't apply (validate-desc / fix-desc), errors with a
specific message rather than silently doing the wrong
thing.

**Flag-surface changes.**

- Drop `-R` / `--repo` everywhere. Currently sync has it
  (mutually exclusive with `--scope`); finalize has its
  own `--repo` (single repo). Both fold into the new
  `--scope=<path>` form.
- `--scope` gets short form `-s` for ergonomics.
- The path form covers what `-R` / `--repo` did before.
  Multi-repo (sync's old `-R . -R .claude` style) is
  deliberately not preserved — that capability had no
  real users beyond manually emulating today's default.

**Rationale for the cycle pivot.**

- The 0.41.0-3 capture committed to "consistency
  everywhere", which means push, finalize, and the
  remaining commands all need to agree on the type
  model. Implementing push on the soon-to-be-changed
  type would be churn.
- The enum refactor touches scope.rs, common.rs,
  init, sync, plus push and finalize at the same time.
  That's a 0.42.0-sized cycle, not a sub-step inside
  0.41.0.
- Closing 0.41.0 here produces a clean checkpoint: the
  scope foundation (0.40.0 init) and one consumer
  (0.41.0-2 sync) are shipped, the direction is captured
  in 0.41.0-3 and 0.41.0-4. 0.42.0 opens with the type
  refactor as its `-0` plan.

Edits:

- `Cargo.toml`: bump to `0.41.0-4` (notes-only step).
- `src/push.rs`: revert the partial scope work that was
  in flight (`--scope` flag on `PushArgs`, scope-related
  imports). Push stays unchanged on main; its
  scope wiring lands in 0.42.0 against the new type.
- `notes/chores-06.md`: cycle-step sketch updated (0.41.0-3
  marked shipped; 0.41.0-4 redefined as the enum
  capture; 0.41.0-5 dropped from the cycle); this
  subsection added; legacy default-scope rules marked
  superseded.
- `notes/todo.md`: dev-ladder updated (0.41.0-3 → done;
  0.41.0-4 current; 0.41.0-5 removed; 0.41.0 close-out
  noted).

### 0.41.0: cycle close-out
```

> AGENT

Reading the prior design history, "the full sweep" is the long-planned **"CommonArgs sweep"** — it's well-specified in `chores-06.md` ("Generalize --scope across commands", the 0.41.0-3/-4 captures) and `chores-07.md` ("--scope enum refactor (0.42.0)"). Three things bundled:

1. **Migration A** — `XxxParams` + `fn x(&Context, &XxxParams)` ports for chid/desc/list/show.
2. **Migration B** — decompose `CommonArgs`'s fields into `options_flags/` leaves; the bundle relocates to `src/options_flags/`.
3. **`--scope` rollout** — replace `-R`/`--repo` with `-s`/`--scope` (`code|bot|code,bot|<path>`), wiring up `scope.rs`'s `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single` (currently `#[allow(dead_code)]` — they exist *waiting for exactly this*) plus `common.rs`'s `default_scope` / `scope_to_repos` (already there).

Things that follow from the captured design (so you know what you're approving):

- **`-R`/`--repo` goes away.** The 0.42.0 capture deliberately drops it everywhere — the `--scope=<path>` form covers single-repo; arbitrary multi-repo (`-R . -R .claude`) is *not* preserved ("had no real users beyond emulating today's default"). So `chid -R .claude` becomes `chid -s ./.claude`, and the default behavior is `default_scope()` (dual workspace → both repos).
- **All four `From` become `TryFrom`** — scope→repo resolution is fallible (`--scope=bot` in a POR errors).
- **`for_each_repo` simplifies** — takes an already-resolved `Vec<PathBuf>`; the comma-expansion + `["."]` default move to the boundary.
- **`init`'s `--scope` is left alone** — it uses the separate `ScopeKind` (`code,bot|por`); reconciling the two `--scope` vocabularies is the separate "por/dual parity" todo, not this cycle.

Proposed ladder (keeps the chid work already staged):

- `0.49.0-1` chid + `CommonParams` — **staged**; I'll just rewrite its ARCHITECTURE.md/todo framing to the expanded plan (and add the missing `Cargo.toml` bump). Still ports against `-R` for now.
- `0.49.0-2` desc · `0.49.0-3` list · `0.49.0-4` show — Migration A ports.
- `0.49.0-5` decompose `CommonArgs` → `options_flags/` leaves + relocate to `src/options_flags/common_bundle.rs`. Pure refactor.
- `0.49.0-6` `-R`/`--repo` → `-s`/`--scope`: wire `parse_scope`/`default_scope`/`scope_to_repos`, flip the four `From`→`TryFrom`, slim `for_each_repo`, update tests + `README.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md`, mark the "CommonArgs sweep" todo done + Migration A 12/12. (May split into `-6.N` sub-steps.)
- `0.49.0` close-out.

Two things to confirm:

1. **Order** — A-first (above; keeps the staged chid work, costs 4 trivial `From`→`TryFrom` edits in `-6`), or scope+B-first (cleaner dependency order, but means discarding the staged `0.49.0-1` and restarting)? I lean A-first.
2. **`0.49.0-0`** — it's pushed with the title "finish Migration A", now too narrow. Leave it and record the expanded scope in `0.49.0-1`'s chores section (history shows the plan evolved), or amend it via `--ignore-immutable`+force-push? I lean leave-it.

OK to proceed on A-first + leave-`0.49.0-0`?

> DEVELOPER

Hmm, why not decompose CommonArgs first (i.e. Migration B first)?

> AGENT

Good call — B-first *is* cleaner, for a concrete reason: Migration A's shape (the `From` vs `TryFrom` boundary, what `CommonParams` carries) depends on what `CommonArgs` ends up looking like. If A goes first against today's fat `CommonArgs` (with `-R`), then `-5` decomposes it (the `From<&CommonArgs> for CommonParams` internals change to read `.value`) and `-6` swaps `-R`→`--scope` (the four `From`s flip to `TryFrom`, and `CommonParams.repos` changes source) — so every A-port gets re-touched twice. B-and-scope first means the A-ports are written *once*, against the final shape. The only thing A-first buys is keeping the chid code I already staged — but that's ~30 lines, cheap to re-apply later.

Revised ladder (B-first):

//! `ProvisionOptionFlagBundle` — bundle of OFs shared by every
//! provisioning subcommand (today `init`; later `clone` once it
//! migrates). Composes `DryRunFlag`, `PrivateFlag` (Flag leaves)
//! and `PushRetryOptions` (Option leaf), so a consumer picks them
//! all up with one `#[command(flatten)]` line. Mixed-domain →
//! implements `OptionFlagBundle`. See [options_flags](README.md) for
//! shared architecture.

use clap::Args;

use super::dry_run::DryRunFlag;
use super::private::PrivateFlag;
use super::push_retry::PushRetryOptions;

/// Provisioning bundle — see [Bundle](README.md#architecture).
///
/// - `dry_run` — `--dry-run` (Flag).
/// - `private` — `--private` (Flag).
/// - `push_retry` — `--push-retries` + `--push-retry-delay`
///   (Option).
#[derive(Args, Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct ProvisionOptionFlagBundle {
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub dry_run: DryRunFlag,

    #[command(flatten)]
    pub private: PrivateFlag,

    #[command(flatten)]
    pub push_retry: PushRetryOptions,
}

impl super::OptionFlagBundle for ProvisionOptionFlagBundle {}

=== squash.rs ===
//! `--squash SOURCE,TARGET` — pick the `jj squash --from/--into`
//! revision pair (e.g. `@,@-`). See [options_flags](README.md) for
//! shared architecture.

use clap::Args;

/// Parsed `--squash` value: the source and target revisions.
///
/// - Produced by [`SquashSpec::parse`] (also wired as the leaf's
///   `value_parser`, so clap rejects malformed input at parse time).
/// - Both halves are guaranteed non-empty.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SquashSpec {
    pub source: String,
    pub target: String,
}

impl SquashSpec {
    /// Parse a `SOURCE,TARGET` pair (e.g. `@,@-`); both halves
    /// must be non-empty.
    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let parts: Vec<&str> = s.split(',').collect();
        if parts.len() != 2 || parts[0].is_empty() || parts[1].is_empty() {
            return Err(format!(
                "invalid --squash value '{s}': expected SOURCE,TARGET (e.g. @,@-)"
            ));
        }
        Ok(SquashSpec {
            source: parts[0].to_string(),
            target: parts[1].to_string(),
        })
    }
}

/// `OptionParser` impl for `--squash` (non-boolean domain).
/// Documentation-level — consumers can use either
/// `SquashSpec::parse` directly or `SquashSpecParser::parse`.
pub struct SquashSpecParser;

impl super::OptionParser for SquashSpecParser {
    type Value = SquashSpec;

    fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self::Value, String> {
        SquashSpec::parse(s)
    }
}

/// `--squash` leaf (Option — non-boolean domain) — see
/// [Consuming an OF](README.md#consuming-an-of).
///
/// - The single field is named `value` (the parsed value-side of
///   the option); the flag name comes from `#[arg(long = "squash")]`,
///   so the consumer reads `args.<leaf>.value` rather than doubling
///   the flag name.
/// - Bare `--squash` (no value) defaults to `@,@-`.
/// - `num_args = 0..=1` so the value form `--squash @,@-` also
///   works without quoting.
#[derive(Args, Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct SquashOption {
    /// Squash SOURCE into TARGET [default: @,@-]
    #[arg(
        long = "squash",
        value_name = "SOURCE,TARGET",
        value_parser = SquashSpec::parse,
        default_missing_value = "@,@-",
        num_args = 0..=1
    )]
    pub value: Option<SquashSpec>,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn squash_parse_valid() {
        let sq = SquashSpec::parse("@,@-").unwrap();
        assert_eq!(sq.source, "@");
        assert_eq!(sq.target, "@-");
    }

    #[test]
    fn squash_parse_invalid() {
        assert!(SquashSpec::parse("@").is_err());
        assert!(SquashSpec::parse(",").is_err());
        assert!(SquashSpec::parse("@,").is_err());
        assert!(SquashSpec::parse(",@-").is_err());
    }
}

ListArgs {\n    #[command(flatten)]\n    pub common: CommonOptionFlagBundle,\n\n    /// ochid column width\n    #[arg(short = 'w', long = \"width\", default_value_t = DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH)]\n    pub width: usize,\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH: usize = 21;\n\n/// List commits in the resolved range with the ochid column.\npub fn list(args: &ListArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    debug!(\"list: enter\");\n    let c = &args.common;\n    let spec = common::resolve_spec(\n        c.pos_rev.as_deref(),\n        c.pos_count,\n        &c.revision.value,\n        c.limit.value,\n        \"@\",\n    );\n    trace!(\n        \"list: spec rev={} desc={:?} anc={:?}\",\n        spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count\n    );\n    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.repo_label.label, c.repo_label.no_label);\n\n    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {\n        let (ids, anchor_index) =\n            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;\n        debug!(\"list: {} commits, anchor at {anchor_index}\", ids.len());\n\n        if ids.is_empty() {\n            warn!(\"list: no commits found for revision '{}'\", spec.rev);\n        }\n\n        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {\n            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;\n assert!(args.common.limit.value.is_none());\n        assert_eq!(args.width, super::DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_revision() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", 96	## Module map
97	
98	CLI layer:
99	
100	- `src/main.rs` — the clap edge:
101	  - `pub struct Cli` — clap `Parser`.
102	  - `pub enum Commands` — clap `Subcommand`; matched in the
103	    dispatch arms.
104	  - `cli_with_banner()` — walks the command tree adding the
105	    `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as `before_help` on every subcommand.
106	  - `CompleteEnv` wiring for dynamic completion.
107	  - `bm_track` — a permanent `main`-bookmark tracking
108	    diagnostic printed on entry/exit of every command.
109	
110	- `src/options_flags/` — options/flags shared across
111	  subcommands, so a flag is defined once (parser, help,
112	  completer); Migration B tracks what's been moved here so
113	  far. See
114	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md).
115	  - reusable **leaves**: `account`, `config`, `dry_run`,
116	    `private`, `push_retry`, `repo`, `scope`, `squash`,
117	    `use_template`.
118	  - reusable **bundles**: `provision_bundle`.
119	- `src/common.rs` — `CommonArgs` (the shared positional-rev /
120	  `-R` repo-list / `-n` / `--limit` / `-L` flag set flattened
121	  by `chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`); `CommonParams`, its
122	  clap-free counterpart (resolved `DotSpec` + `Header` + repos,
123	  built `From<&CommonArgs>`); plus the repo-iteration and
124	  revision-resolution helpers they share. The 0.49.0 CommonArgs
125	  sweep relocates `CommonArgs` to `src/options_flags/` (-5) and
126	  swaps `-R` for `-s`/`--scope` (-6); the helpers stay here.
127	
128	Subcommand layer scaffolding:
129	
130	- `src/context.rs` — `Context`: the shared platform handle
131	  every subcommand runs against. Today it carries the loaded
132	  `UserConfig` and the `--log` path; built once at startup
133	  via `Context::load(log)`.
134	- `src/config.rs` — `UserConfig` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`).
135	- `src/scope.rs` — `Scope` enum (`Roles(Vec<Side>)` for the
136	  dual-repo `code`/`bot` roles, `Single(PathBuf)` for
137	  single-repo mode) and `parse_scope`.
138	
139	Subcommand modules — each holds an `XxxArgs` `#[derive(Args)]`
140	struct and a `pub fn x(...)` entrypoint:
141	
142	| Module | Subcommand | Notes |
143	| --- | --- | --- |
144	| `chid.rs` | `chid` | migrated (0.49.0-1) — `chid(&Context, &ChidParams)`, `From<&ChidArgs>`; flattens `CommonArgs` (→ `CommonParams`) |

151	| `init.rs` (+ `init/params.rs`) | `init` | subcommand-layer worked example (0.44.0) |
152	| `symlink.rs` | `symlink` | migrated (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`, `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
153	| `sync.rs` | `sync` | migrated (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`, `From<&SyncArgs>` |
154	| `finalize.rs` | `finalize` | migrated (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`, `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` |

157	Support:
158	
159	- `src/repo_utils.rs`, `src/url.rs`, `src/toml_simple.rs`,
160	  `src/logging.rs` — jj/repo helpers, URL parsing, a minimal
161	  TOML reader, the CLI logger.
162	- `src/test_helpers.rs`, `src/test_tmp_root.rs` —
163	  `#[cfg(test)]` fixtures (`Fixture` / `FixturePor`) and
164	  tempdir resolution. Subcommand modules also carry their

168	## Subcommand model
169	
170	Adding a subcommand `x`:
171	
172	1. Create `src/x.rs` with `pub struct XxxArgs`
173	   (`#[derive(Args)]`), composing leaves from
174	   `src/options_flags/` where one exists.
175	2. Add a variant `X(x::XxxArgs)` to `Commands` in
176	   `src/main.rs` with a `///` summary (and
177	   `#[command(long_about = …)]` for the long form).
178	3. Add a dispatch arm in `main()` calling `x::x(&args)` (or,
179	   once ported, `x::x(&ctx, &params)`).
180	4. Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help`; add
181	   `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, …)]` on any field whose doc
182	   comment uses bullets (clap otherwise reflows them into
183	   prose).
184	5. Dynamic value completion (`--account=<TAB>`) is an
185	   `ArgValueCompleter` attached to the leaf in
186	   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
187	   and stays at this layer.
188	
189	## Migration A — args → Context + Params
190	
191	Port each subcommand's `pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to
192	`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, adding an
193	`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the
194	conversion is fallible) at the binary edge. `init` (0.44.0) is
195	the worked example; `finalize` (0.46.0) added the `TryFrom` /
196	`Context.log` variant; the `0.48.0` cycle swept the standalone
197	subcommands; the `0.49.0` cycle is the "CommonArgs sweep" for
198	the four `CommonArgs`-flattening ones — Migration A (`chid` -1,
199	`desc` -2, `list` -3, `show` -4; these embed a shared clap-free
200	`CommonParams`), then Migration B (`CommonArgs` → `options_flags/`
201	leaf-bundle, -5) and the `--scope` rollout (`-R`/`--repo` →
202	`-s`/`--scope`, -6) — see the Migration B section below and
203	`notes/chores-09.md`. The live checklist is the "Subcommand
204	layer / CLI decoupling" item in [`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md).
205	
206	| Subcommand | Status |
207	| --- | --- |
208	| `init` | done (0.44.0) — `init(&Context, &InitParams)`; `From<&InitArgs>` |
209	| `finalize` | done (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`; `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` (fallible boundary); `--log` moved onto `Context` |
210	| `symlink` | done (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`; `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
211	| `clone` | done (0.48.0-2) — `clone_repo(&Context, &CloneParams)`; `From<&CloneArgs>` |
212	| `sync` | done (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`; `From<&SyncArgs>` |
213	| `validate-desc` | done (0.48.0-4) — `validate_desc(&Context, &ValidateDescParams)`; `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |
214	| `fix-desc` | done (0.48.0-5) — `fix_desc(&Context, &FixDescParams)`; `From<&FixDescArgs>` |
215	| `push` | done (0.48.0-6) — `push(&Context, &PushParams)`; `From<&PushArgs>` (collapses the two bookmark spellings) |
216	| `chid` | done (0.49.0-1) — `chid(&Context, &ChidParams)`; `From<&ChidArgs>` (wraps `CommonParams`). Migration B + `--scope` for `CommonArgs` land in 0.49.0-5/-6. |
217	| `desc` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-2) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep |
218	| `list` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-3) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep |
219	| `show` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-4) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep (`TryFrom`, `FileLimit` parse) |
220	
221	Out of scope for these ports (deferred until a real consumer
222	surfaces): typed errors, returned outcomes vs `println!`, the
223	`ProgressSink`, and `Context` fields beyond `UserConfig` + the
224	`--log` path (`finalize` surfaced `log`).
225	
226	## Migration B — per-subcommand flags → `src/options_flags/`
227	
228	Independently of Migration A, per-subcommand inline `#[arg]`
229	fields are being lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under
230	`src/options_flags/` so a flag is defined (parser, help,
231	completer) exactly once. See
232	[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
233	for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
234	Flag-vs-Option classification.
235	
236	State today:
237	
238	- **`init`** — fully composed from leaves/bundles
239	  (`account`, `repo`, `scope`, the `provision` bundle,
240	  `use_template`, `config`).
241	- **`chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`** — share
242	  `common::CommonArgs`, a per-domain shared struct rather
243	  than an `options_flags/` leaf. The 0.49.0 "CommonArgs
244	  sweep" cycle (in flight) folds these into the leaf model:
245	  0.49.0-5 decomposes `CommonArgs` into `options_flags/`
246	  leaves (`revision`, the `-n` commit limit, the `-l`/`-L`
247	  label pair, the two positionals) and relocates the bundle
248	  to `src/options_flags/common_bundle.rs`; 0.49.0-6 replaces
249	  the repeatable `-R`/`--repo` with `-s`/`--scope`
250	  (`code|bot|code,bot|<path>` — wiring up `scope.rs`'s
251	  `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single`, today `#[allow(dead_code)]`).
252	- **`finalize`** — `--squash` lifted to the `squash` leaf
253	  (which carries the `value`-field naming convention — see
254	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
255	  "Adding a new leaf"). `--delay` / `--detach` / `--exec` /

947	## refactor: CommonArgs → options_flags (0.49.0-1)
948	
949	Step 1 of the cycle (Migration B), and the point where the
950	cycle is re-scoped (see below). Decompose `common::CommonArgs`
951	into `options_flags/` leaves and relocate the bundle to
952	`src/options_flags/common_bundle.rs`, so the four read-only
953	commit-query subcommands flatten a proper leaf-bundle the way
954	`init` flattens `ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`. Pure refactor —
955	no behavior change; `vc-x1 chid -h` etc. are byte-identical.
956	
957	- New leaves (modeled on `squash.rs`): `revision`
958	  (`RevisionOption`, `-r`/`--revision`, default `@`),
959	  `commit_limit` (`CommitLimitOption`, `-n`/`--commits`),
960	  `repo_label` (`RepoLabelOptions`, the coupled `-l`/`-L`
961	  pair). The two positionals (`REVISION` / `COMMITS`) and the
962	  `-R`/`--repo` repo list stay inline in the bundle — no second
963	  consumer would compose them independently, and `-R` is on the
964	  chopping block in 0.49.0-2.
965	- `CommonOptionFlagBundle` (`common_bundle.rs`,
966	  `OptionFlagBundle` marker) flattens the three leaves +
967	  inline `pos_rev` / `pos_count` / `repos`. `CommonArgs`
968	  removed from `common.rs` (which keeps the
969	  `for_each_repo` / `collect_ids` / `resolve_*` / `format_*`
970	  helpers — those didn't move).
971	- `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` flatten the bundle; their
972	  bodies read `c.revision.value` / `c.limit.value` /
973	  `c.repo_label.{label,no_label}`. `main.rs`'s `suppress_banner`
974	  match reads `a.common.repo_label.no_label`. All four `.rs`
975	  files also gain the `//!` module docstring they were missing.
976	
977	### `value`-field clash on flattened leaves
978	
979	`RevisionOption` and `CommitLimitOption` both follow the
980	single-field-named-`value` convention
981	([`options_flags/README.md`](../src/options_flags/README.md)
982	"Adding a new leaf"). clap derives an arg's *id* from the field
983	name, so two `value` fields flattened into the same struct
984	collide — `clap_builder` panics at parse time ("Argument names
985	must be unique, but 'value' is in use by more than one
986	argument"). Fix: an explicit `#[arg(id = "revision")]` /
987	`#[arg(id = "commits")]` on each. The convention's worked
988	example (`finalize`'s `--squash`) never hit this because no
989	command had flattened two `value` leaves before — this is the
990	first; the README is updated to note the `id` requirement.
991	
992	### Cycle re-scope (0.49.0-1)
993	
994	The 0.49.0-0 plan opened a "finish Migration A" cycle for the
995	four `CommonArgs`-flattening subcommands. During 0.49.0-1
996	review the cycle was expanded to the full **"CommonArgs sweep"**
997	long planned in `chores-06` / `chores-07` — Migration A is
998	joined by Migration B and the `--scope` rollout for these four,
999	and re-ordered B-first so the Migration A ports land once,
1000	against the final `CommonArgs` shape. (The 0.49.0-0 commit and
1001	its chores section keep the original narrow framing; this
1002	subsection is the record of the change of plan.)
1003	
1004	- **Migration B** (this step, 0.49.0-1) — decompose
1005	  `CommonArgs` into `options_flags/` leaves + relocate the
1006	  bundle. Done; see above.
1007	- **`--scope`** (0.49.0-2) — replace the repeatable
1008	  `-R`/`--repo` with `-s`/`--scope` (`code|bot|code,bot|<path>`),
1009	  wiring up `scope.rs`'s `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single` (both
1010	  `#[allow(dead_code)]` — built in 0.42.0 for exactly this) and
1011	  `common.rs`'s `default_scope` / `scope_to_repos`. Per the
1012	  0.42.0 capture (`chores-06` 0.41.0-4): `-R` is dropped, not
1013	  aliased; arbitrary multi-repo (`-R . -R .claude`) is not
1014	  preserved — `--scope=<path>` covers single-repo, the default
1015	  is `default_scope()`. `for_each_repo` then takes an
1016	  already-resolved `Vec<PathBuf>` (comma-expansion + `["."]`
1017	  default move to the boundary). `init`'s `--scope` (the
1018	  separate `ScopeKind` `code,bot|por`) is left alone —
1019	  reconciling the two vocabularies is the "por/dual parity"
1020	  todo.
1021	- **Migration A** (0.49.0-3..-6) — `XxxParams` +
1022	  `fn x(&Context, &XxxParams)` ports against the post-B/-scope
1023	  `CommonArgs`; introduces the shared clap-free `CommonParams`
1024	  (resolved `DotSpec` + `Header` + repos). All four take a
1025	  fallible `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>` (scope→repo resolution can
1026	  error); `show` also parses `--files` into `FileLimit` at the
1027	  boundary.
1028	
1029	Revised ladder (supersedes the 0.49.0-0 one):
1030

This file covers the `0.49.0`\ncycle onward, plus a living **Migration A / Migration B\ntracking** section (the per-subcommand status that used to sit\nin `ARCHITECTURE.md`).\n\nSee [`../ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md) for what\nMigration A / B *are* and why; this file is the *how* and the\n*live status*. Reference numbering is file-local — see\n[`README.md`](README.md#reference-numbering); chores-10 starts\nat `[1]`.\n\n## Migration A / Migration B — live tracking\n\nTwo parallel refactors of the subcommand layer (see\n`ARCHITECTURE.md`). Status as of the entries below; update in\nplace as cycles land.\n\n### Migration A — `pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` → `pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`\n\n| Subcommand | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| `init` | done (0.44.0) — worked example; `From<&InitArgs>` |\n| `finalize` | done (0.46.0) — `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` (fallible); `--log` onto `Context` |\n| `symlink` | done (0.48.0-1) — `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |\n| `clone` | done (0.48.0-2) — `From<&CloneArgs>` |\n| `sync` | done (0.48.0-3) — `From<&SyncArgs>` |\n| `validate-desc` | done (0.48.0-4) — `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |\n| `fix-desc` | done (0.48.0-5) — `From<&FixDescArgs>` |\n| `push` | done (0.48.0-6) — `From<&PushArgs>` (collapses the two bookmark spellings) |\n| `chid` | pending (0.49.0-3) — introduces the shared `CommonParams`; `TryFrom` |\n| `desc` | pending (0.49.0-4) — `TryFrom` |\n| `list` | pending (0.49.0-5) — `TryFrom` |\n| `show` | pending (0.49.0-6) — `TryFrom`; also parses `--files` → `FileLimit` at the boundary |\n\nOut of scope for the ports (deferred until a real consumer\nsurfaces): typed errors, returned-outcomes-vs-`println!`,\n`ProgressSink`, `Context` fields beyond `UserConfig` + `--log`.\n\n### Migration B — per-subcommand inline `#[arg]` → `src/options_flags/` leaves/bundles\n\n| Subcommand(s) | Status |\n| --- | --- |\n| `init` | fully composed — `account` / `repo` / `scope` / the `provision` bundle / `use_template` / `config` |\n| `finalize` | `--squash` → `squash` leaf; `--delay` / `--detach` / `--exec` / `--repo` / `--push` still inline |\n| `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` | being moved onto `options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle` — `chid` 0.49.0-1.1, `desc` -1.3, `list` -1.4, `show` -1.5 (`common::CommonArgs` removed after the last); then `-R`/`--repo` → `-s`/`--scope` leaf in 0.49.0-2 |\n| `sync` / `push` / `clone` / `validate-desc` / `fix-desc` / `symlink` | mostly inline; the `--scope` retrofits queued in `todo.md` are the usual entry point |\n\n## chore: open 0.49.0 — finish Migration A (0.49.0-0)\n\nCommits: [[1]]\n\nMulti-step. Finish Migration A: port the last four subcommands\n`pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` → `pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params:\n&XxxParams)`, same shape as the `0.48.0` sweep. `chid` / `desc`\n/ `list` / `show` all `#[command(flatten)]` `common::CommonArgs`,\nso the cycle also adds a shared clap-free `CommonParams` they\nreuse. Mechanical; no behavior change.\n\n(Superseded at 0.49.0-1 — the cycle was expanded to the full\n\"CommonArgs sweep\", B-first; see the next section's `### Cycle\nre-scope`. This section keeps the original narrow framing as the\nrecord of what the 0.49.0-0 commit's plan was.)\n\n### Per-step shape\n\n- `common::CommonParams` (flat, clap-free): the resolved\n  `DotSpec` + `Header` + raw `repos: Vec<PathBuf>`, with\n  `impl From<&CommonArgs>` doing the `resolve_spec` /\n  `resolve_header` work at the binary edge. The `..` parsing and\n  `-l`/`-L` resolution move out of the subcommand bodies.\n- `XxxParams`: flat struct embedding `CommonParams`, plus the\n  subcommand's own fields — `list` adds `width: usize`, `show`\n  adds `files: FileLimit` (the `--files` string is parsed at the\n  boundary). `impl From<&XxxArgs>` (total) for `chid` / `desc` /\n  `list`; `impl TryFrom<&ShowArgs>` for `show` (fallible —\n  `FileLimit::parse`), mirroring `finalize`.\n- `pub fn x(args)` → `pub fn x(_ctx: &Context, params:\n  &XxxParams)`; `ctx` unused (uniform-signature placeholder, as\n  in `symlink` / `validate-desc` / `fix-desc`).\n- `main.rs` dispatch arm builds `Context::load(cli.log)` + the\n  params; the `suppress_banner` match keeps reading\n  `a.common.no_label` off the args (clap edge, unchanged).\n- Tests: existing `XxxArgs` parse tests untouched; add a small\n  \"construct `XxxParams` directly\" test per the worked-example\n  precedent.\n\n### Ladder (original — superseded)\n\nSmallest first; `show` (the `TryFrom` + `FileLimit` parse) last.\n\n- 0.49.0-0 plan + version bump + this section + todo ladder\n  (current)\n- 0.49.0-1 chid + introduce `CommonParams` in `common.rs`\n- 0.49.0-2 desc\n- 0.49.0-3 list\n- 0.49.0-4 show\n- 0.49.0 close-out — drop suffix, todo→Done, ARCHITECTURE.md\n  Migration A table all-done (12/12)\n\nThis cycle is Migration A only. Migration B for these four\n(folding `CommonArgs` into the `options_flags/` leaf model,\ndropping the repeatable `-R`/`--repo` for the `--scope` path\nform) stays the separate \"CommonArgs sweep\" todo.\n\n### Per-substep contract\n\nPer `notes/substep-protocol.md`: `cargo fmt` / `clippy\n--all-targets -- -D warnings` / `test` / `install --path .\n--locked` + retest before each commit; bump `Cargo.toml` at\nsub-step start; flip todo ladder markers; pair commits across\nboth repos with ochid trailers.\n\n## refactor: CommonArgs → options_flags (0.49.0-1)\n\nThe Migration B step of the cycle, and the point where the cycle\nis re-scoped (see `### Cycle re-scope`). Decompose\n`common::CommonArgs` into `options_flags/` leaves + a\n`common_bundle` bundle, so the four read-only commit-query\nsubcommands flatten a proper leaf-bundle the way `init` flattens\n`ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`. Pure refactor — no behavior change;\n`vc-x1 chid -h` etc. stay byte-identical.\n\nLanded across sub-steps so each commit is one migration, not a\ngiant move:\n\n- **0.49.0-1.1** — create the leaves + bundle; migrate `chid`.\n  New leaves (modeled on `squash.rs`): `revision`\n  (`RevisionOption`, `-r`/`--revision`, default `@`),\n  `commit_limit` (`CommitLimitOption`, `-n`/`--commits`),\n  `repo_label` (`RepoLabelOptions`, the coupled `-l`/`-L`\n  pair). `CommonOptionFlagBundle` (`common_bundle.rs`,\n  `OptionFlagBundle` marker) flattens the three leaves +\n  inline `pos_rev` / `pos_count` / `repos` (the two positionals\n  and the `-R` list stay inline — no second consumer composes\n  them, and `-R` is dropped in 0.49.0-2). `chid` flattens the\n  bundle; its body reads `c.revision.value` / `c.limit.value` /\n  `c.repo_label.{label,no_label}`. `main.rs`'s `suppress_banner`\n  match reads `a.common.repo_label.no_label` for `Chid`.\n  `chid.rs` gains the `//!` docstring it was missing.\n  `desc` / `list` / `show` keep flattening `common::CommonArgs`\n  for now (the two coexist).\n- **0.49.0-1.2** — the ARCHITECTURE.md slim + chores-10 reorg\n  (its own section below); slotted into this step's ladder\n  because ARCHITECTURE.md had accumulated this cycle's transient\n  detail.\n- **0.49.0-1.3 / -1.4 / -1.5** — migrate `desc`, `list`, `show`\n  onto the bundle in turn; -1.5 removes `CommonArgs` from\n  `common.rs` (which keeps the `for_each_repo` / `collect_ids` /\n  `resolve_*` / `format_*` helpers — those don't move) once\n  nothing references it.\n\n(Each `.rs` file also gains the `//!` module docstring it was\nmissing, as it's migrated.)\n\n### `value`-field clash on flattened leaves\n\n`RevisionOption` and `CommitLimitOption` both follow the\nsingle-field-named-`value` convention\n([`options_flags/README.md`](../src/options_flags/README.md)\n\"Adding a new leaf\"). clap derives an arg's *id* from the field\nname, so two `value` fields flattened into the same struct\ncollide — `clap_builder` panics at parse time (\"Argument names\nmust be unique, but 'value' is in use by more than one\nargument\"). Fix: an explicit `#[arg(id = \"revision\")]` /\n`#[arg(id = \"commits\")]` on each. The convention's worked\nexample (`finalize`'s `--squash`) never hit this because no\ncommand had flattened two `value` leaves before — this is the\nfirst; the README is updated to note the `id` requirement.\n\n### Cycle re-scope (0.49.0-1)\n\nThe 0.49.0-0 plan opened a \"finish Migration A\" cycle for the\nfour `CommonArgs`-flattening subcommands. During 0.49.0-1\nreview the cycle was expanded to the full **\"CommonArgs sweep\"**\nlong planned in `chores-06` / `chores-07` — Migration A is\njoined by Migration B and the `--scope` rollout for these four,\nand re-ordered B-first so the Migration A ports land once,\nagainst the final `CommonArgs` shape. (The 0.49.0-0 commit and\nits chores section keep the original narrow framing; this\nsubsection is the record of the change of plan.)\n\n- **Migration B** (0.49.0-1, sub-steps -1.1, -1.3, -1.4, -1.5;\n  `-1.2` is the docs reorg) — decompose `CommonArgs` into\n  `options_flags/` leaves + a bundle, migrate the four\n  subcommands one per sub-step, remove `CommonArgs`. See above.\n- **`--scope`** (0.49.0-2) — replace the repeatable\n  `-R`/`--repo` with `-s`/`--scope` (`code|bot|code,bot|<path>`),\n  wiring up `scope.rs`'s `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single` (both\n  `#[allow(dead_code)]` — built in 0.42.0 for exactly this) and\n  `common.rs`'s `default_scope` / `scope_to_repos`. Per the\n  0.42.0 capture (`chores-06` 0.41.0-4): `-R` is dropped, not\n  aliased; arbitrary multi-repo (`-R . -R .claude`) is not\n  preserved — `--scope=<path>` covers single-repo, the default\n  is `default_scope()`. `for_each_repo` then takes an\n  already-resolved `Vec<PathBuf>` (comma-expansion + `[\".\"]`\n  default move to the boundary). `init`'s `--scope` (the\n  separate `ScopeKind` `code,bot|por`) is left alone —\n  reconciling the two vocabularies is the \"por/dual parity\"\n  todo.\n- **Migration A** (0.49.0-3..-6) — `XxxParams` +\n  `fn x(&Context, &XxxParams)` ports against the post-B/-scope\n  `CommonArgs`; introduces the shared clap-free `CommonParams`\n  (resolved `DotSpec` + `Header` + repos). All four take a\n  fallible `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>` (scope→repo resolution can\n  error); `show` also parses `--files` into `FileLimit` at the\n  boundary.\n\nRevised ladder (supersedes the 0.49.0-0 one):\n\n- 0.49.0-1 Migration B — `CommonArgs` → `options_flags/`\n  leaf-bundle + relocate; this re-scope. Sub-steps:\n  - 0.49.0-1.1 leaves + bundle + migrate `chid`\n  - 0.49.0-1.2 docs: slim ARCHITECTURE.md; start chores-10\n  - 0.49.0-1.3 migrate `desc`\n  - 0.49.0-1.4 migrate `list`\n  - 0.49.0-1.5 migrate `show`; remove `CommonArgs`\n  - 0.49.0-1 close-out (squash to one commit or keep separate —\n    decided then)\n- 0.49.0-2 `-R`/`--repo` → `-s`/`--scope` (wire `parse_scope` /\n  `default_scope` / `scope_to_repos`; slim `for_each_repo`) —\n  may split into `-2.N`\n- 0.49.0-3 chid Migration A + introduce `CommonParams`\n- 0.49.0-4 desc Migration A\n- 0.49.0-5 list Migration A\n- 0.49.0-6 show Migration A (`TryFrom`, `FileLimit` parse)\n- 0.49.0 close-out — drop suffix, todo→Done (Migration A\n  12/12 + CommonArgs sweep), README + ARCHITECTURE.md\n\n## docs: slim ARCHITECTURE.md; chores-10 (0.49.0-1.2)\n\nActing on review feedback that `ARCHITECTURE.md` had drifted\ninto \"how\" / transient territory — per-subcommand migration\nstatus, version-by-version tables, sub-step ladders. Pull that\nout so `ARCHITECTURE.md` is \"what + some why, generic\" and the\ntransient tracking lives here.\n\n- `ARCHITECTURE.md` — keeps the Overview, the two-layer\n  (CLI-args vs `Context`+`Params`) section + rationale + the\n  `Naming` subsection, a generic module map (the *kinds* of\n  module and their roles, no per-subcommand table or version\n  annotations), the Subcommand-model recipe, and the See-also.\n  The `## Migration A` / `## Migration B` sections become short\n  \"what it is + why\" with a pointer here for live status — the\n  per-subcommand status table, the version-by-version \"done\"\n  list, and the \"State today\" bullets are gone.\n- `notes/chores-10.md` — new (this file). Carries the\n  `## Migration A / Migration B — live tracking` section (the\n  tables that came out of `ARCHITECTURE.md`) plus the `0.49.0-0`\n  and `0.49.0-1` sections moved out of `chores-09.md`.\n- `notes/chores-09.md` — the `0.49.0-*` sections removed; it now\n  ends at `0.48.4` (all done/closed).\n- `notes/README.md` — notes that `chores-09` is closed and\n  `chores-10` is the active file with the tracking section.\n- `notes/todo.md` — \"Design:\" link repointed to `chores-10.md`;\n  the `0.49.0-1` sub-step ladder inserts `-1.2` (this) and\n  shifts `desc` → `-1.3`, `list` → `-1.4`, `show` → `-1.5`.\n\n# References\n\n[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/10788bd158c4 \"10788bd158c4574fe5a10fab41ea32e4becc86d3\"\n"

1	# Architecture
2	
3	How the `vc-x1` binary is structured: the clap-aware CLI
4	layer and the (emerging) clap-free subcommand layer.
5	
6	This is a living document; the app is under continuous
7	development and the repo will keep changing. Per-cycle design
8	discussion lives in `notes/chores-*.md`; near-term tasks in
9	`notes/todo.md`.
10	
11	## Overview
12	
13	`vc-x1` is a single binary that supports subcommands,
14	`vc-x1 <subcommand>`, for managing a jj-git **dual-repo workspace**
15	with an app repo plus a `.claude` bot-session repo. The commits
16	cross-reference each other via `ochid:` trailers at the bottom
17	of each commit message. See [`README.md`](README.md)
18	for the user-facing picture and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) for
19	the bot workflow.
20	
21	## Two layers: CLI args vs subcommand Context + Params
22	
23	Goal: separate clap-aware argument parsing from subcommand
24	operation logic, so a future front-end (TUI, library
25	embedding) can call the same core without dragging clap
26	along. The trigger was `args.account.account`-style
27	nested-leaf access leaking into subcommand bodies; accessor
28	shortcuts were rejected as hiding the mismatch rather than
29	fixing it.
30	
31	- **CLI layer (clap-aware)**:
32	  Builds `XxxParams` from the user-facing `XxxArgs`
33	  `#[derive(Args)]` clap struct. Options/flags used in more
34	  than one subcommand live as flattened leaves in
35	  `src/options_flags/`.
36	- **Subcommand layer (clap-free)**:
37	  Entrypoint shape: `fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams) -> Result<…>`.
38	  And this isolates the subcommand from user and clap.
39	  - `Context` — common state shared with all subcommands.
40	  - `XxxParams` — a subcommand's parameters, derived from
41	    config or command-line arguments.
42	- **Boundary conversion**:
43	  Converting `XxxArgs` to `XxxParams` uses either
44	  `impl From<&XxxArgs> for XxxParams` or
45	  `impl TryFrom<&XxxArgs> for XxxParams`, depending on whether
46	  the conversion can fail.
47	
48	Two parameters per subcommand; the signature documents what
49	the subcommand depends on. `Context` is the same across all
50	subcommands; `XxxParams` carry the per-subcommand inputs.
51	
52	Rules for the subcommand layer (some still aspirational — see
53	[Migration A](#migration-a--args--context--params)):
54	
55	1. Plain options, flat fields, `Default` — no clap types in
56	   `XxxParams`. Domain types (`RepoSelector`, `Scope`) are
57	   fine; leaf wrappers (`RepoOption`) are not.
58	2. Typed errors (`enum XError`, not `Box<dyn Error>`) — a
59	   TUI matches variants to pick dialogs; CLI formats them.
60	3. Returned outcomes, not `println!` — each subcommand
61	   returns a structured result; CLI formats it, a library
62	   writes nothing to stdout itself.
63	4. Progress via an optional `&mut dyn ProgressSink` on
64	   long-running subcommands — CLI installs a stderr sink, tests a
65	   recording sink.
66	5. No globals, no implicit cwd/env reads in subcommands — CLI
67	   resolves cwd/env once at startup and builds `Context`.
68	
69	None of this is sacred — the whole structure is an experiment
70	and the repo keeps changing. The current scope is deliberately
71	narrow:
72	
73	- a small `Context` — two params, not one god blob;
74	- no trait-based DI yet;
75	- one crate, not a workspace split;
76	- `src/options_flags/` leaves left in place — only their
77	  consumers change shape.
78	
79	Widen any of it when the evidence (a second front-end, a second
80	consumer crate, a real platform-surface divergence) calls for
81	it — not before.
82	
83	### Naming
84	
85	Earlier drafts of this design (and the `notes/chores-09.md`
86	capture) used `Workspace` / `XOptions`. The implementation
87	(0.44.0) chose `Context` / `XxxParams` instead:
88	
89	- `Workspace` → `Context` — Cargo owns "workspace" formally,
90	  and this codebase already uses "workspace" for the
91	  dual-repo project root (`find_workspace_root`).
92	- `XOptions` → `XxxParams` — avoids visual collision with
93	  `Option<T>` (a params struct mixes required and
94	  `Option<T>`-typed fields) and with `src/options_flags/`.
95	
96	## Module map
97	
98	CLI layer:
99	
100	- `src/main.rs` — the clap edge:
101	  - `pub struct Cli` — clap `Parser`.
102	  - `pub enum Commands` — clap `Subcommand`; matched in the
103	    dispatch arms.
104	  - `cli_with_banner()` — walks the command tree adding the
105	    `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner as `before_help` on every subcommand.
106	  - `CompleteEnv` wiring for dynamic completion.
107	  - `bm_track` — a permanent `main`-bookmark tracking
108	    diagnostic printed on entry/exit of every command.
109	
110	- `src/options_flags/` — options/flags shared across
111	  subcommands, so a flag is defined once (parser, help,
112	  completer); Migration B tracks what's been moved here so
113	  far. See
114	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md).
115	  - reusable **leaves**: `account`, `commit_limit`, `config`,
116	    `dry_run`, `private`, `push_retry`, `repo`, `repo_label`,
117	    `revision`, `scope`, `squash`, `use_template`.
118	  - reusable **bundles**: `common_bundle`
119	    (`CommonOptionFlagBundle` — the read-only commit-query OFs,
120	    flattened by `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`),
121	    `provision_bundle`.
122	- `src/common.rs` — the repo-iteration and revision-resolution
123	  helpers the read-only commit-query subcommands share:
124	  `for_each_repo`, `collect_ids`, `resolve_revset`, `DotSpec` /
125	  `parse_dot_rev` / `resolve_spec` (`..` notation + count
126	  reconciliation), `Header` / `resolve_header`, the `format_*`
127	  printers, plus `find_workspace_root` / `default_scope` /
128	  `scope_to_repos`. Also still holds `CommonArgs` — being
129	  retired: the 0.49.0-1 sub-steps move the four read-only
130	  subcommands onto `options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle`
131	  one at a time (`chid` at 0.49.0-1.1), and `CommonArgs` is
132	  removed once the last lands; 0.49.0-2 then swaps `-R` for
133	  `-s`/`--scope`.
134	
135	Subcommand layer scaffolding:
136	
137	- `src/context.rs` — `Context`: the shared platform handle
138	  every subcommand runs against. Today it carries the loaded
139	  `UserConfig` and the `--log` path; built once at startup
140	  via `Context::load(log)`.
141	- `src/config.rs` — `UserConfig` (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`).
142	- `src/scope.rs` — `Scope` enum (`Roles(Vec<Side>)` for the
143	  dual-repo `code`/`bot` roles, `Single(PathBuf)` for
144	  single-repo mode) and `parse_scope`. `parse_scope` /
145	  `Scope::Single` are `#[allow(dead_code)]` until 0.49.0-2
146	  wires `-s`/`--scope` into the read-only commit-query commands.
147	
148	Subcommand modules — each holds an `XxxArgs` `#[derive(Args)]`
149	struct and a `pub fn x(...)` entrypoint:
150	
151	| Module | Subcommand | Notes |
152	| --- | --- | --- |
153	| `chid.rs` | `chid` | flattens `options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle` (0.49.0-1.1; Migration A → 0.49.0-3) |
154	| `desc.rs` (+ `desc_helpers.rs`) | `desc` | flattens `common::CommonArgs` → `CommonOptionFlagBundle` in 0.49.0-1.2; Migration A → 0.49.0-4 |
155	| `list.rs` | `list` | flattens `common::CommonArgs` + `-w`/`--width` → bundle in 0.49.0-1.3; Migration A → 0.49.0-5 |
156	| `show.rs` | `show` | flattens `common::CommonArgs` + `-f`/`--files` → bundle in 0.49.0-1.4; Migration A → 0.49.0-6 |
157	| `validate_desc.rs` | `validate-desc` | migrated (0.48.0-4) — `validate_desc(&Context, &ValidateDescParams)`, `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |
158	| `fix_desc.rs` | `fix-desc` | migrated (0.48.0-5) — `fix_desc(&Context, &FixDescParams)`, `From<&FixDescArgs>` |
159	| `clone.rs` | `clone` | migrated (0.48.0-2) — `clone_repo(&Context, &CloneParams)`, `From<&CloneArgs>` |
160	| `init.rs` (+ `init/params.rs`) | `init` | subcommand-layer worked example (0.44.0) |
161	| `symlink.rs` | `symlink` | migrated (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`, `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
162	| `sync.rs` | `sync` | migrated (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`, `From<&SyncArgs>` |
163	| `finalize.rs` | `finalize` | migrated (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`, `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` |
164	| `push.rs` | `push` | resumable state machine; migrated (0.48.0-6) — `push(&Context, &PushParams)`, `From<&PushArgs>` |
165	
166	Support:
167	
168	- `src/repo_utils.rs`, `src/url.rs`, `src/toml_simple.rs`,
169	  `src/logging.rs` — jj/repo helpers, URL parsing, a minimal
170	  TOML reader, the CLI logger.
171	- `src/test_helpers.rs`, `src/test_tmp_root.rs` —
172	  `#[cfg(test)]` fixtures (`Fixture` / `FixturePor`) and
173	  tempdir resolution. Subcommand modules also carry their
174	  own `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` (and `integration_tests` for
175	  `sync` / `push`).
176	
177	## Subcommand model
178	
179	Adding a subcommand `x`:
180	
181	1. Create `src/x.rs` with `pub struct XxxArgs`
182	   (`#[derive(Args)]`), composing leaves from
183	   `src/options_flags/` where one exists.
184	2. Add a variant `X(x::XxxArgs)` to `Commands` in
185	   `src/main.rs` with a `///` summary (and
186	   `#[command(long_about = …)]` for the long form).
187	3. Add a dispatch arm in `main()` calling `x::x(&args)` (or,
188	   once ported, `x::x(&ctx, &params)`).
189	4. Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help`; add
190	   `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, …)]` on any field whose doc
191	   comment uses bullets (clap otherwise reflows them into
192	   prose).
193	5. Dynamic value completion (`--account=<TAB>`) is an
194	   `ArgValueCompleter` attached to the leaf in
195	   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
196	   and stays at this layer.
197	
198	## Migration A — args → Context + Params
199	
200	Port each subcommand's `pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to
201	`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, adding an
202	`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the
203	conversion is fallible) at the binary edge. `init` (0.44.0) is
204	the worked example; `finalize` (0.46.0) added the `TryFrom` /
205	`Context.log` variant; the `0.48.0` cycle swept the standalone
206	subcommands; the `0.49.0` cycle is the "CommonArgs sweep" for
207	the four `CommonArgs`-flattening ones — first Migration B
208	(decompose `CommonArgs` → `options_flags/` leaf-bundle, -1) and
209	the `--scope` rollout (`-R`/`--repo` → `-s`/`--scope`, -2), then
210	Migration A against the final shape (`chid` -3, `desc` -4,
211	`list` -5, `show` -6; these embed a shared clap-free
212	`CommonParams`, and all four take a fallible `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>`
213	because scope→repo resolution can error). See the Migration B
214	section below and `notes/chores-09.md`. The live checklist is
215	the "Subcommand layer / CLI decoupling" item in
216	[`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md).
217	
218	| Subcommand | Status |
219	| --- | --- |
220	| `init` | done (0.44.0) — `init(&Context, &InitParams)`; `From<&InitArgs>` |
221	| `finalize` | done (0.46.0) — `finalize(&Context, &FinalizeParams)`; `TryFrom<&FinalizeArgs>` (fallible boundary); `--log` moved onto `Context` |
222	| `symlink` | done (0.48.0-1) — `symlink(&Context, &SymlinkParams)`; `From<&SymlinkArgs>` |
223	| `clone` | done (0.48.0-2) — `clone_repo(&Context, &CloneParams)`; `From<&CloneArgs>` |
224	| `sync` | done (0.48.0-3) — `sync(&Context, &SyncParams)`; `From<&SyncArgs>` |
225	| `validate-desc` | done (0.48.0-4) — `validate_desc(&Context, &ValidateDescParams)`; `From<&ValidateDescArgs>` |
226	| `fix-desc` | done (0.48.0-5) — `fix_desc(&Context, &FixDescParams)`; `From<&FixDescArgs>` |
227	| `push` | done (0.48.0-6) — `push(&Context, &PushParams)`; `From<&PushArgs>` (collapses the two bookmark spellings) |
228	| `chid` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-3) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep; introduces the shared `CommonParams` |
229	| `desc` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-4) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep |
230	| `list` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-5) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep |
231	| `show` | Migration A pending (0.49.0-6) — the 0.49.0 CommonArgs sweep (`TryFrom`, `FileLimit` parse) |
232	
233	Out of scope for these ports (deferred until a real consumer
234	surfaces): typed errors, returned outcomes vs `println!`, the
235	`ProgressSink`, and `Context` fields beyond `UserConfig` + the
236	`--log` path (`finalize` surfaced `log`).
237	
238	## Migration B — per-subcommand flags → `src/options_flags/`
239	
240	Independently of Migration A, per-subcommand inline `#[arg]`
241	fields are being lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under
242	`src/options_flags/` so a flag is defined (parser, help,
243	completer) exactly once. See
244	[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
245	for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
246	Flag-vs-Option classification.
247	
248	State today:
249	
250	- **`init`** — fully composed from leaves/bundles
251	  (`account`, `repo`, `scope`, the `provision` bundle,
252	  `use_template`, `config`).
253	- **`chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`** — being migrated off
254	  `common::CommonArgs` onto
255	  `options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle` (the
256	  0.49.0 "CommonArgs sweep" cycle, one subcommand per sub-step:
257	  `chid` 0.49.0-1.1, `desc` -1.2, `list` -1.3, `show` -1.4 —
258	  `CommonArgs` removed when the last lands). The bundle is
259	  composed of the `revision` and `commit_limit` leaves, the
260	  `repo_label` leaf (the `-l`/`-L` pair), plus the two
261	  positionals (`REVISION` / `COMMITS`) and the `-R`/`--repo`
262	  list inline; `-R`/`--repo` is then swapped for a `--scope`
263	  leaf (`code|bot|code,bot|<path>` — wiring up `scope.rs`'s
264	  `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single`) in 0.49.0-2; the positionals
265	  stay inline. (Two of the leaves — `RevisionOption`,
266	  `CommitLimitOption` — both use the `value` field-name
267	  convention, so each carries an explicit `#[arg(id = …)]` to
268	  keep clap arg ids unique when flattened into the same struct.)
269	- **`finalize`** — `--squash` lifted to the `squash` leaf
270	  (which carries the `value`-field naming convention — see
271	  [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
272	  "Adding a new leaf"). `--delay` / `--detach` / `--exec` /
273	  `--repo` / `--push` stay inline (no second consumer yet).
274	- **`sync` / `push` / `clone` / `validate-desc` /
275	  `fix-desc` / `symlink`** — still mostly inline `#[arg]`
276	  fields. The `--scope` retrofits queued in
277	  [`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md) are the usual entry
278	  point for converting one.
279	
280	## See also
281	
282	- [`README.md`](README.md) — user-facing overview and
283	  per-subcommand usage.
284	- [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) — bot workflow, versioning,
285	  commit/push conventions, code conventions.
286	- [`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
287	  — leaf/bundle patterns for Migration B.
288	- [`notes/todo.md`](notes/todo.md) — live task list,
289	  including both migrations.
290	- [`notes/chores-09.md`](notes/chores-09.md) — the
291	  0.43.0 / 0.44.0 design capture this document supersedes.

> AGENT

Those are all fair — and I think they point at the same root cause: `0.49.0-1.1` decomposed `CommonArgs` into single-field leaves (`revision`, `commit_limit`) that buy *zero* reuse, and that decomposition is what dragged in the `value`/`id` awkwardness and the mixed-shape bundle. My take on each:

**1. `value` vs `id` — sharp edge, and not worth it here.** The `value`-field convention (`squash.rs`) is fine when exactly one such leaf sits in a struct — clap derives the arg *id* from the field name, so a lone `value` field is unambiguous. The moment you flatten *two* `value` leaves, the ids collide and you need `#[arg(id=…)]` to disambiguate. So the rule would be "field is `value`; if it can be flattened next to another `value` leaf, also give it an explicit `id`" — which is exactly the "not obvious when" you're flagging. For `revision`/`commit_limit` this paid nothing: no second consumer, so they're not "defined once" any more than they would be as inline fields of the shared bundle. Not a dead end for `squash.rs`'s case, but the wrong tool here.

**2. The bundle mixes inline (`pos_rev`/`pos_count`/`repos`) and leaf-flattened (`revision`/`limit`/`repo_label`) fields** — a symptom of (1). The fix: don't decompose at all. `CommonArgs` becomes a shared `#[derive(Args)]` struct relocated into `options_flags/` (all 7 fields inline, no sub-leaves) — uniform, no `value`/`id`, and it still satisfies "the shared arg set lives in `options_flags/`, defined once". (`options_flags/` then has three shapes: leaves, bundles-of-leaves like `provision_bundle`, and shared-args groups like this — worth a README note. Or keep it a "bundle" in name; bikeshed.)

**3. `RepoLabelOptions` → one `label: Option<String>`?** Doesn't quite work in clap-derive: there's no clean way for `--no-label` to write `None` into a `label: Option<String>` field, and `--label` alone never yields `None` — so you'd still end up with a `no_label: bool` companion. `label: String` (default `===`) + `no_label: bool` is the natural "value flag + its negation flag" shape; `resolve_header` combines them. (`--label ""` is *technically* distinct from `--no-label` — empty-decoration header line vs no header at all — though obscure. And re "is empty string used": not as a default, but a user could pass it; the `String` field allows it.) A *possible future CLI simplification* is dropping `-L`/`--no-label` and using `-l ""` for "no header" — but that's a behavior change, not part of this refactor.

So I'd propose: **amend `0.49.0-1.1` (and the matching bits of `0.49.0-1.2`'s `chores-10.md`)** to drop the three leaf files — `CommonArgs` just relocates into `options_flags/` (e.g. `options_flags/common_args.rs`, fields inline), `chid` flattens it, the `### value-field clash` chores subsection and the `options_flags/README.md` `id`-caveat note go away. Then `0.49.0-1.3/.4/.5` migrate `desc`/`list`/`show` onto the relocated struct, `0.49.0-1.5` removes `src/common.rs`'s `CommonArgs`, and `0.49.0-2` swaps the inline `repos` for `--scope` as before.

That's a two-commit amend (`0.49.0-1.1` is `@--`, `0.49.0-1.2` is `@-`; jj rebases the latter over the former). Want me to do that? And — keep the name `CommonOptionFlagBundle` in `common_bundle.rs`, or go `CommonArgs` in `common_args.rs`?

The statement "The fix: don't decompose at all". Are you saying we should only have the notiion of "Bundles" and only if two or more subcommands have the exact same set of arguments would anything be shared?

> DEVELOPER

The statement "The fix: don't decompose at all". Are you saying we should only have the notiion of "Bundles" and only if two or more subcommands have the exact same set of arguments would anything be shared?

> AGENT

Not quite — I'm not saying drop the leaf concept. Leaves and bundles-of-leaves stay; they're earning their keep (`init` is fully leaf-composed; `provision_bundle` flattens `dry_run`/`private`/`push_retry`, and each of those *is* independently meaningful — `--dry-run` will land on `clone`, etc.).

The distinction I'm drawing is about *granularity vs. actual reuse*:

- **Make a leaf when that specific flag / small group is genuinely shared at that granularity** — `--dry-run`, `--squash`, `--scope`, `--account`, `--push-retries`+`--push-retry-delay`. Those show up (or will) on commands that *don't* share the rest of each other's args, so a per-flag leaf is the unit of sharing.
- **When a whole *set* of args is shared by N commands but the individual args inside it aren't reused anywhere else, the right shape is one shared `#[derive(Args)]` struct with inline fields** — not N per-flag leaves flattened into it. Atomizing it preemptively (a `revision.rs` leaf nobody else composes) buys nothing and drags in the `value`/`id` friction. That's the README's "Layout note" ("Mechanical when needed; not done preemptively") applied at flag granularity.

And sharing isn't only "exact same set":
- `init` / `clone` share a *sub-set* (the provision leaves) + each has its own args → leaves + a bundle of them.
- `chid` / `desc` share *exactly* `CommonArgs`; `list` adds `--width`, `show` adds `--files` → they flatten the shared struct **plus** their own extras. So `CommonArgs` is the shared whole-set; the extras stay per-command.

So `CommonArgs` → one shared struct in `options_flags/`, fields inline, flattened by all four (`list`/`show` adding their extra `#[arg]` alongside). Call it a "bundle" or a "shared args group" — either label is fine; the README documents the shape. If some future command wants just `--revision`, *then* extract a `revision` leaf — when the need is real.

So my proposal stands: amend `0.49.0-1.1` (+ the matching `chores-10` bits in `0.49.0-1.2`) to drop the three leaf files — `CommonArgs` relocates into `options_flags/` with inline fields, `chid` flattens it, the `value`-field-clash subsection and the README `id`-caveat go away. Then `-1.3/.4/.5` migrate `desc`/`list`/`show`, `-1.5` removes `src/common.rs`'s `CommonArgs`, `0.49.0-2` does `--scope`.

Go ahead with that amend? (And: `CommonArgs` in `options_flags/common_args.rs`, or keep `CommonOptionFlagBundle` in `common_bundle.rs`?)

At that point `CommonArgs` becomes a hybrid (some inline fields, some composed leaves) — which is fine *when the extraction is justified by real reuse*, unlike `0.49.0-1.1` where it wasn't (the mix there was the symptom).

29:pub struct CommonArgs {
=== chid.rs ===
//! `chid` subcommand — print the short change ID of each commit in a
//! revision range, one per line (script-friendly output).
//!
//! - `ChidArgs`: clap surface; flattens
//!   `options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle`.
//! - `chid(&ChidArgs)`: the op — `resolve_spec` / `resolve_header` /
//!   `for_each_repo` + print `format_chid`.

use clap::Args;
use jj_lib::repo::Repo;
use log::{debug, info};

use crate::common;
use crate::options_flags::common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle;

/// CLI args for `chid` — just the shared read-only commit-query OFs.
#[derive(Args, Debug)]
pub struct ChidArgs {
    #[command(flatten)]
    pub common: CommonOptionFlagBundle,
}

/// Print the short change ID of each commit in the resolved range.
pub fn chid(args: &ChidArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    debug!("chid: enter");
    let c = &args.common;
    let spec = common::resolve_spec(
        c.pos_rev.as_deref(),
        c.pos_count,
        &c.revision.value,
        c.limit.value,
        "@",
    );
    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.repo_label.label, c.repo_label.no_label);

    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {
        let (ids, _) =
            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;

        for commit_id in &ids {
            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;
            info!("{}", common::format_chid(&commit));
        }
        Ok(())
    })?;
    debug!("chid: exit");
    Ok(())
}

  "content": "//! `chid` subcommand — print the short change ID of each commit in a\n//! revision range, one per line (script-friendly output).\n//!\n//! - `ChidArgs`: clap surface; flattens\n//!   `options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs`.\n//! - `chid(&ChidArgs)`: the op — `resolve_spec` / `resolve_header` /\n//!   `for_each_repo` + print `format_chid`.\n\nuse clap::Args;\nuse jj_lib::repo::Repo;\nuse log::{debug, info};\n\nuse crate::common;\nuse crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;\n\n/// CLI args for `chid` — just the shared read-only commit-query args.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct ChidArgs {\n    #[command(flatten)]\n    pub common: CommonArgs,\n}\n\n/// Print the short change ID of each commit in the resolved range.\npub fn chid(args: &ChidArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    debug!(\"chid: enter\");\n    let c = &args.common;\n    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, \"@\");\n    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);\n\n    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {\n        let (ids, _) =\n            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;\n\n        for commit_id in &ids {\n            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;\n            info!(\"{}\", common::format_chid(&commit));\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    })?;\n    debug!(\"chid: exit\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use std::path::PathBuf;\n\n    use clap::Parser;\n\n    use crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;\n    use crate::{Cli, Commands};\n\n    fn parse(args: &[&str]) -> CommonArgs {\n        let cli = Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap();\n        match cli.command {\n            Commands::Chid(a) => a.common,\n            _ => panic!(\"expected Chid\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn defaults() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"@\");\n        assert!(c.repos.is_empty());\n        assert_eq!(c.limit, None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_revision() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-r\", \"@-\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"@-\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_repo() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-R\", \".claude\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\".claude\")]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_limit() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-n\", \"5\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.limit, Some(5));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_opts() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-r\", \"@--\", \"-R\", \".claude\", \"-n\", \"3\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"@--\");\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\".claude\")]);\n        assert_eq!(c.limit, Some(3));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn multi_repo() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-R\", \".\", \"-R\", \".claude\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\".\"), PathBuf::from(\".claude\")]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn comma_repo() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-R\", \".,.claude\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\".,.claude\")]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn label_default() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.label, \"===\");\n        assert!(!c.no_label);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn label_custom() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-l\", \"---\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.label, \"---\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn no_label() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"-L\"]);\n        assert!(c.no_label);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_rev() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"@-\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"@-\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_rev_and_count() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"@..\", \"5\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"@..\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, Some(5));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_both_dots() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"chid\", \"..abcd..\", \"3\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"..abcd..\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, Some(3));\n    }\n}\n"
}

`format_commit_full` + `indent_body`.\n\nuse clap::Args;\nuse jj_lib::repo::Repo;\nuse log::{debug, info};\n\nuse crate::common;\nuse crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;\n\n/// CLI args for `desc` — just the shared read-only commit-query args.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct DescArgs {\n    #[command(flatten)]\n    pub common: CommonArgs,\n}\n\n/// Print each commit in the resolved range with its full description.\npub fn desc(args: &DescArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    debug!(\"desc: enter\");\n    let c = &args.common;\n    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, \"@\");\n    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);\n\n    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {\n        let (ids, anchor_index) =\n            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;\n\n        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {\n            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;\n            let bookmarks = common::format_bookmarks_at(repo, commit_id);\n            let line = common::format_commit_full(&commit, &bookmarks);\n            let indented = common::indent_body(&line, 4);\n            if i == anchor_index {\n                info!(\"{}\", common::bold_first_line(&indented));\n            } else {\n                info!(\"{indented}\");\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(())\n    })?;\n    debug!(\"desc: exit\");\n    Ok(())\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests {\n    use std::path::PathBuf;\n\n    use clap::Parser;\n\n    use crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;\n    use crate::{Cli, Commands};\n\n    fn parse(args: &[&str]) -> CommonArgs {\n        let cli = Cli::try_parse_from(args).unwrap();\n        match cli.command {\n            Commands::Desc(a) => a.common,\n            _ => panic!(\"expected Desc\"),\n        }\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn defaults() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"@\");\n        assert!(c.repos.is_empty());\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_revision() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"-r\", \"wmuxkqwu\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"wmuxkqwu\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_repo() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"-R\", \"/tmp\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\"/tmp\")]);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_limit() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"-n\", \"3\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.limit, Some(3));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_rev() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"@-\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"@-\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, None);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_rev_and_count() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"@..\", \"5\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"@..\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, Some(5));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn positional_both_dots() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"..abcd..\", \"3\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_rev, Some(\"..abcd..\".to_string()));\n        assert_eq!(c.pos_count, Some(3));\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn all_opts() {\n        let c = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"desc\", \"-r\", \"@-\", \"-R\", \".claude\", \"-n\", \"5\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.revision, \"@-\");\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, \".claude\"]);\n        assert_eq!(c.repos, vec![PathBuf::from(\".\"), PathBuf::from(\".claude\")]);\n    }\n}\n"
}

flattens\n//!   `options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs` plus a `-w`/`--width`\n//!   for the ochid column.\n//! - `list(&ListArgs)`: the op — `resolve_spec` / `resolve_header` /\n//!   `for_each_repo` + `format_commit_with_ochid`.\n\nuse clap::Args;\nuse jj_lib::repo::Repo;\nuse log::{debug, info, trace, warn};\n\nuse crate::common;\nuse crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;\n\n/// CLI args for `list` — the shared read-only commit-query args plus\n/// the ochid column width.\n#[derive(Args, Debug)]\npub struct ListArgs {\n    #[command(flatten)]\n    pub common: CommonArgs,\n\n    /// ochid column width\n    #[arg(short = 'w', long = \"width\", default_value_t = DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH)]\n    pub width: usize,\n}\n\nconst DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH: usize = 21;\n\n/// List commits in the resolved range with the ochid column.\npub fn list(args: &ListArgs) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    debug!(\"list: enter\");\n    let c = &args.common;\n    let spec = common::resolve_spec(c.pos_rev.as_deref(), c.pos_count, &c.revision, c.limit, \"@\");\n    trace!(\n        \"list: spec rev={} desc={:?} anc={:?}\",\n        spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count\n    );\n    let hdr = common::resolve_header(&c.label, c.no_label);\n\n    common::for_each_repo(&c.repos, &hdr, |workspace, repo| {\n        let (ids, anchor_index) =\n            common::collect_ids(workspace, repo, &spec.rev, spec.desc_count, spec.anc_count)?;\n        debug!(\"list: {} commits, anchor at {anchor_index}\", ids.len());\n\n        if ids.is_empty() {\n            warn!(\"list: no commits found for revision '{}'\", spec.rev);\n        }\n\n        for (i, commit_id) in ids.iter().enumerate() {\n            let commit = repo.store().get_commit(commit_id)?;\n            let bookmarks = common::format_bookmarks_at(repo, commit_id);\n            let line = common::format_commit_with_ochid(&commit, args.width, &bookmarks);\n            if i == anchor_index {\n                info!(\"{}\", common::bold(&line));\n            } else {\n                info!(\"{line}\");\n            }\n        }\n assert!(args.common.repos.is_empty());\n        assert!(args.common.limit.is_none());\n        assert_eq!(args.width, super::DEFAULT_OCHID_WIDTH);\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_revision() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", \"list\", \"-r\", \"@-\"]);\n        assert_eq!(args.common.revision, \"@-\");\n    }\n\n    #[test]\n    fn with_repo() {\n        let args = parse(&[\"vc-x1\", 12	## Architecture
13	
14	Three composition patterns:
15	
16	- **Leaf** — a `#[derive(Args)]` struct holding the flag(s),
17	  `value_parser`, default, and help text (via the field
18	  doc-comment). One `#[derive(Args)]` per logical OF — single
19	  flag or a small fixed pair (e.g. `push_retry`'s two fields).
20	  Help text aims to be generic enough for any reasonable
21	  consumer.
22	- **Bundle** — a `#[derive(Args)]` that flattens N leaves into a
23	  named role (e.g. `ProvisionOptionFlagBundle`). One
24	  `#[command(flatten)]` line at the consumer picks up the whole
25	  bundle.
26	- **Pattern A escape hatch** — when a consumer needs unique help
27	  text (or different defaults), it skips the leaf's flatten and
28	  inlines its own `#[arg(value_parser = …)]` field, reusing the
29	  leaf's typed value and parser.
30	
31	## Flag vs Option — classify by domain, not wire syntax
32	
33	Every leaf falls into one of two categories, picked by the value
34	domain it carries:
35	
36	- **Flag** — boolean domain. Wire form may be presence/absence

Use this when the constituent\n    flags are themselves reused elsewhere.\n  - *inline-fields* — holds the `#[arg]` fields directly (e.g.\n    `common_args::CommonArgs` — the read-only commit-query arg\n    set).
