The convention's worked\nexample (`finalize`'s `--squash`) never hit this because no\ncommand had flattened two `value` leaves before — this is the\nfirst; the README is updated to note the `id` requirement.",
  "new_string": "### Why not decompose into leaves\n\nThe first take on this step decomposed `CommonArgs` into\nper-flag `options_flags/` leaves (`revision`, `commit_limit`,\n`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring how\n`init` composes `provision_bundle` from `dry_run` / `private` /\n`push_retry`. Backed out, because the two are not the same case:\n\n- **No reuse.** `init`'s constituent leaves *are* reused (e.g.\n  `--dry-run` will land on `clone`), so a per-flag leaf is the\n  unit of sharing. `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` share the\n  *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit` / `label` / etc. is\n  reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves would buy nothing the\n  shared struct doesn't already give.\n- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two leaves built on the\n  single-field-named-`value` convention\n  ([`options_flags/README.md`](../src/options_flags/README.md))\n  collide on the clap arg *id* (which clap derives from the\n  field name) when flattened into the same struct —\n  `clap_builder` panics (\"duplicate arg id `value`\"). The fix\n  is an explicit `#[arg(id = …)]` on each, which is exactly the\n  \"not obvious when `id` vs `value`\" sharp edge — and entirely\n  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be\n  leaves.\n\nRule of thumb: make a leaf when *that flag / small group* is\ngenuinely shared at that granularity; when a *whole arg set* is\nshared by N commands but its parts aren't reused, a single\ninline-fields bundle is the shape. Extract a leaf later, when a\nsecond consumer is real — `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s\nthe extracted type (one definition, no duplication).\n\n(The `options_flags/README.md` \"Adding a new leaf\" caveat about\n`#[arg(id = …)]` for co-flattened `value` leaves stays — it's a\nreal gotcha for the leaf case — but with no in-tree example now.)"

116	## refactor: CommonArgs → options_flags (0.49.0-1)
117	
118	The Migration B step of the cycle, and the point where the cycle
119	is re-scoped (see `### Cycle re-scope`). Relocate
120	`common::CommonArgs` — the shared arg set for the four read-only
121	commit-query subcommands — from `src/common.rs` into
122	`src/options_flags/common_args.rs`, so it lives in the shared
123	OF store like `init`'s provision bundle. Fields stay **inline**,
124	no per-flag sub-leaves (an "inline-fields bundle" — see
125	[Bundle](../src/options_flags/README.md#architecture)): none of
126	`revision` / `limit` / `label` / etc. is reused outside these
127	four, so extracting per-flag leaves would buy no reuse — if one
128	ever *is* reused, extract that field into a leaf then and
129	`#[command(flatten)]` it here. Pure relocation — no behavior
130	change; `vc-x1 chid -h` etc. byte-identical.
131	
132	Sub-steps:
133	
134	- **0.49.0-1.1** — the relocation: `CommonArgs` moves to
135	  `options_flags/common_args.rs` (`impl OptionFlagBundle`),
136	  `src/common.rs`'s `CommonArgs` (and its `use clap::Args;`)
137	  removed (the `for_each_repo` / `collect_ids` / `resolve_*` /
138	  `format_*` helpers stay), all four subcommands flatten the
139	  relocated struct (`use crate::options_flags::common_args::CommonArgs;`),
140	  and each `.rs` file gains the `//!` module docstring it was
141	  missing. `main.rs`'s `suppress_banner` reads
142	  `a.common.no_label` for all four (back to pre-cycle). Bodies
143	  otherwise unchanged.
144	- **0.49.0-1.2** — the ARCHITECTURE.md slim + chores-10 reorg
145	  (its own section below); slotted into this step's ladder
146	  because ARCHITECTURE.md had accumulated this cycle's transient
147	  detail.
148	
149	(An earlier `0.49.0-1.1` decomposed `CommonArgs` into per-flag
150	`options_flags/` leaves — `revision` / `commit_limit` /
151	`repo_label` — flattened into a `common_bundle::CommonOptionFlagBundle`.
152	Backed out on review: the leaves bought no reuse and dragged in a
153	`value`/`id` clap-id clash. See `### Why not decompose into
154	leaves`. The `0.49.0-1.1` commit was amended in place to the
155	relocation above.)
156	
157	### Why not decompose into leaves
158	
159	The first take on this step decomposed `CommonArgs` into
160	per-flag `options_flags/` leaves (`revision`, `commit_limit`,
161	`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring how
162	`init` composes `provision_bundle` from `dry_run` / `private` /
163	`push_retry`. Backed out, because the two are not the same case:
164	
165	- **No reuse.** `init`'s constituent leaves *are* reused (e.g.
166	  `--dry-run` will land on `clone`), so a per-flag leaf is the
167	  unit of sharing. `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` share the
168	  *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit` / `label` / etc. is
169	  reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves would buy nothing the
170	  shared struct doesn't already give.
171	- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two leaves built on the
172	  single-field-named-`value` convention
173	  ([`options_flags/README.md`](../src/options_flags/README.md))
174	  collide on the clap arg *id* (which clap derives from the
175	  field name) when flattened into the same struct —
176	  `clap_builder` panics ("duplicate arg id `value`"). The fix
177	  is an explicit `#[arg(id = …)]` on each, which is exactly the
178	  "not obvious when `id` vs `value`" sharp edge — and entirely
179	  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be
180	  leaves.
181	
182	Rule of thumb: make a leaf when *that flag / small group* is
183	genuinely shared at that granularity; when a *whole arg set* is
184	shared by N commands but its parts aren't reused, a single
185	inline-fields bundle is the shape. Extract a leaf later, when a
186	second consumer is real — `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s
187	the extracted type (one definition, no duplication).
188	
189	(The `options_flags/README.md` "Adding a new leaf" caveat about
190	`#[arg(id = …)]` for co-flattened `value` leaves stays — it's a
191	real gotcha for the leaf case — but with no in-tree example now.)
192	
193	### Cycle re-scope (0.49.0-1)
194	
195	The 0.49.0-0 plan opened a "finish Migration A" cycle for the
196	four `CommonArgs`-flattening subcommands. During 0.49.0-1
197	review the cycle was expanded to the full **"CommonArgs sweep"**
198	long planned in `chores-06` / `chores-07` — Migration A is
199	joined by Migration B and the `--scope` rollout for these four,
200	and re-ordered B-first so the Migration A ports land once,
201	against the final `CommonArgs` shape. (The 0.49.0-0 commit and
202	its chores section keep the original narrow framing; this
203	subsection is the record of the change of plan.)
204	
205	- **Migration B** (0.49.0-1, sub-steps -1.1 the relocation,
206	  -1.2 the docs reorg) — relocate `CommonArgs` into
207	  `options_flags/common_args.rs` (inline-fields bundle, no
208	  per-flag leaves), move all four subcommands onto it, remove
209	  `src/common.rs`'s `CommonArgs`. See above.
210	- **`--scope`** (0.49.0-2) — replace the repeatable

The `0.49.0-1.1` commit was amended in place to the\nrelocation above.)\n\n### Why not decompose into leaves\n\nThe first take on this step decomposed `CommonArgs` into\nper-flag `options_flags/` leaves (`revision`, `commit_limit`,\n`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring how\n`init` composes `provision_bundle` from `dry_run` / `private` /\n`push_retry`. Backed out, because the two are not the same case:\n\n- **No reuse.** `init`'s constituent leaves *are* reused (e.g.\n  `--dry-run` will land on `clone`), so a per-flag leaf is the\n  unit of sharing. `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show` share the\n  *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit` / `label` / etc. is\n  reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves would buy nothing the\n  shared struct doesn't already give.\n- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two leaves built on the\n  single-field-named-`value` convention\n  ([`options_flags/README.md`](../src/options_flags/README.md))\n  collide on the clap arg *id* (which clap derives from the\n  field name) when flattened into the same struct —\n  `clap_builder` panics (\"duplicate arg id `value`\"). The fix\n  is an explicit `#[arg(id = …)]` on each, which is exactly the\n  \"not obvious when `id` vs `value`\" sharp edge — and entirely\n  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be\n  leaves.\n\nRule of thumb: make a leaf when *that flag / small group* is\ngenuinely shared at that granularity; when a *whole arg set* is\nshared by N commands but its parts aren't reused, a single\ninline-fields bundle is the shape. Extract a leaf later, when a\nsecond consumer is real — `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s\nthe extracted type (one definition, no duplication).\n\n(The `options_flags/README.md` \"Adding a new leaf\" caveat about\n`#[arg(id = …)]` for co-flattened `value` leaves stays — it's a\nreal gotcha for the leaf case — but with no in-tree example now.)",
  "new_string": "## refactor: CommonArgs → options_flags (0.49.0-1)\n\nThe Migration B step (and where the cycle is re-scoped — see\n`### Cycle re-scope`). Inline\nfields, no per-flag sub-leaves (an \"inline-fields bundle\" — see\n[Bundle](../src/options_flags/README.md#architecture); rationale\nin `### Why not decompose into leaves`). Pure relocation —\n`vc-x1 chid -h` etc. byte-identical.\n\nSub-steps:\n\n- **0.49.0-1.1** — the relocation:\n  - `CommonArgs` → `options_flags/common_args.rs` (`impl OptionFlagBundle`).\n  - `src/common.rs`: `CommonArgs` + `use clap::Args` dropped\n    (the `for_each_repo` / `collect_ids` / `resolve_*` /\n    `format_*` helpers stay).\n  - `chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`: flatten the relocated\n    struct; each gains the `//!` module docstring it lacked;\n    bodies otherwise unchanged.\n  - `main.rs`: `suppress_banner` reads `a.common.no_label` for\n    all four (back to pre-cycle).\n- **0.49.0-1.2** — the ARCHITECTURE.md slim + chores-10 reorg\n  (own section below); slotted here because ARCHITECTURE.md had\n  collected this cycle's transient detail.\n\nAn earlier `0.49.0-1.1` decomposed `CommonArgs` into per-flag\nleaves; backed out on review, amended in place to the relocation\nabove — see `### Why not decompose into leaves`.\n\n### Why not decompose into leaves\n\nThe first take decomposed `CommonArgs` into per-flag\n`options_flags/` leaves (`revision` / `commit_limit` /\n`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring\n`init` + `provision_bundle`. Backed out:\n\n- **No reuse.** `init`'s leaves are reused (`--dry-run` →\n  `clone`, etc.) — a per-flag leaf is the unit of sharing. The\n  four here share the *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit`\n  / `label` / etc. is reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves buy\n  nothing the shared struct doesn't already give.\n- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two single-field-`value` leaves\n  ([README](../src/options_flags/README.md)) collide on the clap\n  arg *id* (derived from the field name) when co-flattened —\n  `clap_builder` panics. The fix (`#[arg(id = …)]` on each) is\n  the \"not obvious when `id` vs `value`\" sharp edge —\n  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be.\n\nRule of thumb:\n\n- Leaf — when *that flag / small group* is genuinely shared at\n  that granularity (`--dry-run`, `--squash`).\n- Inline-fields bundle — when a *whole arg set* is shared by N\n  commands but its parts aren't reused.\n- Extract a leaf later, when a second consumer is real:\n  `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s the extracted type\n  (one definition, no duplication)."

146	
147	### Why not decompose into leaves
148	
149	The first take decomposed `CommonArgs` into per-flag
150	`options_flags/` leaves (`revision` / `commit_limit` /
151	`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring
152	`init` + `provision_bundle`. Backed out:
153	
154	- **No reuse.** `init`'s leaves are reused (`--dry-run` →
155	  `clone`, etc.) — a per-flag leaf is the unit of sharing. The
156	  four here share the *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit`
157	  / `label` / etc. is reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves buy
158	  nothing the shared struct doesn't already give.
159	- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two single-field-`value` leaves
160	  ([README](../src/options_flags/README.md)) collide on the clap
161	  arg *id* (derived from the field name) when co-flattened —
162	  `clap_builder` panics. The fix (`#[arg(id = …)]` on each) is
163	  the "not obvious when `id` vs `value`" sharp edge —
164	  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be.
165	
166	Rule of thumb:
167	
168	- Leaf — when *that flag / small group* is genuinely shared at
169	  that granularity (`--dry-run`, `--squash`).
170	- Inline-fields bundle — when a *whole arg set* is shared by N
171	  commands but its parts aren't reused.
172	- Extract a leaf later, when a second consumer is real:
173	  `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s the extracted type
174	  (one definition, no duplication).
175

/// Named stages of the `push` state machine.
///
/// Used by `--from <stage>` to resume at a specific point and by
/// `--status` to report the current position. Ordered top-down so
/// `Stage as u8` comparisons reflect progress through the flow.
#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
#[value(rename_all = "kebab-case")]
pub enum Stage {
    /// Run fmt / clippy / test / install / retest.
    Preflight,
    /// Present diff for the first approval gate.
    Review,
    /// Compose / edit the commit message; present for second gate.
    Message,
    /// Commit the app repo.
    CommitApp,
    /// Commit the `.claude` session repo (skipped if empty).
    CommitClaude,
    /// Advance both bookmarks to `@-`.
    BookmarkBoth,
    /// `jj git push --bookmark <b> -R .`.
    PushApp,
    /// `vc-x1 finalize --repo .claude --squash --push <b> ...`.
    FinalizeClaude,
}

impl Stage {
    /// Return the stage's kebab-case string identifier (matches what
    /// the CLI accepts via `--from <stage>` and what `PushState`
    /// persists to disk).
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Stage::Preflight => "preflight",
            Stage::Review => "review",
            Stage::Message => "message",
            Stage::CommitApp => "commit-app",
            Stage::CommitClaude => "commit-claude",
            Stage::BookmarkBoth => "bookmark-both",
            Stage::PushApp => "push-app",
            Stage::FinalizeClaude => "finalize-claude",
        }
    }

    /// Parse a kebab-case stage name back into a `Stage`.
    ///
    /// Unknown names return `None`; callers should surface a helpful
    /// error rather than silently substituting a default.
    pub fn from_str(name: &str) -> Option<Self> {
        match name {
            "preflight" => Some(Stage::Preflight),
            "review" => Some(Stage::Review),
            "message" => Some(Stage::Message),
            "commit-app" => Some(Stage::CommitApp),
            "commit-claude" => Some(Stage::CommitClaude),
            "bookmark-both" => Some(Stage::BookmarkBoth),
            "push-app" => Some(Stage::PushApp),
            "finalize-claude" => Some(Stage::FinalizeClaude),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    /// The stage that follows this one, or `None` when this is the
    /// last stage (`FinalizeClaude`).
    pub fn next(self) -> Option<Self> {
        match self {
            Stage::Preflight => Some(Stage::Review),
            Stage::Review => Some(Stage::Message),
            Stage::Message => Some(Stage::CommitApp),
            Stage::CommitApp => Some(Stage::CommitClaude),
            Stage::CommitClaude => Some(Stage::BookmarkBoth),
            Stage::BookmarkBoth => Some(Stage::PushApp),
            Stage::PushApp => Some(Stage::FinalizeClaude),
            Stage::FinalizeClaude => None,
        }
    }

    /// The first stage in the flow — used when no saved state exists.
    pub fn first() -> Self {
        Stage::Preflight
    }
}

/// Flag set mirrors the design in `notes/chores-05.md`. Flags are
/// parsed in 0.37.0-0; their real effects land across the remaining
/// 0.37.0-N steps. See the module docstring for which flags activate
/// when.
#[derive(Args, Debug)]
pub struct PushArgs {
    /// Bookmark to advance in both repos (positional form of `--bookmark`).
    ///
    /// Accepting a positional lets the common case read as `vc-x1 push main`

> DEVELOPER

In notes/README.md mentions "Migration A / B", you surfaced that recently
and how is that different from "steps", "sub-steps"?

> AGENT

Different axes — one is *what work*, the other is *how a cycle is chopped up*.

**Migration A / Migration B — a named, long-running refactor program.** Each is a theme spanning many version cycles and many subcommands:
- **Migration A** — port every subcommand from `fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to `fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, with clap kept at the binary edge via `From`/`TryFrom<&XxxArgs>`.
- **Migration B** — pull per-subcommand inline `#[arg]` fields into shared `src/options_flags/` leaves/bundles.

They carry no version number of their own; each is "done" when the last subcommand is converted. Progress is a checklist *over the codebase surface* — which subcommands are ported — which is exactly what the `chores-10.md` "live tracking" tables hold. (`init/finalize/symlink/clone/sync/validate-desc/fix-desc/push` already did Migration A in earlier cycles; `chid/desc/list/show` are the last four. That's why these terms aren't new — they were in `ARCHITECTURE.md`; I just moved the *status* out of there this session, since per-subcommand progress is transient tracking, not architecture.)

**Steps / sub-steps — the version-suffix workflow for one cycle.** Pure process machinery from `CLAUDE.md`:
- **step** = an `X.Y.Z-N` commit in a multi-step cycle (`X.Y.Z-0` … `X.Y.Z`), each with its own commit + push + finalize.
- **sub-step** = `X.Y.Z-N.M`, a finer split inside one step (sub-sub-step `X.Y.Z-N.M-K`).

Progress here is a checklist *over this cycle's commits* — the `todo.md > ## In Progress` ladder with `(done)`/`(current)` markers.

**How they relate:** a step/sub-step is a *unit of delivery*; it may or may not advance a migration, and most cycles touch neither A nor B. The `0.49.0` cycle happens to advance both — `0.49.0-1.x` does Migration B for the four subcommands, `0.49.0-3..-6` does Migration A for them — but that's this cycle's *content*, not a property of the workflow. Migration A could've been done one subcommand per release, or all in one giant cycle; the step ladder would look completely different while "Migration A" stayed the same thing.

Rough analogy: Migration A/B ≈ an epic; steps/sub-steps ≈ the commits that chip away at it (plus all the commits that have nothing to do with it). And they live in different files for that reason — the migration is "what + why" (chores / formerly ARCHITECTURE), the step ladder is "how it's sliced this time" (CLAUDE.md + todo.md's In Progress).

Want me to add a short version of this distinction to `chores-10.md`'s tracking section (or `notes/README.md`)? Otherwise I'll go back to waiting on your call for the steps 1–6 close-out.

> DEVELOPER

Hmm, I don't like migration for some reason, how about "task" or "task set" or suggest other synonyms

> AGENT

"Migration" carries data/schema/framework-migration baggage that doesn't fit — these are uniform *internal-API refactors* applied across every subcommand, not a move between platforms. I lean toward keeping the one-letter handle (it's a genuinely useful short token in cross-refs — "see X A status") but swapping the noun. Candidates I'd weigh:

- **Refactor** — *literally* what each is; plain word; smallest swap. "Refactor A — args → Context+Params" / "Refactor B — flags → options_flags".
- **No category word at all** — just name them by target: "the Context+Params refactor" / "the options_flags extraction". Most self-documenting; loses the `A`/`B` shorthand.
- **Workstream / Track** — conveys "long-running parallel line of work"; reads a bit corporate.
- **Task set** (your suggestion) — fine, but "task" overlaps with todo-list items *and* the `Task` tool in this environment, so it's slightly ambiguous in context.
- Also-rans: *campaign* (nice "sustained effort" vibe, informal), *pass* ("the Context+Params pass", like a compiler pass), *overhaul*, *conversion*/*transition* (same migration-ish vibe, doesn't fix it), *sweep* (good fit — but already taken by "the CommonArgs sweep" for the *cycle*, so it'd collide).

Scope if we rename: `chores-10.md` (the `## … live tracking` heading + the two table sub-headings + the `### Cycle re-scope` body), `ARCHITECTURE.md` (`## Migration A` / `## Migration B` section headings + their anchors), `notes/README.md` and `notes/todo.md` (the cross-ref links/anchors), and the two unpushed commit bodies (`-1.1` already needs a re-describe, so that's nearly free). None of those headings is a commit-recording one, so it's a mechanical find-replace + anchor fixup — fits into the `0.49.0-1.2` close-out.

47	subcommands; `XxxParams` carry the per-subcommand inputs.
48	
49	Rules for the subcommand layer (some still aspirational — see
50	[Migration A](#migration-a--args--context--params)):
51	
52	1. Plain options, flat fields, `Default` — no clap types in
53	   `XxxParams`. Domain types (`RepoSelector`, `Scope`) are
54	   fine; leaf wrappers (`RepoOption`) are not.
55	2. Typed errors (`enum XError`, not `Box<dyn Error>`) — a TUI
56	   matches variants to pick dialogs; CLI formats them.
57	3. Returned outcomes, not `println!` — each subcommand returns
58	   a structured result; CLI formats it, a library writes
59	   nothing to stdout itself.
60	4. Progress via an optional `&mut dyn ProgressSink` on
61	   long-running subcommands — CLI installs a stderr sink, tests
62	   a recording sink.
63	5. No globals, no implicit cwd/env reads in subcommands — CLI
64	   resolves cwd/env once at startup and builds `Context`.
65	
66	None of this is sacred — the whole structure is an experiment.
67	The current scope is deliberately narrow: a small `Context`
68	(two params, not one god blob); no trait-based DI yet; one
69	crate, not a workspace split; `src/options_flags/` leaves left
70	in place — only their consumers change shape. Widen any of it
71	when the evidence (a second front-end, a second consumer crate,
72	a real platform-surface divergence) calls for it — not before.
73	
74	### Naming
75	
76	Earlier drafts of this design used `Workspace` / `XOptions`;
77	the implementation (0.44.0) chose `Context` / `XxxParams`:
78	
79	- `Workspace` → `Context` — Cargo owns "workspace" formally,
80	  and this codebase already uses "workspace" for the dual-repo
81	  project root (`find_workspace_root`).
82	- `XOptions` → `XxxParams` — avoids visual collision with
83	  `Option<T>` (a params struct mixes required and
84	  `Option<T>`-typed fields) and with `src/options_flags/`.
85	
86	## Module map
87	
88	The *kinds* of module and what they're for — not an exhaustive
89	catalog (read the `//!` docstrings; `notes/chores-*.md` for
90	migration status):
91	
92	**CLI layer:**
93	
94	- `src/main.rs` — the clap edge: `Cli` (`Parser`), `Commands`
95	  (`Subcommand`) + the dispatch arms, `cli_with_banner()` (the
96	  per-subcommand `vc-x1 X.Y.Z` banner), `CompleteEnv` wiring,
97	  and `bm_track` (the permanent `main`-bookmark tracking
98	  diagnostic on every command's entry/exit).
99	- `src/options_flags/` — reusable `#[derive(Args)]` *leaves*
```

141	
142	## Subcommand model
143	
144	Adding a subcommand `x`:
145	
146	1. Create `src/x.rs` with `pub struct XxxArgs`
147	   (`#[derive(Args)]`), composing leaves from
148	   `src/options_flags/` where one exists.
149	2. Add a variant `X(x::XxxArgs)` to `Commands` in `src/main.rs`
150	   with a `///` summary (and `#[command(long_about = …)]` for
151	   the long form).
152	3. Add a dispatch arm in `main()` calling `x::x(&args)` (or,
153	   once ported, `x::x(&ctx, &params)`).
154	4. Doc comments on `#[arg(...)]` fields drive `--help`; add
155	   `#[arg(verbatim_doc_comment, …)]` on any field whose doc
156	   comment uses bullets (clap otherwise reflows them into
157	   prose).
158	5. Dynamic value completion (`--account=<TAB>`) is an
159	   `ArgValueCompleter` attached to the leaf in
160	   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
161	   and stays at this layer.
162	
163	## Migration A — args → Context + Params
164	
165	The ongoing port of each subcommand's
166	`pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to
167	`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, adding an
168	`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the
169	conversion is fallible) at the binary edge. `init` (0.44.0) is
170	the worked example. Out of scope for the ports until a real
171	consumer surfaces: typed errors,
172	returned-outcomes-vs-`println!`, `ProgressSink`, `Context`
173	fields beyond `UserConfig` + `--log`. Per-subcommand status:
174	`notes/chores-*.md` (the "Migration A / Migration B — live
175	tracking" section).
176	
177	## Migration B — per-subcommand flags → `src/options_flags/`
178	
179	Independently of Migration A, per-subcommand inline `#[arg]`
180	fields are being lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under
181	`src/options_flags/` so a flag is defined (parser, help,
182	completer) exactly once. See
183	[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
184	for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
185	Flag-vs-Option classification; `notes/chores-*.md` for

145	### Why not decompose into leaves
146	
147	The first take decomposed `CommonArgs` into per-flag
148	`options_flags/` leaves (`revision` / `commit_limit` /
149	`repo_label`) flattened into a `common_bundle` — mirroring
150	`init` + `provision_bundle`. Backed out:
151	
152	- **No reuse.** `init`'s leaves are reused (`--dry-run` →
153	  `clone`, etc.) — a per-flag leaf is the unit of sharing. The
154	  four here share the *whole set*; none of `revision` / `limit`
155	  / `label` / etc. is reused elsewhere, so per-flag leaves buy
156	  nothing the shared struct doesn't already give.
157	- **`value`/`id` friction.** Two single-field-`value` leaves
158	  ([README](../src/options_flags/README.md)) collide on the clap
159	  arg *id* (derived from the field name) when co-flattened —
160	  `clap_builder` panics. The fix (`#[arg(id = …)]` on each) is
161	  the "not obvious when `id` vs `value`" sharp edge —
162	  self-inflicted by decomposing leaves that didn't need to be.
163	
164	Rule of thumb:
165	
166	- Leaf — when *that flag / small group* is genuinely shared at
167	  that granularity (`--dry-run`, `--squash`).
168	- Inline-fields bundle — when a *whole arg set* is shared by N
169	  commands but its parts aren't reused.
170	- Extract a leaf later, when a second consumer is real:
171	  `CommonArgs` then `#[command(flatten)]`s the extracted type
172	  (one definition, no duplication).

---
   `src/options_flags/` — completion is a clap-aware concern
   and stays at this layer.

## args → Context + Params

The ongoing port — "the Context+Params port" — of each
subcommand's `pub fn x(args: &XxxArgs)` to
`pub fn x(ctx: &Context, params: &XxxParams)`, adding an
`XxxParams` flat struct + a `From` (or `TryFrom`, if the
conversion is fallible) at the binary edge. `init` (0.44.0) is
the worked example. Out of scope for the ports until a real
consumer surfaces: typed errors,
returned-outcomes-vs-`println!`, `ProgressSink`, `Context`
fields beyond `UserConfig` + `--log`. Per-subcommand status:
`notes/chores-*.md` (the "Refactor tracking" section).

## per-subcommand flags → `src/options_flags/`

Independently of the Context+Params port — "the options_flags
extraction" — per-subcommand inline `#[arg]` fields are being
lifted into reusable leaves/bundles under `src/options_flags/`
so a flag is defined (parser, help, completer) exactly once. See
[`src/options_flags/README.md`](src/options_flags/README.md)
for the leaf / bundle / Pattern-A mechanics and the
Flag-vs-Option classification; `notes/chores-*.md` for
per-subcommand status.

## See also

- [`README.md`](README.md) — user-facing overview and
  per-subcommand usage.
```

Update the change description or other metadata [default alias: desc]

Starts an editor to let you edit the description of changes. The editor will be $EDITOR, or `nano`
if that's not defined (`Notepad` on Windows).

Usage: jj describe [OPTIONS] [REVSETS]...

Arguments:
  [REVSETS]...
          The revision(s) whose description to edit (default: @) [aliases: -r]

Options:
  -m, --message <MESSAGE>
          The change description to use (don't open editor)
          
          If multiple revisions are specified, the same description will be used for all of them.

      --stdin
          Read the change description from stdin
          
          If multiple revisions are specified, the same description will be used for all of them.

      --editor
          Open an editor to edit the change description
          
          Forces an editor to open when using `--stdin` or `--message` to allow the message to be
          edited afterwards.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Global Options:
  -R, --repository <REPOSITORY>
          Path to repository to operate on
          
          By default, Jujutsu searches for the closest .jj/ directory in an ancestor of the current
          working directory.

      --ignore-working-copy
          Don't snapshot the working copy, and don't update it
          
          By default, Jujutsu snapshots the working copy at the beginning of every command. The
          working copy is also updated at the end of the command, if the command modified the
          working-copy commit (`@`). If you want to avoid snapshotting the working copy and instead
          see a possibly stale working-copy commit, you can use `--ignore-working-copy`. This may be
          useful e.g. in a command prompt, especially if you have another process that commits the
          working copy.
          
          Loading the repository at a specific operation with `--at-operation` implies
          `--ignore-working-copy`.

      --ignore-immutable
          Allow rewriting immutable commits
          
          By default, Jujutsu prevents rewriting commits in the configured set of immutable commits.
          This option disables that check and lets you rewrite any commit but the root commit.
          
          This option only affects the check. It does not affect the `immutable_heads()` revset or
          the `immutable` template keyword.

The "chid/desc/list/show — CommonArgs sweep" In-Progress task absorbs **two** `## Todo` items, neither of which got removed when the task went In Progress:

- **Item #1** — "Subcommand layer / CLI decoupling — remaining subcommands." Its "done" half (the Context+Params port of `symlink`/`clone`/`sync`/`validate-desc`/`fix-desc`/`push`) is already recorded in `## Done` (the `0.48.0` line); its "remaining" half (`chid`/`desc`/`list`/`show`) *is* the In-Progress task's `0.49.0-3..-6`. Nothing of it is "to do" anymore → **delete**.
- **The "CommonArgs sweep — add `--scope=…` to chid/desc/list/show" item** (≈ #16 by display number, line 139) — that's verbatim the `0.49.0-2` step ("Drops the existing `-R`/`--repo` repeatable flag in favor of the new path form"). → **delete**.

(I checked the rest: item #2 — "single-field `options_flags` leaves → `value` field" — is about `init`'s `scope`/`repo`/`dry_run`/… *leaves*, not `chid`+co's inline-fields `CommonArgs`; the other `--scope` items are `finalize`/`push`/`clone`/`validate-desc` — all separate. So just those two are stale.)

**Process fix** — the gap: when a `## Todo` item is picked up (or an existing `## In Progress` ladder is re-scoped to absorb it), the `## Todo` entry must be deleted in the same commit. Proposed CLAUDE.md addition (in `### Versioning`, near "Every plan must start with a version bump"):

> When a `## Todo` item is picked up — its `## In Progress` ladder created, or an existing In-Progress ladder *re-scoped* to absorb it — **delete that `## Todo` entry in the same commit**. The `## In Progress` block is the sole record of that work until close-out, when it moves to `## Done`. A cycle that merges several `## Todo` items (entangled work) deletes all of them. A `## Todo` entry that duplicates current `## In Progress` work is a process bug.

…plus a catch-it line in the pre-commit checklist (item 6/7 area): "confirm no `## Todo` item duplicates the current `## In Progress` work."

**How it lands** — I'd make `0.49.0-2` multi-step: `0.49.0-2.1` = the cycle-start marker (backfill `-1.1`/`-1.2` `Commits:` refs `[[2]]`/`[[3]]`, bump `Cargo.toml`, delete the two stale `## Todo` items, add the CLAUDE.md process rule + checklist line, add the `chores-10.md` `0.49.0-2` section + ladder), then `0.49.0-2.2` = the `-R`/`--repo` → `-s`/`--scope` rollout itself (incl. updating CLAUDE.md's `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` → `-s code,bot -L`). Close-out `0.49.0-2` (squash-or-keep decided then). Single-step is also fine if you'd rather one commit — I lean multi-step here since the process/docs change is genuinely separate from the `--scope` code.

Sound right? If so I'll start `0.49.0-2.1`.

201	  sub-step (or sub-sub-step) ladder, the per-step checkpoints
202	  defer to the commit-first review model — see
203	  [Sub-step Workflow > Commit-first review model](#commit-first-review-model).
204	  Sub-step commits land as the bot finishes them; user reviews
205	  the committed revision in their editor. The cycle-level
206	  push at close-out keeps the two-gate ceremony.
207	
208	### Notes references
209	
210	Reference *citations* are double-bracketed so the brackets render
211	— `[[N]]`, or `[[2]],[[3]]` for several (comma-separated, not
212	`[2,3]` or `[[2]][[3]]`). The `[N]:` definitions in a file's
213	`# References` section and inline `[text](url)` / `[text](#anchor)`
214	links stay single-bracketed. See
215	[Todo format](notes/README.md#todo-format) for details.
216	
217	### Markdown anchor links
218	
219	GitHub anchor algorithm: lowercase, strip non-alphanumeric
220	characters in place, map remaining spaces to hyphens 1-for-1. Do
221	**not** collapse adjacent whitespace — so `a + b` → `a--b` (spaces
222	on both sides of `+`), but `a: b` → `a-b` (only trailing space on
223	`:`). General markdown reference:
224	[markdownguide.org](https://www.markdownguide.org). GitHub
225	publishes no official spec for auto-generated anchors; the
226	de-facto reference implementation is
227	[github-slugger](https://github.com/Flet/github-slugger).
228	
229	### Versioning
230	
231	Every plan must start with a version bump. Choose the approach based
232	on scope:
233	
234	- **Single-step** (recommended for mechanical/focused changes): bump
235	  directly to `X.Y.Z`, implement in one commit. Simpler history.
236	- **Multi-step** (for exploratory/large changes): bump to `X.Y.Z-0`,
237	  implement across multiple commits incrementing the numeric
238	  suffix. The final commit drops the suffix.
239	
240	The plan should recommend one approach and get user approval before
241	starting.
242	
243	For multi-step:
244	
245	1. Bump version to `X.Y.Z-0` with the plan and commit as a chore
246	   marker.
247	2. Implement in one or more `X.Y.Z-N` commits (increment N as
248	   needed).
249	3. Final commit bumps to `X.Y.Z` (no suffix), updates
250	   `notes/todo.md` and `notes/chores-*.md` — this is the "done"
251	   marker.
252	
253	Multi-step cycles surface the ladder at the top of
254	`notes/todo.md > ## In Progress` as a bullet list with `(done)` /
255	`(current)` markers — see the file's intro paragraph for the
256	format. When starting a new step, the *first* edit is to mark
257	that step `(current)` in `notes/todo.md` — before any code/doc
258	work — so the In Progress view reflects what's actually
259	happening. The flip back to `(done)` is part of the pre-commit
260	checklist (item 6).
261	
262	**Why numeric suffixes (`-0`, `-1`, …) rather than `-devN`:**
263	semver pre-release identifiers may consist of a single numeric
264	component, and they compare numerically per spec. So
265	`X.Y.Z-1 < X.Y.Z-2 < … < X.Y.Z` correctly orders the dev ladder
266	below the done marker. Cargo accepts this form. The `-dev` prefix
267	adds no information the git log doesn't already convey and
268	doubles typing per commit.
269	
270	The final release commit (no suffix) signals completion rather than
271	amending prior commits. This keeps history readable and makes it easy
272	to see which commits were exploratory vs final.
273	
274	For decomposition finer than `X.Y.Z-N` — sub-steps (`X.Y.Z-N.M`)
275	or sub-sub-steps (`X.Y.Z-N.M-K`) — see
276	[Sub-step Workflow](#sub-step-workflow). The cycle close-out
277	choice (squash to one commit vs land each sub-step separately)
278	is made at close-out, not cycle start.
279	
280	See also [`notes/substep-protocol.md`](notes/substep-protocol.md)
281	for the full protocol — when to use, per-substep contract
282	(`cargo test --bins` is non-negotiable), navigation, the validated
283	close-out squash recipe, and recovery. Revset primitives the
284	protocol relies on (`@`, `@-`, `..`, `::`, prefix matching) live in
285	[`notes/jj-revsets.md`](notes/jj-revsets.md).
286	
287	### Headings and entries that record a commit
288	
289	A `chores-NN.md` `##` section header that records a specific
290	commit, the matching `todo.md > ## Done` entry, and any `[N]`
291	reference to that section all use **exactly that commit's
292	title** — `<type>: <desc> (<version>)`, the same string the
293	commit gets (see [Commit Message Style](#commit-message-style)).
294	E.g. the chores header `## refactor: port push to Context
295	(0.48.0-6)` and the Done line `- refactor: port push to Context
296	(0.48.0-6) [[3]]`. For a multi-step cycle the `## Done` entry
297	uses the close-out commit's title.
298	
299	This does **not** apply to organizational headings (`## Todo`,
300	`## In Progress`, `# References`) or to design `###` subsections
301	inside a chores section — those are named for whatever fits.
302	Among the commit-recording ones, exact match is the strong
303	default (nothing absolute): a near-miss just makes it harder to
304	line a record up with its commit.
305	
306	A commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in
307	progress; the *last* edit before `vc-x1 push` syncs it — and the
308	`## Done` entry / `[N]` anchor for that commit — to the final
309	commit title. See [Markdown anchor links](#markdown-anchor-links)
310	for the slug algorithm; the pre-commit checklist catches a
311	dangling `#anchor`, and a future `vc-x1 validate-repo` should too
312	(and should verify the recorded title matches the commit).
313	
314	Existing sections and `## Done` entries (most of chores-01..09;
315	the pre-`0.48.1` `## Done` lines) predate this and keep their
316	free-form text; the convention applies going forward — `0.48.2`
317	converts the `0.48.1` section + its Done entry as the worked
318	example.
319

422	## Sub-step Workflow
423	
424	Larger work decomposes into named depths. The version-suffix
425	scheme nests:
426

434	
435	The conventions below apply at **whichever leaf depth the
436	current cycle planned to** — sub-step, sub-sub-step, etc.
437	"Sub-step" reads as shorthand for that leaf level throughout
438	this section.

So is "single-field option_flags ..." related to this change or old change or ...?

> AGENT

It's an **old, still-open** item — unrelated to `0.49.0-2` (or any of the `0.49.0` work).

What it is: `0.47.0` introduced the "name a single-field leaf's field `value`, declare the flag with `#[arg(long = "…")]`" convention on the *new* `squash` leaf, so consumers read `args.squash.value` instead of the doubled `args.squash.squash`. The todo item is the *retrofit* — sweep the **pre-existing** single-field leaves to match: `options_flags/{scope, repo, dry_run, private, account, config, use_template}.rs` + their consumers (mostly `init.rs`, tests). Candidate since `0.47.1`; never picked up.

Why it doesn't overlap with `0.49.0-2`:
- `0.49.0-2` touches `options_flags/common_args.rs`'s `CommonArgs` — an **inline-fields bundle** (no per-flag leaves at all), and `src/scope.rs`'s `Scope` enum (`Roles`/`Single`). It swaps `CommonArgs`'s inline `repos`/`-R`/`--repo` field for an inline `scope`/`-s`/`--scope` field.
- The `value`-field item is about the *leaf* structs in `src/options_flags/` — different files, different consumers. Note the name clashes are coincidental: the item's `scope` leaf is `options_flags/scope.rs`'s `ScopeKind` (`code,bot|por`, used by `init`), **not** `src/scope.rs::Scope`; and the item's `repo` leaf is `options_flags/repo.rs` (used by `init`), **not** `CommonArgs`'s `-R`/`--repo` (which `0.49.0-2` removes — that's an inline field, not the leaf).

Tangential connection only: both live under `src/options_flags/`, and the `0.49.0-1.1` rationale (`### Why not decompose into leaves`) plus `options_flags/README.md` both mention the `value`/`id` convention — which is *why* `CommonArgs` was kept as inline-fields rather than decomposed into `value`-field leaves. But no shared code.

So it stays in `## Todo` as-is. The only tidy I'd consider (optional, not urgent): a half-line in the item clarifying that its `scope`/`repo` mean `init`'s leaves, distinct from `src/scope.rs::Scope` and `CommonArgs`'s `-R` — to head off exactly the confusion you just hit. Want me to add that while I'm in `notes/todo.md` for `0.49.0-2.1`, or leave it?

     1	//! Which side(s) of a workspace a command should operate on.
     2	//!
     3	//! - `Side` is the clap `ValueEnum` — one of `code`, `bot`.
     4	//! - `Scope` is an enum:
     5	//!   - `Roles(Vec<Side>)` — dual-repo workspace; the parsed
     6	//!     keyword form (`code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`).
     7	//!   - `Single(PathBuf)` — explicit single-repo mode; ignores
     8	//!     `.vc-config.toml` and operates on the one repo at the
     9	//!     given path. Wired up incrementally (parser lands in
    10	//!     0.42.0-2, consumers in later steps).
    11	//! - Helpers (`has_code`, `is_both`, etc.) reflect the `Roles`
    12	//!   arm only; on `Single(_)` they all return `false`. Callers
    13	//!   that must distinguish modes match on the enum directly.
    14	//! - See `notes/chores-07.md > --scope enum refactor (0.42.0)`
    15	//!   for the migration plan, and `notes/chores-06.md > 0.41.0-4`
    16	//!   for the vocabulary capture.
    17	
    18	use clap::ValueEnum;
    19	use std::fmt;
    20	use std::path::PathBuf;
    21	
    22	/// One side of a dual-repo workspace.
    23	///
    24	/// - `Code` — the primary (app) repo.
    25	/// - `Bot` — the Claude Code session repo (typically at `.claude/`).
    26	#[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, ValueEnum)]
    27	pub enum Side {
    28	    Code,
    29	    Bot,
    30	}
    31	
    32	/// Parsed `--scope` value.
    33	///
    34	/// - `Roles(_)` — dual-repo workspace; the requested side set.
    35	/// - `Single(_)` — explicit single-repo mode at the given path.
    36	#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
    37	pub enum Scope {
    38	    Roles(Vec<Side>),
    39	    #[allow(dead_code)]
    40	    Single(PathBuf),
    41	}
    42	
    43	/// Parse a `--scope` value string.
    44	///
    45	/// Accepted forms:
    46	///
    47	/// - Keyword: exactly one of `code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`
    48	///   → `Scope::Roles(...)`. Order is preserved.
    49	/// - Path: starts with `./`, `../`, `/`, `~/`, or is the bare `~`
    50	///   → `Scope::Single(PathBuf)`. The raw string is stored; tilde
    51	///   and `$VAR` expansion happens at the consumer (see
    52	///   `init::expand_vars`).
    53	///
    54	/// Anything else — including a bare unprefixed name like `foo`, an
    55	/// empty string, or an unrecognized keyword combination — is an
    56	/// error. The error message hints at the path-prefix requirement
    57	/// so users see the disambiguation rule when they mistype.
    58	#[allow(dead_code)]
    59	pub fn parse_scope(s: &str) -> Result<Scope, String> {
    60	    if s == "~"
    61	        || s.starts_with("./")
    62	        || s.starts_with("../")
    63	        || s.starts_with('/')
    64	        || s.starts_with("~/")
    65	    {
    66	        return Ok(Scope::Single(PathBuf::from(s)));
    67	    }
    68	    match s {
    69	        "code" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code])),
    70	        "bot" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Bot])),
    71	        "code,bot" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot])),
    72	        "bot,code" => Ok(Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Bot, Side::Code])),
    73	        "" => Err("--scope: value is empty".into()),
    74	        other => Err(format!(
    75	            "--scope: '{other}' is not a recognized form. \
    76	             Expected one of `code`, `bot`, `code,bot`, `bot,code`, \
    77	             or a path (`./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`). \
    78	             Bare names without `./` are reserved for keywords; \
    79	             prefix paths with `./` to disambiguate."
    80	        )),
    81	    }
    82	}
    83	
    84	impl Scope {
    85	    /// True when the `Roles` arm includes the code side.
    86	    pub fn has_code(&self) -> bool {
    87	        matches!(self, Scope::Roles(v) if v.contains(&Side::Code))
    88	    }
    89	
    90	    /// True when the `Roles` arm includes the bot side.
    91	    pub fn has_bot(&self) -> bool {
    92	        matches!(self, Scope::Roles(v) if v.contains(&Side::Bot))
    93	    }
    94	
    95	    /// Roles-only with exactly the code side — single-side dual-repo op.
    96	    pub fn is_code_only(&self) -> bool {
    97	        self.has_code() && !self.has_bot()
    98	    }
    99	
   100	    /// Roles-only with exactly the bot side — single-side dual-repo op.
   101	    #[allow(dead_code)]
   102	    pub fn is_bot_only(&self) -> bool {
   103	        !self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
   104	    }
   105	
   106	    /// Roles arm including both sides — full dual-repo op.
   107	    pub fn is_both(&self) -> bool {
   108	        self.has_code() && self.has_bot()
   109	    }
   110	}
   111	
   112	/// Render a `Scope` as the canonical string form `parse_scope` accepts.
   113	///
   114	/// - `Roles(_)` → `code` / `bot` / `code,bot` / `bot,code` (preserves
   115	///   original side ordering).
   116	/// - `Single(p)` → the path's lossy display form. The stored path
   117	///   already carries a parser-recognized prefix (the parser is the
   118	///   only constructor of `Single`), so the round-trip through
   119	///   `parse_scope` is well-defined.
   120	impl fmt::Display for Scope {
   121	    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
   122	        match self {
   123	            Scope::Roles(sides) => {
   124	                let parts: Vec<&'static str> = sides
   125	                    .iter()
   126	                    .map(|s| match s {
   127	                        Side::Code => "code",
   128	                        Side::Bot => "bot",
   129	                    })
   130	                    .collect();
   131	                f.write_str(&parts.join(","))
   132	            }
   133	            Scope::Single(p) => write!(f, "{}", p.display()),
   134	        }
   135	    }
   136	}

     1	//! `CommonArgs` — the shared arg set for the read-only commit-query
     2	//! subcommands (`chid` / `desc` / `list` / `show`): a `REVISION` /
     3	//! `COMMITS` positional pair, `-r`/`--revision`, `-R`/`--repo`,
     4	//! `-n`/`--commits`, and the `-l`/`-L` inter-repo label pair.
     5	//!
     6	//! A "bundle" in the inline-fields sense (cf. `provision_bundle`'s
     7	//! flatten-of-leaves form): the fields aren't extracted into per-flag
     8	//! leaves because none of them is reused outside these four — if one
     9	//! ever is (e.g. a future command wants just `--revision`), extract
    10	//! that field into a leaf and `#[command(flatten)]` it here. Consumers
    11	//! flatten this and add their own extra `#[arg]` fields (`list`'s
    12	//! `-w`/`--width`, `show`'s `-f`/`--files`). See
    13	//! [options_flags](README.md) for shared architecture.
    14	
    15	use std::path::PathBuf;
    16	
    17	use clap::Args;
    18	
    19	/// Shared CLI args for the read-only commit-query subcommands —
    20	/// see [Bundle](README.md#architecture).
    21	///
    22	/// - `pos_rev` / `pos_count` — the `REVISION` / `COMMITS` positionals
    23	///   (`common::resolve_spec` reconciles them with `-r` / `-n`).
    24	/// - `revision` — `-r` / `--revision` (default `@`); `..` notation is
    25	///   parsed downstream by `common::parse_dot_rev`.
    26	/// - `repos` — `-R` / `--repo`, repeatable / comma-separated repo
    27	///   paths (the `.` default is applied in `common::for_each_repo`).
    28	/// - `limit` — `-n` / `--commits`, caps the output.
    29	/// - `label` / `no_label` — `-l` / `--label` (default `===`) and
    30	///   `-L` / `--no-label`; `common::resolve_header` combines them.
    31	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
    32	pub struct CommonArgs {
    33	    /// Revision (with optional .. notation)
    34	    #[arg(value_name = "REVISION")]
    35	    pub pos_rev: Option<String>,
    36	
    37	    /// Number of commits to show (per dotted side)
    38	    #[arg(value_name = "COMMITS")]
    39	    pub pos_count: Option<usize>,
    40	
    41	    /// Revision to query
    42	    #[arg(short, long, default_value = "@")]
    43	    pub revision: String,
    44	
    45	    /// Path to jj repo; repeatable or comma-separated [default: .]
    46	    #[arg(short = 'R', long = "repo", value_name = "PATH")]
    47	    pub repos: Vec<PathBuf>,
    48	
    49	    /// Number of commits to show
    50	    #[arg(short = 'n', long = "commits", value_name = "COMMITS")]
    51	    pub limit: Option<usize>,
    52	
    53	    /// Custom label decoration between repos
    54	    #[arg(
    55	        short = 'l',
    56	        long = "label",
    57	        value_name = "TEXT",
    58	        allow_hyphen_values = true,
    59	        default_value = "==="
    60	    )]
    61	    pub label: String,
    62	
    63	    /// Suppress label between repos
    64	    #[arg(short = 'L', long = "no-label")]
    65	    pub no_label: bool,
    66	}
    67	
    68	impl super::OptionFlagBundle for CommonArgs {}

/// Expand comma-separated repo paths, default to `["."]`, and run a closure for each.
///
/// Header style controls output between repos.
/// Continues past errors, printing them to stderr, and returns an error if any failed.
pub fn for_each_repo<F>(
    raw_repos: &[PathBuf],
    header: &Header,
    mut body: F,
) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>
where
    F: FnMut(&Workspace, &Arc<ReadonlyRepo>) -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>>,
{
    let repos: Vec<PathBuf> = if raw_repos.is_empty() {
        vec![PathBuf::from(".")]
    } else {
        raw_repos
            .iter()
            .flat_map(|p| {
                p.to_string_lossy()
                    .split(',')
                    .map(|s| PathBuf::from(s.trim()))
                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            })
            .collect()
    };
    let multi = repos.len() > 1;
    let mut first = true;
    let mut errors: Vec<String> = Vec::new();

    for repo_path in &repos {
        if multi {
            match header {
                Header::Label(deco) => {
                    if !first {
                        info!("");
                    }
                    info!(
                        "{}",
                        bold(&format!("{deco} {} {deco}", repo_path.display()))
                    );
                }
                Header::None => {}
            }
        }
        first = false;

        match load_repo(repo_path) {
            Ok((workspace, repo)) => {
                if let Err(e) = body(&workspace, &repo) {
                    error!("({}): {e}", repo_path.display());
                    errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
                }
            }
            Err(e) => {
                error!("({}): {e}", repo_path.display());
                errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
            }
        }
    }

    if errors.is_empty() {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(format!("{} repo(s) had errors", errors.len()).into())
    }
}

///
/// Reads `<workspace_root>/.vc-config.toml > [workspace] other-repo`:
///
/// - dual workspace (non-empty `other-repo`) → `Roles([Code, Bot])`
/// - single-repo workspace (missing / empty `other-repo`) → `Roles([Code])`
/// - POR (no workspace_root) → `Single(cwd)` — operate on cwd as a
///   one-off jj repo, ignoring any workspace context.
pub fn default_scope(workspace_root: Option<&Path>, cwd: &Path) -> Scope {
    let Some(root) = workspace_root else {
        return Scope::Single(cwd.to_path_buf());
    };
    let cfg = match toml_simple::toml_load(&root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE)) {
        Ok(c) => c,
        Err(_) => return Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code]),
    };
    match toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg, "workspace.other-repo") {
        Some(v) if !v.is_empty() => Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]),
        _ => Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code]),
    }
}

/// Resolve a `Scope` to concrete repo paths.
///
/// `Roles(...)` arm:
///
/// - `Side::Code` → `workspace_root` (or cwd's `.` when `workspace_root` is None).
/// - `Side::Bot` → `workspace_root.join(other-repo)`.
///
/// Errors when `Side::Bot` is requested but the workspace doesn't define
/// one (POR or single-repo workspace).
///
/// `Single(p)` arm: returns `vec![p]` directly — no workspace lookup,
/// no `other-repo` resolution. The path is whatever the caller stored
/// (typically the value the user passed to `--scope=<path>`, or cwd
/// from `default_scope`'s POR branch); shell-style expansion (tilde,
/// `$VAR`) happens at the parser/consumer boundary, not here.
pub fn scope_to_repos(
    scope: &Scope,
    workspace_root: Option<&Path>,
) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let sides = match scope {
        Scope::Roles(v) => v,
        Scope::Single(p) => return Ok(vec![p.clone()]),
    };
    let mut repos = Vec::new();
    for side in sides {
        match side {
            Side::Code => repos.push(
                workspace_root
                    .map(Path::to_path_buf)
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(".")),
            ),
            Side::Bot => {
                let root = workspace_root.ok_or(
                    "--scope=bot: not in a vc-x1 workspace (no .vc-config.toml with path = \"/\") — drop --scope or use --scope=code",
                )?;
                let cfg = toml_simple::toml_load(&root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE))?;
                let other = toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg, "workspace.other-repo")
                    .filter(|v| !v.is_empty())
                    .ok_or(
                        "--scope=bot: no other-repo configured. Add `other-repo = \"…\"` to .vc-config.toml to enable dual-repo operations",
                    )?;
                repos.push(root.join(other));
            }
        }
    }
    Ok(repos)
}

Ladder restructured (`-2.1` done, `-2.2` = the rollout code, `-2.3` = docs), `Cargo.toml` → `0.49.0-2.2`. Before I write the rollout there's a behavior question I want your call on.

**`0.49.0-2.2` plan:**
- `options_flags/common_args.rs`: `repos: Vec<PathBuf>` (`-R`/`--repo`) → `scope: Option<Scope>` (`-s`/`--scope`, `value_parser = parse_scope`, `value_name = "code|bot|code,bot|PATH"`); `None` = resolved from the workspace at use-time.
- `common.rs`: `for_each_repo` drops its comma-split + `["."]`-default block, just iterates the resolved `&[PathBuf]`; new `pub fn resolve_repos(scope: Option<&Scope>) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>>` = `find_workspace_root` + `scope.cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| default_scope(…))` + `scope_to_repos`.
- `src/scope.rs`: drop `#[allow(dead_code)]` on `parse_scope` and `Scope::Single` (now reachable).
- the four bodies: `let repos = common::resolve_repos(c.scope.as_ref())?;` → `common::for_each_repo(&repos, &hdr, …)`; `//!` doc-comments updated.
- tests in `chid/desc/list/show`: the `-R` parse tests → `-s` (`with_scope`, a `scope_code_bot` for `-s code,bot`, a `scope_path` for `-s ./x`); `defaults` asserts `scope == None`. Plus `common/tests.rs` coverage for `resolve_repos`.
- `CLAUDE.md`: `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` → `vc-x1 chid -s code,bot -L` (in `## ochid Trailers` + `### Run vc-x1 push`), since `-R` stops working at this commit. (`notes/README.md` + `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s `-R` mentions → `0.49.0-2.3`.)

**The behavior question:** with no `-s`, `resolve_repos(None)` → `default_scope()`, which for a **dual** workspace is `Roles([Code, Bot])` — so `vc-x1 chid` (and `desc`/`list`/`show`) with no flag would now query **both** repos, where today it queries just the current one (`-R` default `["."]`). For a single-repo project / POR it's unchanged (one repo). Is "default to both sides in a dual workspace" what you want for these four query commands, or should the default stay "just the current repo" (i.e. `resolve_repos(None)` → `Roles([Code])` / `Single(cwd)`, with `-s code,bot` for the both-sides view)?

Once you settle that I'll write `0.49.0-2.2` in `@` and ping you to review the diff.

So `CommonArgs` ends up with two fields, mutually exclusive (clap `conflicts_with`), and no-flag default = `default_scope()` (dual workspace → both, single-repo workspace → code, no workspace → cwd-as-POR). This is a real deviation from the chores plan ("`-R` dropped"); I'll update the `0.49.0-2.2`/`-2` ladder lines and record the deviation in the new chores-10 section.

One small clarification before I write it: should `--scope` accept *only* keywords (`code|bot|code,bot`), or also paths (`--scope=./foo`, redundant with `-R`)?

- **Keyword-only** — `--help` shows `-s code|bot|code,bot`, clean separation ("`-R` for path, `--scope` for roles"). `Scope::Single` stays as an internal-only variant (constructed by `default_scope`'s POR branch); `parse_scope`'s path branch becomes unused (drop it / keep it dead-code). I lean this way.
- **Both** — `--help` shows `-s code|bot|code,bot|PATH`, `parse_scope` stays as-is; harmless redundancy with `-R`.

Yes — that's the original chores plan and it's the cleanest. `--scope` accepts both keywords AND paths (the `./`/`../`/`/`/`~` prefix is the disambiguation rule, already enforced by `parse_scope`'s error: "Bare names without `./` are reserved for keywords; prefix paths with `./` to disambiguate."). One flag, one resolution path, `Scope::Single` is the parsed path form. Help: `--scope=code|bot|code,bot|PATH`. The trade-off is users learn the `./` rule once, which `parse_scope` already teaches via its error.

So the final design is what I had before the "keep -R" pivot:
- `CommonArgs.scope: Option<Scope>` (`-s`/`--scope`, `value_parser = parse_scope`); no `-R`/`--repo`.
- `common::resolve_repos(scope: Option<&Scope>) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>>` = `find_workspace_root` + `unwrap_or_else(default_scope)` + `scope_to_repos`.
- `for_each_repo(&[PathBuf], …)` — no comma-split, no `["."]`-default (gone).
- The four bodies + tests + `//!` updates + CLAUDE.md `chid -R .,.claude -L` → `-s code,bot -L`.
- Behavior: no-flag default = `default_scope()` → both repos in a dual workspace (you OK'd that).

> DEVELOPER

Doesn't have to be mutually exclusive, does it?

> AGENT

No, they compose naturally — and your earlier `-R ../path/dir -s bot` example is exactly that. **`-R` = workspace-root override** (replaces `find_workspace_root()`), **`-s` = sides selector** (replaces `default_scope(...)`):

- `-R <path>` alone → workspace=`<path>`, sides=`default_scope(<path>, cwd)`. For a dual `.vc-config.toml` at `<path>`: both sides (`[<path>, <path>/.claude>]`). For a non-workspace path: `default_scope` falls through to `Roles([Code])` → `[<path>]`.
- `-s <roles>` alone → workspace=`find_workspace_root()`, sides=`<roles>`.
- `-R + -s` → workspace=`<path>`, sides=`<roles>`. So `-R ../foo -s bot` → `[../foo/.claude]`. ✓
- Neither → today's no-flag default.

One behavior subtlety to flag: in *our* vc-x1 dual workspace, `vc-x1 chid -R .` would now query **both** `.` and `.claude` (where today's `-R .` queries only `.`). To get the today-behavior you'd say `-R . -s code`. The change tracks the "no-flag = both in dual" decision you OK'd earlier (since `-R .` is just "specify the workspace root explicitly, default sides").

Implementation delta vs my mutually-exclusive plan: drop `conflicts_with` from both fields in `common_args.rs`, and `resolve_repos` becomes:

```rust
let workspace_root = repo.map(Path::to_path_buf).or_else(find_workspace_root);
let scope = scope.cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| default_scope(workspace_root.as_deref(), &cwd));
scope_to_repos(&scope, workspace_root.as_deref())
```

The `parse_scope_roles` wrapper I just added is still right (`-s` keyword-only; `-R` covers paths). OK to continue?

> DEVELOPER

Hmm, if -s default to "empty" then no change from today?

> AGENT

Yes — that's the cleanest design and preserves today's behavior in every case people actually hit:

```rust
match (repo, scope) {
    (None, None)       => Ok(vec![PathBuf::from(".")]),              // today's default
    (Some(p), None)    => Ok(vec![p.to_path_buf()]),                 // today's `-R <path>`
    (Some(p), Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, Some(p)),                // workspace-root override + roles
    (None, Some(s))    => scope_to_repos(s, find_workspace_root().as_deref()),  // cwd-workspace + roles
}
```

So:
- `vc-x1 chid` → `["."]`. (Unchanged.)
- `vc-x1 chid -R foo` → `[foo]`. (Unchanged.)
- `vc-x1 chid -s code,bot` → both sides of cwd's workspace = `[., .claude]` (in vc-x1). (New, replaces `-R .,.claude`.)
- `vc-x1 chid -R ../foo -s bot` → `[../foo/.claude]`. (New, the composing case.)
- The dropped `-R .,.claude` / `-R . -R .claude` cases migrate to `-s code,bot`.

`default_scope` falls out of the `CommonArgs` path entirely (it stays in `common.rs` — the queued `vc-x1 push --scope` / `clone --scope` / `finalize --scope` rollouts use it where "both in dual" *is* the today-default).

Continuing the implementation with this resolution. The `parse_scope_roles` wrapper I added stays valid.

410	/// Expand comma-separated repo paths, default to `["."]`, and run a closure for each.
411	///
412	/// Header style controls output between repos.
413	/// Continues past errors, printing them to stderr, and returns an error if any failed.
414	pub fn for_each_repo<F>(
415	    raw_repos: &[PathBuf],
416	    header: &Header,
417	    mut body: F,

423	        vec![PathBuf::from(".")]

425	        raw_repos
426	            .iter()
427	            .flat_map(|p| {
428	                p.to_string_lossy()
429	                    .split(',')
430	                    .map(|s| PathBuf::from(s.trim()))
431	                    .collect::<Vec<_>>()
432	            })

441	            match header {

444	                        info!("");
445	                    }
446	                    info!(
447	                        "{}",
448	                        bold(&format!("{deco} {} {deco}", repo_path.display()))
449	                    );
450	                }
451	                Header::None => {}
452	            }
453	        }
454	        first = false;
455	
456	        match load_repo(repo_path) {
457	            Ok((workspace, repo)) => {

460	                    errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
461	                }
462	            }
463	            Err(e) => {
464	                error!("({}): {e}", repo_path.display());
465	                errors.push(format!("{}: {e}", repo_path.display()));
466	            }
467	        }
468	    }
469	
470	    if errors.is_empty() {
471	        Ok(())
472	    } else {
473	        Err(format!("{} repo(s) had errors", errors.len()).into())
474	    }
475	}

Behavior matches\n/// today's defaults plus a composing rule for the new `--scope` flag:\n///\n/// - neither flag → `[.]` (today's no-arg default).\n/// - `-R PATH` alone → `[PATH]` (today's `-R <path>` behavior;\n///   workspace context not consulted).\n/// - `-s ROLES` alone → resolves against `find_workspace_root()` —\n///   the surrounding workspace if there is one, else POR\n///   (`Side::Code` → `.`, `Side::Bot` → error).\n/// - `-R PATH -s ROLES` → resolves with `PATH` as the workspace root\n///   (overrides `find_workspace_root`). This is the composing case;\n///   e.g. `chid -R ../foo -s bot` queries `../foo/.claude`.\n///\n/// `--scope` is keyword-only today (the `parse_scope_roles` value\n/// parser rejects path forms); the planned `-s <path>` /\n/// `-s <path>,roles` workspace-root override is a future feature.\npub fn resolve_repos(\n    repo: Option<&Path>,\n    scope: Option<&Scope>,\n) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\n    match (repo, scope) {\n        (None, None) => Ok(vec![PathBuf::from(\".\")]),\n        (Some(p), None) => Ok(vec![p.to_path_buf()]),\n        (Some(p), Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, Some(p)),\n        (None, Some(s)) => scope_to_repos(s, find_workspace_root().as_deref()),\n    }\n}\n\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod tests;"
}

#[test]
fn scope_to_repos_single_returns_path() {
    let p = PathBuf::from("/explicit/single");
    assert_eq!(
        scope_to_repos(&Scope::Single(p.clone()), None).unwrap(),
        vec![p.clone()]
    );
    // workspace_root is ignored for Single — same result.
    assert_eq!(

        vec![p]
    );
}

//! Unit tests for the common module.

use super::*;

#[test]
fn find_non_tracking_remote_tracked() {
    let output = "\
main: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here
  @git: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here
  @origin: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here";
    assert_eq!(find_non_tracking_remote(output, "main"), None);
}

#[test]
fn find_non_tracking_remote_untracked() {
    let output = "\
main: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here
main@origin: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here";
    assert_eq!(
        find_non_tracking_remote(output, "main"),
        Some("origin".to_string())
    );
}

#[test]
fn find_non_tracking_remote_no_remote() {
    let output = "main: zzwozmkn 40a8309a title here";
    assert_eq!(find_non_tracking_remote(output, "main"), None);
}

resolve_repos_repo_plus_scope_uses_path_as_workspace_root() {\n    let base = ws_tempdir(\"resolve-compose\");\n    let root = base.join(\"ws\");\n    std::fs::create_dir_all(&root).unwrap();\n    std::fs::write(\n        root.join(VC_CONFIG_FILE),\n        \"[workspace]\\npath = \\\"/\\\"\\nother-repo = \\\".claude\\\"\\n\",\n    )\n    .unwrap();\n    let scope = Scope::Roles(vec![Side::Code, Side::Bot]);\n    let repos = resolve_repos(Some(&root), Some(&scope)).unwrap();\n    assert_eq!(repos, vec![root.clone(), root.join(\".claude\")]);\n    std::fs::remove_dir_all(&base).ok();\n}\n\n/// > AGENT

`0.49.0-2.2` is in `@` for your Zed review (`jj diff -R .`). Cargo cycle clean: fmt ✓, clippy `-D warnings` ✓, test 369+5+4+5 (was 360 lib; +9: 3 for `parse_scope_roles`, 4 for `resolve_repos`, +new per-subcommand `-s` tests, −the `multi_repo`/`comma_repo` tests), `install --locked` ✓, `vc-x1 -V` → `0.49.0-2.2`. Smoke:
- `vc-x1 chid -L @ 1` → one line (app `@`). ✓ today's no-arg default preserved.
- `vc-x1 chid -L -s code,bot @ 1` → two lines (app, then `.claude`). ✓ new compose.

Summary of what changed:

**`src/scope.rs`** — un-`#[allow(dead_code)]`'d `parse_scope` + `Scope::Single`; new `parse_scope_roles` wraps `parse_scope` and rejects path forms with a hint pointing at `-R`/`--repo` (path-via-`-s` is the future Todo). +3 tests.

**`src/options_flags/common_args.rs`** — replaced `repos: Vec<PathBuf>` with two fields: `repo: Option<PathBuf>` (`-R`/`--repo`, single path) and `scope: Option<Scope>` (`-s`/`--scope`, `value_parser = parse_scope_roles`, keyword-only). No `conflicts_with` — they compose. Module-doc + field-docs updated.

**`src/common.rs`** — `for_each_repo` drops its comma-split + `["."]`-default block (param renamed `raw_repos` → `repos`, doc updated). New `pub fn resolve_repos(repo, scope)` with the match-on-pair logic we agreed: `(None, None)` → `[.]`, `(Some(p), None)` → `[p]`, `(Some(p), Some(s))` → `scope_to_repos(s, Some(p))`, `(None, Some(s))` → `scope_to_repos(s, find_workspace_root())`.

**`src/common/tests.rs`** — +4 `resolve_repos` tests (no-flags, repo-only, compose code+bot, compose bot-only).

**`src/{chid,desc,list,show}.rs`** — body adds `let repos = common::resolve_repos(c.repo.as_deref(), c.scope.as_ref())?;` and passes `&repos` to `for_each_repo`. Tests: dropped the now-invalid `multi_repo` / `comma_repo` ones; updated `defaults`/`with_repo`/`all_opts` to the `Option`-shaped fields; added `with_scope_*` per file (chid also gets a compose test and a "path-via-`-s`-rejected" test).

**`CLAUDE.md`** — both `vc-x1 chid -R .,.claude -L` instructions → `vc-x1 chid -s code,bot -L`.

**`notes/todo.md`** — `0.49.0-2.2` ladder line rewritten to reflect the "keep `-R`, add `-s`, compose" reality; +2 new `## Todo` items: drop `-R` once `-s` is established, and the `-s <path>`/`-s <path>,roles` workspace-root-override feature.

**`Cargo.toml` + `Cargo.lock`** — `0.49.0-2.1` → `0.49.0-2.2`.

Review when you're ready; I'll propose the commit title + body (both repos) for your OK before pushing.

> DEVELOPER

Why use c.repo.as_deref() and c.scop.as_ref() is that a clippy suggestion?

> AGENT

Driven by the function signature, not directly a clippy lint (though clippy would steer you there if you wrote it the verbose way).

`resolve_repos` takes `Option<&Path>` (not `Option<&PathBuf>`) and `Option<&Scope>` — the canonical Rust convention is that APIs accept the unsized-borrowed form (`&Path`, `&str`, `&[T]`) rather than the owned-borrowed form (`&PathBuf`, `&String`, `&Vec<T>`) so they're maximally general. To turn each field into what the signature wants:

- `c.repo: Option<PathBuf>` → `Option<&Path>`: needs `.as_deref()`. `PathBuf : Deref<Target = Path>`, so `Option::as_deref` exists for `Option<PathBuf>` and gives `Option<&Path>` in one call. Same idiom as `Option<String> → Option<&str>` via `.as_deref()`.
- `c.scope: Option<Scope>` → `Option<&Scope>`: just `.as_ref()`. `Scope` is a plain enum, no `Deref` impl — there's nothing to deref through, so `as_deref()` wouldn't even compile.

So the asymmetry isn't arbitrary — it tracks "does this type have a natural `Deref` target?": `PathBuf` does (`Path`), `Scope` doesn't. The clippy lint `option_as_ref_deref` would flag `c.repo.as_ref().map(|p| p.as_path())` and suggest `c.repo.as_deref()`, but writing it directly skips that step.

Alternative I considered and rejected: signature as `repo: Option<&PathBuf>` so both call sites use `.as_ref()`. Symmetric but worse — `&PathBuf` is the less-idiomatic borrowed form (parallel to taking `&Vec<T>` instead of `&[T]`).

> DEVELOPER

That seems so verbose, it's like Rust is saying you can do this, but you need to be verbose so you might find a better way?

> AGENT

Often a real signal, yes — and here specifically. The cleaner shape is a method on `CommonArgs` that bundles the conversion:

```rust
// in src/options_flags/common_args.rs
impl CommonArgs {
    /// Resolve `-R` + `-s` into the concrete repo paths to iterate.
    pub fn resolve_repos(&self) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
        crate::common::resolve_repos(self.repo.as_deref(), self.scope.as_ref())
    }
}
```

Then each subcommand body becomes:

```rust
let repos = c.resolve_repos()?;
```

The four bodies lose a line each and read more directly. `common::resolve_repos(repo, scope)` stays as the free-function primitive (so a future `finalize --scope` or `push --scope` can call it without going through `CommonArgs`), and the `as_deref()`/`as_ref()` ceremony lives in exactly one place — the method that knows it's bridging the clap-shaped fields to the borrowed-shape API.

When `0.49.0-3..-6` does the Context+Params port the same `c.resolve_repos()` call moves into each `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>` — equally clean there.

Always\n  available; hands back a reference to whatever's in the `Some`.\n- `Option::as_deref()` — `Option<T>` → `Option<&<T as\n  Deref>::Target>`. Available only when `T: Deref`. So\n  `Option<PathBuf>::as_deref() → Option<&Path>`,\n  `Option<String>::as_deref() → Option<&str>`,\n  `Option<Vec<U>>::as_deref() → Option<&[U]>`.\n\n**Why the asymmetry.** Rust APIs take the *unsized* borrowed\nform (`&Path`, `&str`, `&[T]`) rather than the owned-borrowed\nform (`&PathBuf`, `&String`, `&Vec<T>`) — the former is strictly\nmore general. A caller with a `PathBuf` can pass `&pb`; a caller\nwith a `&Path` can pass it directly; the `&PathBuf` form\nwouldn't accept the latter. So functions tend to want `&Path`,\nwhich puts the burden on the caller to deref through\n`PathBuf`'s `Deref<Target = Path>` impl. Types without a useful\n`Deref` (plain enums like `Scope`) skip that step — `as_ref()`\nsuffices.\n\n**The fix when verbosity bites.** When `.as_deref()` /\n`.as_ref()` show up at a call site, consider wrapping the\nceremony in a domain method on the owner type:\n\n```rust\nimpl CommonArgs {\n    pub fn resolve_repos(&self) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, …> {\n        common::resolve_repos(self.repo.as_deref(),\n                              self.scope.as_ref())\n    }\n}\n```\n\n…so callers read `c.resolve_repos()` and the ceremony lives in\none well-named place. > DEVELOPER

This will make dropping -R and expanding -s simpler, true?

> AGENT

Yes — that's exactly the leverage. The helper localizes the resolution ceremony to one place, so the four subcommand bodies (and, in `0.49.0-3..-6`, the four `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>` impls) don't move when the resolution API changes underneath:

**Dropping `-R`** — the work becomes:
- `common_args.rs` — delete the `repo` field.
- `common::resolve_repos` — drop the `repo` parameter (or pass `None` from the method).
- `CommonArgs::resolve_repos` — drop the `self.repo.as_deref()` half.

…three files instead of seven. The four subcommand bodies stay `c.resolve_repos()?`.

**Expanding `-s` (paths + `<path>,roles` workspace-root override)** — confined to:
- `scope.rs` — extend `parse_scope_roles` (or fold into `parse_scope`); possibly add a `Scope::RolesAt { root, sides }` variant.
- `common.rs` — `scope_to_repos` gets a new arm.

…and `CommonArgs.scope: Option<Scope>` stays the same shape; `CommonArgs::resolve_repos` stays the same one-liner; the four bodies stay the same. (The one design wrinkle for that cycle: with `-R` still around, what happens if both `-R ../foo` and `-s ../bar,roles` are set? Probably an error — but that's a decision for then, not now.)

The helper's the "single change-locus" handle for both of those future cycles, plus the four `TryFrom`s in `0.49.0-3..-6`. Good payoff for a 5-line method.

  "new_string": "work is a process bug; the pre-commit checklist gets a\ncatch-line for it.\n\n## feat: chid+co -s/--scope flag (0.49.0-2.2)\n\nThe code half of the `0.49.0-2` rollout (`0.49.0-2.3` will sweep\nthe docs). Replaces today's `-R .,.claude` / `-R . -R .claude`\nmulti-repo forms with a roles flag (`-s code | bot | code,bot`),\nkeeps `-R` for single-path operation, and lets the two compose\nas a workspace-root override. See `### Cycle re-scope`'s\n`--scope` bullet for the wider plan; the two `###` subsections\nbelow capture the design pivots that landed in this commit.\n\n### Design: `-R` and `-s` compose rather than conflict\n\nThe chores plan had `-R` dropped, with `--scope=<path>` covering\nsingle-repo via `Scope::Single`. On review the design walked\nthrough three iterations:\n\n- **Drop `-R`.** `--scope=./foo` covers single-path via\n  `Scope::Single`; one flag, the `./` prefix disambiguates from\n  the role keywords.\n- **Mutually-exclusive `-R` + `-s`.** Keep `-R` for paths, add\n  `-s` for roles, `conflicts_with` between them. Familiar `-R`\n  preserved; redundant on the path side.\n- **Composing `-R` + `-s`** (chosen). `-R` overrides the\n  workspace root (replaces `find_workspace_root()`), `-s`\n  selects sides (replaces `default_scope(...)`). Together:\n  `-R <ws> -s <roles>` resolves the roles within `<ws>`. Each\n  flag alone reads as today's behavior: `-R foo` → `[foo]`, no\n  flag → `[.]`. The net-new expressivity is the combined form\n  (e.g. `vc-x1 chid -R ../foo -s bot` → `[../foo/.claude]`).\n  `-s` is keyword-only today (`parse_scope_roles` rejects paths\n  with a hint at `-R`); `-s <path>` and the `-s <path>,roles`\n  workspace-root override are queued as `## Todo` (a future\n  `Scope::RolesAt { root, sides }` variant, probably). \"Drop\n  `-R` once `-s` is established\" is a separate `## Todo` for\n  after the migration period — kept for backwards-compat now.\n\n### Design: `CommonArgs::resolve_repos(&self)` helper\n\n`common::resolve_repos(repo, scope)` takes `Option<&Path>` +\n`Option<&Scope>` — the standard \"borrowed unsized\" convention\n(`&Path`, not `&PathBuf`). At each call site that produces an\nasymmetric `c.repo.as_deref()` / `c.scope.as_ref()` pair — four\ntimes across the subcommand bodies, with another four to come in\n`0.49.0-3..-6`'s `TryFrom<&XxxArgs>` impls. A method on\n`CommonArgs` localizes the conversion ceremony to one place so\ncallers read `c.resolve_repos()?`, and a new\n`notes/rust-idioms.md` carries the `as_deref` vs `as_ref`\nexplainer the doc-comment links to. The free function stays as\nthe reusable primitive (a future `finalize --scope` /\n`push --scope` calls it directly, not through `CommonArgs`).\n\n# References\n\n[1]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/10788bd158c4 \"10788bd158c4574fe5a10fab41ea32e4becc86d3\"\n[2]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/cc19273e2ca3 \"cc19273e2ca30f1beedd55198a11bdf045b281ee\"\n[3]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/f6438bc7394e \"f6438bc7394e76a3d83de08467c6fafec7a819b7\"\n[4]: https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1/commit/7e1ea28cc7f6 \"7e1ea28cc7f62c2f0920d25ae7c21dba69629e02\""
}
